The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

For a smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, let
$$C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)=\mathbb R^{(S_k^\infty(M))}\quad(k\ge0),\qquad C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)=0\quad(k<0),$$
using [[def-smooth-singular-simplex]]. It is the subspace of [[def-real-singular-chain-complex]] spanned by the smooth simplices, with the same signed face differential.

This is a subcomplex: an affine face map $\delta_i:A^{k-1}\to A^k$ has the open inverse image $\delta_i^{-1}(O)$ containing $\Delta^{k-1}$. Composing $\bar\sigma$ with this affine map on that inverse image extends $\sigma\delta_i$ smoothly into $M$. Thus every face is smooth, and the already proved signed cancellation gives $\partial^2=0$ on this subspace.

Define the **smooth singular cochain complex** by
$$C_\infty^k(M;\mathbb R)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R),\mathbb R),\qquad \delta\varphi=\varphi\partial.$$
As for [[def-real-singular-cochain-complex]], these are arbitrary real functions on the supplied smooth-simplex basis, evaluated by finite sums. Precomposition gives $\delta^2\varphi=\varphi\partial^2=0$. Define $H_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)=\ker\partial_k/\operatorname{im}\partial_{k+1}$ and $H_\infty^k(M;\mathbb R)=\ker\delta^k/\operatorname{im}\delta^{k-1}$; both quotients are licensed by square-zero.

Negative groups vanish and the degree-zero boundary is zero. On a point all simplices are smooth, so the complexes are the ordinary unnormalized point complexes; no constant simplices are discarded. For the empty manifold all groups are zero. The specified subspaces and duals require no choice of extensions or bases.

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\sin x:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!},\qquad\cos x:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n}}{(2n)!}.$$

These are real power series in the sense of [[def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence]]. Their convergence for every real argument is discharged by [[lem-sine-and-cosine-series-converge-everywhere]].

For every real $x$, both series
$$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!}$$
converge absolutely. Equivalently, both power series have infinite radius of convergence.

Let

$$f(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n(x-c)^n$$

have radius $R$. For every $x$ with $|x-c|<R$, the function $f$ is differentiable at $x$ ([[def-derivative]]) and

$$f'(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\iota(n+1)a_{n+1}(x-c)^n.$$

The differentiated series has the same radius $R$.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

For every real $x$,
$$\sin x=0\Longleftrightarrow x=m\pi\text{ for some }m\in\mathbb Z,\qquad \cos x=0\Longleftrightarrow x=(m+1/2)\pi\text{ for some }m\in\mathbb Z.$$
Both sine and cosine have period $2\pi$, and no smaller positive number is a common period.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $a < b$ be reals and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $f$ is bounded ([[def-bounded-set]]) and Riemann
integrable on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]).

**The proof gives more than integrability: it gives a partition that works.** For
every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the uniform partition into $N$ parts already
satisfies $U(f,P) - L(f,P) < \varepsilon$, as soon as $N$ is large enough that
$(b-a)/\iota(N)$ is below the $\delta$ that uniform continuity supplies for
$\varepsilon/\bigl(2(b-a)\bigr)$. Uniform continuity is exactly what makes one
$\delta$ serve all $N$ subintervals at once, and it is the only place where the
compactness of $[a,b]$ is used.

Let $a < b$ be reals and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be bounded
([[def-bounded-set]]). Write $\mathcal{P}$ for the set of all partitions of
$[a,b]$ ([[def-partition-and-refinement]]) and put

$$\mathcal{L} \;:=\; \{\, L(f,P) \ : \ P \in \mathcal{P} \,\}, \qquad \mathcal{U} \;:=\; \{\, U(f,P) \ : \ P \in \mathcal{P} \,\}$$

for the sets of lower and of upper Darboux sums ([[def-darboux-sums]]).

### Both extrema exist

**$\mathcal{P}$ is nonempty**: the pair $(1, t)$ with $t_0 := a$ and $t_k := b$
for $k \ge 1$ is a partition of $[a,b]$, since $a < b$. So $\mathcal{L}$ and
$\mathcal{U}$ are nonempty.

**$\mathcal{L}$ is bounded above and $\mathcal{U}$ is bounded below.** Fix any
$Q \in \mathcal{P}$. By claim 2 of [[lem-refinement-inequalities]],
$L(f,P) \le U(f,Q)$ for every $P \in \mathcal{P}$, so $U(f,Q)$ is an upper bound
of $\mathcal{L}$; and $L(f,Q) \le U(f,P)$ for every $P$, so $L(f,Q)$ is a lower
bound of $\mathcal{U}$.

Hence a nonempty set bounded above has a supremum
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]) and a nonempty set bounded below has an infimum
([[thm-infimum-property]], [[def-infimum]]), each unique ([[lem-sup-unique]]).
The **lower** and **upper Darboux integrals** of $f$ over $[a,b]$ are the real
numbers

$$\underline{\int_a^b} f \;:=\; \sup \mathcal{L} \;=\; \sup_{P} L(f,P), \qquad \overline{\int_a^b} f \;:=\; \inf \mathcal{U} \;=\; \inf_{P} U(f,P) .$$

### The lower integral never exceeds the upper one

$$\underline{\int_a^b} f \;\le\; \overline{\int_a^b} f .$$

Indeed, for each fixed $Q \in \mathcal{P}$ the number $U(f,Q)$ is an upper bound
of $\mathcal{L}$, so the least upper bound satisfies
$\underline{\int_a^b} f \le U(f,Q)$. As $Q$ was arbitrary, $\underline{\int_a^b}f$
is a lower bound of $\mathcal{U}$, and the greatest lower bound satisfies
$\underline{\int_a^b} f \le \overline{\int_a^b} f$ ([[def-infimum]]).

Moreover, for **every** partition $P$,

$$L(f,P) \;\le\; \underline{\int_a^b} f \;\le\; \overline{\int_a^b} f \;\le\; U(f,P) ,$$

the outer inequalities because a member of a set is at most its supremum and at
least its infimum.

### Integrability

$f$ is **Darboux integrable on $[a,b]$**, and on this page simply
**integrable**, when

$$\underline{\int_a^b} f \;=\; \overline{\int_a^b} f ,$$

and then the common value is written

$$\int_a^b f \qquad \text{or} \qquad \int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x ,$$

the **integral of $f$ over $[a,b]$**. It is a single well-determined real
number, being the common value of two numbers each of which is unique
([[lem-sup-unique]]). Without the displayed equality the symbol $\int_a^b f$ is
not defined and is never written.

**The inequality above is the whole difficulty.** By the previous paragraph
integrability is *never* a question of one integral exceeding the other, only of
the gap $\overline{\int_a^b} f - \underline{\int_a^b} f \ge 0$ being $0$; and by
[[thm-riemann-criterion]] that gap is $0$ exactly when a single partition can be
found making $U(f,P) - L(f,P)$ small. Whether that is possible is settled
completely, in terms of the discontinuities of $f$, by
[[thm-lebesgue-criterion]].

**"Riemann integrable" means the same thing here.** The definition above is
Darboux's. Riemann's own definition, in terms of tagged partitions of small
mesh, is [[def-tagged-partition-and-riemann-sum]], and the two define the same
class of functions with the same integral by [[thm-darboux-equals-riemann]].
Until that theorem is proved the two phrases are kept apart; after it they are
used interchangeably, as they are throughout the literature.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

Let $\sigma:\Delta^k\to M$ be a smooth singular simplex and let $\omega$ be a smooth $k$-form on an open neighbourhood of its image in $M$. For $k\ge1$ put
$$T_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^k:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j\le1\},\qquad a(x)=v_0+\sum_{j=1}^kx_j(v_j-v_0).$$
Take a smooth extension $\bar\sigma$ near $\Delta^k$, restrict its domain so that $\omega$ is defined on its image, and write $a^*\bar\sigma^*\omega=f(x)\,dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_k$. Define
$$\int_\sigma\omega:=\int_{T_k}f(x)\,dx.$$
The right side is the Jordan-set Riemann integral. In degree zero define $\int_\sigma\omega=\omega(\sigma(v_0))$. This fixes the positive point convention. Reversing the domain orientation negates the integral. Independence of other positive affine coordinates is the forward justification [[lem-simplex-integrals-are-independent-of-affine-coordinate-identification]].

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $g:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be injective and $C^1$, and suppose $Dg(x)$ is invertible for every $x\in U$. Let $K\subseteq U$ be compact and Jordan measurable. For a bounded function $f:g(K)\to\mathbb R$, the following are equivalent:

1. $f$ is Riemann integrable on $g(K)$;
2. $x\mapsto f(g(x))|\det Dg(x)|$ is Riemann integrable on $K$.

When either condition holds,
$$\int_{g(K)}f(y)\,dy=\int_K f(g(x))|\det Dg(x)|\,dx.$$

A metric-bounded set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is Jordan measurable if and only
if its boundary $\partial E$ is null, equivalently has content zero.
Let $m\ge1$, let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be a closed nondegenerate rectangle, and let $f:Q\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Its graph has content zero in $\mathbb R^{m+1}$.
Every continuous real function on a compact Jordan measurable set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is Riemann integrable over $E$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its metrics only there; the last remark below records what
happens at $n = 0$.

Fix $m\ge1$. A **closed cube** is a rectangle $\prod_{j<m}[a_j,a_j+\ell]$ with $\ell\ge0$; its volume is $\ell^m$. A set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is **null** when, for every $\varepsilon>0$, it is covered by a sequence of closed cubes whose nonnegative volume series converges with sum at most $\varepsilon$. It has **content zero** when such a cover can be finite.

The series and finite sums are [[def-series]] and [[def-finite-sum]], and their nonnegative bounds use [[thm-nonnegative-series-bounded-partial-sums]] and [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]. Both properties pass to subsets. Padding a finite cover with degenerate zero-volume cubes proves that content zero implies null. This terminology defines only cover-nullity; it does not define a measure on arbitrary sets.

Let $m\ge1$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be bounded and Jordan measurable, let $N\ge1$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_N\subseteq A$ be bounded Jordan measurable sets such that $A_i\cap A_j$ has content zero whenever $i\ne j$ and such that $A\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^NA_i$ has content zero. Let $f:A\to\mathbb R$ be bounded, Riemann integrable over $A$ and Riemann integrable over each $A_i$. Then

$$\int_Af=\sum_{i=1}^N\int_{A_i}f.$$
Every continuous real function on a closed nondegenerate rectangle $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge1$, is Riemann integrable.

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ and $B\subseteq\mathbb R^q$ be nondegenerate closed rectangles, and let $f:A\times B\to\mathbb R$ be Riemann integrable. Then the four lower and upper section-integral functions of [[def-sections-and-iterated-riemann-integrals]] are Riemann integrable and
$$\int_A\ell_B=\int_Au_B=\int_{A\times B}f=\int_B\ell_A=\int_Bu_A.$$

If the $B$-sections are integrable outside a content-zero set $N\subseteq A$, every bounded exceptionally completed function $h$ with $h(x)=\int_Bf_x$ for $x\notin N$ is integrable and
$$\int_{A\times B}f=\int_Ah.$$
The same assertion holds with the coordinate blocks exchanged. In particular, when every section in an order is integrable, the ordinary iterated integral in that order exists and equals the multiple integral. The theorem does not assert that every section of an integrable function is integrable.

For a bounded function $f:Q\to\mathbb R$ on a nondegenerate rectangle
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, define
$$\underline{\int_Q}f:=\sup_P L(f,P),\qquad \overline{\int_Q}f:=\inf_P U(f,P),$$
over all grid partitions $P$ of $Q$. The grid family is nonempty, since the endpoints in each coordinate give a one-cell grid. Every lower sum is at most every upper sum by a common refinement and [[lem-multidimensional-refinement-inequalities]], so the two sets of sums are nonempty and bounded and the extrema exist ([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[thm-infimum-property]], [[def-infimum]], [[lem-sup-unique]]).

The function is **Riemann integrable over $Q$** when the two values agree.
Their unique common real is $\int_Q f$. No integral is defined here for a
degenerate rectangle, because the grid definition requires every coordinate
interval to have distinct endpoints. This is the multidimensional Darboux
definition; its agreement with the published one-dimensional definition is
proved separately.

Fix a natural number $m\ge1$. For $a,b\in\mathbb R^m$ with $a_j\le b_j$ for $j<m$, define
$$[a,b]:=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:a_j\le x_j\le b_j\ (j<m)\},\qquad \operatorname{vol}[a,b]:=\prod_{j<m}(b_j-a_j).$$
The product is the recursively defined finite product of [[def-finite-sum]]. The rectangle is **nondegenerate** when every $a_j<b_j$, and it is a **cube** when all side lengths are equal.

Every factor is nonnegative, so volume is nonnegative. For a coordinate index $r<m$, cutting at $c\in[a_r,b_r]$ gives two rectangles whose volumes add to the original, by distributivity in that factor and [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]. Under the standard identification $\mathbb R^1\cong\mathbb R$ ([[lem-metrics-on-rn]], [[def-p-norms-on-rn]]), this is the interval $[a_0,b_0]$ and its length.

derivations.claim:
For a fixed permutation $\sigma$, the barycentric coordinates of a point
in the ordered region
$0\le u_{\sigma(3)}\le u_{\sigma(2)}\le u_{\sigma(1)}\le1$ relative to its
four listed vertices are $1-u_{\sigma(1)}$,
$u_{\sigma(1)}-u_{\sigma(2)}$, $u_{\sigma(2)}-u_{\sigma(3)}$, and
$u_{\sigma(3)}$; these are nonnegative, sum to one, and reconstruct the
point. Thus the six tetrahedra cover the cube with disjoint interiors. Each
affine map is smooth on a neighbourhood of its standard simplex, and its
composition with the smooth quotient map [F1] is a smooth singular simplex.
The ordered edge determinant is
$L_1L_2L_3\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$, so the weight
$\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$ orients each tetrahedron by
$dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

The function $h$ is periodic and smooth, with $h'=f$ by [F6]–[F7], so
$F$ and $j$ are smooth global fields on the product. Since
$dF=-\mu_0h'(x^1)dx^1\wedge dx^0\wedge dx^1=0$, the homogeneous equation
holds. Raising indices gives $F^{01}=\mu_0h$ and $F^{10}=-\mu_0h$. Thus
$\nabla_aF^{a0}=\partial_1F^{10}=-\mu_0f=-\mu_0j^0$,
$\nabla_aF^{a1}=\partial_0F^{01}=0=-\mu_0j^1$, and the $b=2,3$ equations
have both sides zero. Thus both field equations are verified everywhere.

An internal facet arises by setting one adjacent-coordinate inequality
to equality. The two permutations differ by swapping those adjacent entries;
their omitted vertices occupy the same position in the ordered vertex lists,
and the remaining three vertices have the same order. Thus the face maps in
[F5] are identical, while the permutation signs are opposite. Their two
coefficients in the signed face boundary therefore sum to zero. This covers
both internal facet types (equal first and second coordinates, or equal
second and third coordinates).

Fix a coordinate $i$ and order the other two indices as $(a,b)$. The
triangle on $x^i=L_i$ comes from permutation $(i,a,b)$ by omitting vertex
$0$; its ordered vertices are $L_ie_i$, $L_ie_i+L_ae_a$, and
$L_ie_i+L_ae_a+L_be_b$. The triangle on $x^i=0$ comes from $(a,b,i)$ by
omitting the final vertex; its ordered vertices are $0$, $L_ae_a$, and
$L_ae_a+L_be_b$. Translation by $L_ie_i$ makes these vertex lists identical,
so their quotient face maps are equal. Moving $i$ from first to last is two
transpositions, so the permutation coefficients agree; the omitted-vertex
boundary signs are $+1$ and $-1$. By [F5] the corresponding face terms
cancel. This pairs every outer triangle, for all three coordinates and both
orders $(a,b)$.

Let $C=[0,L_1]\times[0,L_2]\times[0,L_3]$ and let $T_\sigma\subset C$
be the affine tetrahedron with the ordered vertices specified in the Example;
each $T_\sigma$ is closed and bounded, hence compact by [F9], so the
continuous function $f$ is bounded there. The standard $T_3$ is compact
Jordan by [F8].
Write $\phi_\sigma:T_3\to T_\sigma$ for its affine parametrization and
$\psi_\sigma=q\circ\phi_\sigma$ for the corresponding simplex in $M$.
Since $j=f(x^1)\partial_0$ and $\mathrm{vol}_g=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ by [F1], the interior-product definition in [F2] gives
$\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g=f(x^1)dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. The pullback of
$\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
$\psi_\sigma$ has coefficient
$f(\phi_\sigma^1(s))\det D\phi_\sigma$ in the standard positive affine
coordinates, because the descended coordinate forms pull back under $q$ to
the Euclidean coordinate forms [F1]. By [F8] this is the coefficient whose
integral defines $\int_{\psi_\sigma}\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$. This coefficient
is continuous on compact Jordan $T_3$, hence integrable by [F9]. The determinant
of the three edge vectors is
$\det D\phi_\sigma=L_1L_2L_3\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$, so the chain
coefficient gives
$$\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\int_{\psi_\sigma}\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g =\int_{T_3} f(\phi_\sigma^1(s))|\det D\phi_\sigma|\,ds =\int_{T_\sigma}f(x^1)\,dx^1dx^2dx^3.$$
The last equality is [F8]'s change-of-variables formula: $T_3$ is compact
Jordan, $\phi_\sigma$ extends to an injective affine $C^1$ map on
$\mathbb R^3$ with nonsingular constant derivative, and $f$ is bounded and
continuous on $T_\sigma$.
The cube $C$ and each $T_\sigma$ are closed and bounded, hence compact by
Heine--Borel, and they are bounded Jordan sets. Indeed their
boundaries are finite unions of bounded pieces of affine planes; each such
piece is contained in the graph of an affine function over a containing
closed nondegenerate rectangle after solving the plane equation for a
coordinate with nonzero normal component. These graphs have content zero by
[F9], so the boundary criterion in [F9] applies. By step 1.1 the six
$T_\sigma$ cover $C$ and have disjoint interiors. Thus each pairwise
intersection is contained in the union of their boundaries and has content
zero by finite-union and subset closure in [F9], while the remainder
$C\setminus\bigcup_{\sigma\in S_3}T_\sigma$ is
empty. The coefficient $f$ is continuous and bounded on the compact Jordan
sets $C,T_\sigma$, so all integrals in the finite additivity hypotheses are
defined by [F9]. Applying the finite Jordan-set additivity result in [F9]
and using the chain definition in [F2] gives
$$Q(\Sigma)=\frac1c\sum_{\sigma\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) \int_{\psi_\sigma}\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g =\frac1c\int_C f(x^1)\,dx^1dx^2dx^3.$$

The finite chain boundary is the alternating face sum in [F5]. Steps 2.1
and 2.2 cancel every internal and external face term, respectively. Hence
$\partial\Sigma=0$, as required in [F3]. The explicit finite triangulation
adds no choice, as [F4] records.

Since $\partial\Sigma=0$ by step 3.1, the finite-chain neutrality
result [F3] applies and gives $Q(\Sigma)=0$.

Write $A=[0,L_1]$ and $B=[0,L_2]\times[0,L_3]$, so $C=A\times B$.
The coefficient $f(x^1)$ is continuous on $C$ and hence integrable there by
[F10]. Rectangular Fubini [F10] applies, and its sections over $B$ are the
constant function $f(x^1)$. The multidimensional Darboux sums and volume
formula in [F10] therefore give
$$\int_Cf(x^1)\,dx^1dx^2dx^3 =L_2L_3\int_0^{L_1}f(x^1)\,dx^1.$$
By [F7], $h'=f$ and the one-dimensional FTC gives
$\int_0^{L_1}f(x^1)\,dx^1=h(L_1)-h(0)=0$, since the sine values at $0$ and
$2\pi$ agree. Hence the direct integral computation also yields
$Q(\Sigma)=0$, in agreement with step 4.1.

citations.quote: Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ by $z=x+iy$ and set $U(1)=S^1:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$. Its topology is the subspace topology. Specify its smooth structure by the four charts

$$V_{x,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon x>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto y,\quad y\mapsto(\epsilon\sqrt{1-y^2},y),$$

and

$$V_{y,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon y>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto x,\quad x\mapsto(x,\epsilon\sqrt{1-x^2}),$$

for $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, with each coordinate range $(-1,1)$. They cover $S^1$; their transition maps are restrictions of the positive square-root branch and coordinate projections, hence are smooth by [[lem-emg-positive-square-root-smoothness]] and [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]. In these coordinates multiplication is the restriction of $(x,y)(u,v)=(xu-yv,xv+yu)$ and inversion is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$, so both are smooth; they are also continuous for the stated topology. Thus this is a smooth Lie group and, in particular, a topological group as required by [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].

Let $E:\mathbb R\to U(1)$ be $E(t)=e^{it}=(\cos t,\sin t)$; the Cartesian formula is [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The trigonometric derivative identities of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], iterated, show that $E$ is smooth in the $C^\infty$ sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: every derivative of either coordinate is $\pm\sin$ or $\pm\cos$, and these functions are continuous by [[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]. Surjectivity is [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]]. If $E(t)\in V_{x,\epsilon}$, the chart coordinate $\sin t$ has derivative $\cos t=x\ne0$; if $E(t)\in V_{y,\epsilon}$, the coordinate $\cos t$ has derivative $-\sin t=-y\ne0$. The smooth inverse-function theorem [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] therefore makes $E$ a diffeomorphism from some open interval about $t$ onto an open circle arc. Every smooth map from an open subset of $M$ to $U(1)$ consequently has, near each point, a smooth real phase lift obtained by composing with such a local inverse.

A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, take any smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. If $f$ and $\widetilde f$ are two lifts on a connected neighborhood, [[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]] gives $f-\widetilde f\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ pointwise; continuity makes this difference constant, so $df=d\widetilde f$. Thus the compatibility condition is independent of the chosen lift. The globally defined form $\lambda(g):=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ is real, and [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] together with [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] gives $\lambda(g)=df$ on every phase-lift neighborhood. Hence the equivalent lift-free condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The right principal $U(1)$-bundle convention is as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]: it has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts, with free and transitive action on each fibre. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

Let $M$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable oriented four-manifold, and let $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ be a normalized circle-connection datum as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Use the set-sized-object and quotient convention of [[def-emg-set-size-and-class-schema]]. Then the chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal $U(1)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a global smooth real connection one-form $\omega$ on $P$. Its curvature is basic: there is a smooth closed two-form $f\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $d\omega=\pi^*f$ and $f|_{U_i}=da_i$. The local potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ satisfy $dA_i=F$, where $F=\kappa_0 f$ is global. For two connections on the same fixed bundle with the same transition functions, their local-form differences are restrictions of one global base one-form; adding a global one-form to all local representatives stays in that bundle sector.

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, so that $TM$ carries its canonical smooth
structure. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. A **smooth vector field** on $M$ is a
smooth section

A **local flow** of $X$ consists of an open set $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R\times M$
containing $\{0\}\times M$ and a smooth map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ such that:

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

If $X$ has local flow $\Phi_t$ and $T$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(r,s)$, its Lie derivative is $$\mathcal L_XT=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*T,$$ on every local flow domain where this derivative is defined. Here the pullback by the local diffeomorphism $\Phi_t$ acts by $d\Phi_{-t}$ on each contravariant slot and by $d\Phi_t$ on each covariant slot.

For a covariant $k$-tensor $T=T_{i_1\cdots i_k}dx^{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes dx^{i_k}$, $$ (\mathcal L_XT)_{i_1\cdots i_k}=X^j\partial_jT_{i_1\cdots i_k}+\sum_a(\partial_{i_a}X^j)T_{i_1\cdots j\cdots i_k}. $$

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, let $K\subseteq U$ be compact, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval with $0\in I$, and let $s\mapsto g(s)$, $s\in I$, be a family of
smooth Lorentzian metrics of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ such that

- $g(0)=g$ and $g(s)=g$ on $M\setminus K$ for every $s\in I$; and
- the components $g(s)_{ab}$ in the chart are smooth functions of $(s,x)$ on
  $I\times x(U)$ ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

Write $h_{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)_{ab}|_{s=0}$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field with support in $K$, and
$q^{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)^{ab}|_{s=0}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$). In particular any prescribed smooth compactly
supported inverse-metric direction $q$ is realized by $g+s h$ on a
sufficiently small interval, with $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$.

**(b) Variation of the Christoffel symbols.** The field
$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_s\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}|_{s=0}$ is a smooth
tensor field on $U$ and

$$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}\bigl(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(c) Variation of the Ricci tensor (Palatini identity).**
$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\partial_s\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd}|_{s=0}$
satisfies

$$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\nabla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-\nabla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}.$$

**(d) Variation of the curvature density.** With
$V^{a}:=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$ and
$w(s):=\sqrt{|\det(g(s)_{ab})|}$ the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],

$$\partial_s\bigl(w(s)S(s)\bigr)\big|_{s=0}=w\,G_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a\bigl(wV^{a}\bigr).$$

**(e) Variation of the chart action integral.** For every constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, the function
$F(s):=\int_U\bigl[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)\bigr]\,d^4x$ is the compactly supported chart action difference, differentiable at $0$, and

$$F'(0)=\int_U\bigl(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}\bigr)q^{ab}\,w\,d^4x,$$

where the integrand is compactly supported in $K$ and the integral is an
ordinary Riemann integral in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]).

**(f) Variation of the timelike length and particle action.** Let
$\gamma:[a,b]\to U$ and $H$ be as in
[[lem-gr-first-variation-of-proper-time]], so that $\gamma$ is $C^2$, future
timelike, parametrized with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$, the variation is $C^2$
with fixed endpoints and future timelike fibres, and $L(s)$ is the length
functional of that lemma. Then the first-variation formulas (1)-(3) of that
lemma hold verbatim. Consequently for every $m>0$ the particle action
$S_p(\gamma):=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt$ satisfies
$\partial_sS_p(H(s,\cdot))|_{s=0}=-mc\,L'(0)$, so within this class of curves
and variations $\gamma$ is stationary for $S_p$ if and only if
$D_t\gamma'=0$, i.e. if and only if $\gamma$ is a geodesic in its proper-time
parameter ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

derivations.claim:
Fix any positively oriented coordinate ball and let $\chi$ be a smooth real gauge parameter compactly supported inside it. The gauge variation is $\alpha=d\chi$ together with the associated matter-field gauge variation, whose action contribution vanishes by [A1]. Gauge invariance and the stated first variation give $0=\delta_\chi S_m= rac1c\int_M j^a
abla_a\chi\,\mathrm{vol}_g$. The product rule writes the integrand as $
abla_a(\chi j^a)-\chi
abla_aj^a$; the first term integrates to zero by [F6], because $\operatorname{supp}(\chi j)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\chi$ is compact inside the chosen chart. If $
abla_aj^a$ were nonzero at a point, continuity and a nonnegative compact bump supported where it has fixed sign, whose existence is part of [F6], would contradict the resulting integral identity for all $\chi$. Since the ball and its tests are arbitrary, $
abla_aj^a=0$ at every point of $M$.

Let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field compactly supported inside an arbitrary positively oriented coordinate ball, and use its local flow from [F4] together with the induced horizontal lift to $P$. In a local trivialization with potential $A_a$, the ordinary pullback variation is $(\mathcal L_\xi A)_a=\xi^b\partial_bA_a+A_b\partial_a\xi^b=\xi^bF_{ba}+\partial_a(\xi^bA_b)$. The last term is an infinitesimal gauge variation; the horizontal lift removes it. Thus the connection variation is $\alpha_a=\xi^bF_{ba}$. Since $F$ is global by [F2], this formula agrees on overlaps and defines the required global connection variation.

By [F5], the metric derivative along the same local flow has inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=-(
abla^a\xi^b+
abla^b\xi^a)$. Simultaneous diffeomorphism invariance, the on-shell matter condition [A1], and the first-variation formula therefore give $0= rac1c\int_M\left(T^m_{ab}
abla^a\xi^b+j^a\xi^bF_{ba}ight)\mathrm{vol}_g$, where symmetry of $T^m$ combines its two metric-variation terms.

The product rule gives $T^m_{ab}
abla^a\xi^b=
abla^a(T^m_{ab}\xi^b)-(
abla^aT^m_{ab})\xi^b$. The vector field $W^a=(T^m)^a{}_b\xi^b$ is compactly supported inside the chosen chart, so its divergence integrates to zero by [F6], so step 2.1 becomes $\int_M(-
abla^aT^m_{ab}+F_{ba}j^a)\xi^b\,\mathrm{vol}_g=0$ for every vector test $\xi$ compactly supported inside that ball. The ball was arbitrary; [F6] therefore makes the smooth covector coefficient vanish pointwise throughout $M$. Relabeling the contracted index and raising $b$ yields $
abla_aT_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c$, completing the proof.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ by $z=x+iy$ and set $U(1)=S^1:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$. Its topology is the subspace topology. Specify its smooth structure by the four charts

$$V_{x,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon x>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto y,\quad y\mapsto(\epsilon\sqrt{1-y^2},y),$$

and

$$V_{y,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon y>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto x,\quad x\mapsto(x,\epsilon\sqrt{1-x^2}),$$

for $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, with each coordinate range $(-1,1)$. They cover $S^1$; their transition maps are restrictions of the positive square-root branch and coordinate projections, hence are smooth by [[lem-emg-positive-square-root-smoothness]] and [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]. In these coordinates multiplication is the restriction of $(x,y)(u,v)=(xu-yv,xv+yu)$ and inversion is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$, so both are smooth; they are also continuous for the stated topology. Thus this is a smooth Lie group and, in particular, a topological group as required by [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].

Let $E:\mathbb R\to U(1)$ be $E(t)=e^{it}=(\cos t,\sin t)$; the Cartesian formula is [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The trigonometric derivative identities of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], iterated, show that $E$ is smooth in the $C^\infty$ sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: every derivative of either coordinate is $\pm\sin$ or $\pm\cos$, and these functions are continuous by [[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]. Surjectivity is [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]]. If $E(t)\in V_{x,\epsilon}$, the chart coordinate $\sin t$ has derivative $\cos t=x\ne0$; if $E(t)\in V_{y,\epsilon}$, the coordinate $\cos t$ has derivative $-\sin t=-y\ne0$. The smooth inverse-function theorem [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] therefore makes $E$ a diffeomorphism from some open interval about $t$ onto an open circle arc. Every smooth map from an open subset of $M$ to $U(1)$ consequently has, near each point, a smooth real phase lift obtained by composing with such a local inverse.

A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, take any smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. If $f$ and $\widetilde f$ are two lifts on a connected neighborhood, [[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]] gives $f-\widetilde f\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ pointwise; continuity makes this difference constant, so $df=d\widetilde f$. Thus the compatibility condition is independent of the chosen lift. The globally defined form $\lambda(g):=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ is real, and [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] together with [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] gives $\lambda(g)=df$ on every phase-lift neighborhood. Hence the equivalent lift-free condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The right principal $U(1)$-bundle convention is as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]: it has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts, with free and transitive action on each fibre. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, let $K\subseteq U$ be compact, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval with $0\in I$, and let $s\mapsto g(s)$, $s\in I$, be a family of
smooth Lorentzian metrics of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ such that

- $g(0)=g$ and $g(s)=g$ on $M\setminus K$ for every $s\in I$; and
- the components $g(s)_{ab}$ in the chart are smooth functions of $(s,x)$ on
  $I\times x(U)$ ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

Write $h_{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)_{ab}|_{s=0}$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field with support in $K$, and
$q^{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)^{ab}|_{s=0}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$). In particular any prescribed smooth compactly
supported inverse-metric direction $q$ is realized by $g+s h$ on a
sufficiently small interval, with $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$.

**(b) Variation of the Christoffel symbols.** The field
$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_s\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}|_{s=0}$ is a smooth
tensor field on $U$ and

$$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}\bigl(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(c) Variation of the Ricci tensor (Palatini identity).**
$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\partial_s\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd}|_{s=0}$
satisfies

$$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\nabla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-\nabla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}.$$

**(d) Variation of the curvature density.** With
$V^{a}:=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$ and
$w(s):=\sqrt{|\det(g(s)_{ab})|}$ the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],

$$\partial_s\bigl(w(s)S(s)\bigr)\big|_{s=0}=w\,G_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a\bigl(wV^{a}\bigr).$$

**(e) Variation of the chart action integral.** For every constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, the function
$F(s):=\int_U\bigl[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)\bigr]\,d^4x$ is the compactly supported chart action difference, differentiable at $0$, and

$$F'(0)=\int_U\bigl(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}\bigr)q^{ab}\,w\,d^4x,$$

where the integrand is compactly supported in $K$ and the integral is an
ordinary Riemann integral in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]).

**(f) Variation of the timelike length and particle action.** Let
$\gamma:[a,b]\to U$ and $H$ be as in
[[lem-gr-first-variation-of-proper-time]], so that $\gamma$ is $C^2$, future
timelike, parametrized with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$, the variation is $C^2$
with fixed endpoints and future timelike fibres, and $L(s)$ is the length
functional of that lemma. Then the first-variation formulas (1)-(3) of that
lemma hold verbatim. Consequently for every $m>0$ the particle action
$S_p(\gamma):=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt$ satisfies

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, let $\mathcal X$ be a set, and let

$$S:\mathcal D\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$

be a real-valued functional defined on a subset $\mathcal D$ of the set of
pairs $(\tilde g,\varphi)$ with $\tilde g$ a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal X$. Fix $(\tilde g,\varphi)\in
\mathcal D$; below we always take $\tilde g=g$. The elements $\varphi$ are the
model's matter configurations; nothing about their nature is assumed here.
Assume that $\mathcal D$ admits every compactly supported metric direction at
$(g,\varphi)$: for each smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ with
compact support, there is $\varepsilon_h>0$ such that
$(g+s h,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon_h$. Since
$\mathcal D$ contains only pairs whose metric is Lorentzian, these admitted
linear families are Lorentzian throughout that interval. This condition makes every compactly
supported inverse-metric variation available as well, since
$h\mapsto -g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$ is a bijection on compactly supported smooth
symmetric tensor fields.

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating $L(g,\varphi)\mathrm{vol}_g$ with an orientation-independent
scalar coefficient $L$ and the integral exists (or compact action differences
are used), define the reversed-orientation action by the same construction.
Reversing orientation replaces $\mathrm{vol}_g$ by $-\mathrm{vol}_g$ and
reverses the sign of integration of a fixed top form. These two signs cancel,
so both the action variation and the integral in the defining identity are
unchanged, as is its tensor $T$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold, let $g$ be a smooth symmetric nondegenerate
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $(U,x)$ be any smooth
chart, with indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$. Write $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$,
let $(g^{ab})$ be the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$, and define the strictly
positive chart weight $w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$. These are local
matrix constructions; no signature, time orientation or orientation is assumed.
A continuous covariant tensor field means a family of bilinear forms whose
chart components are continuous; smooth means that they are $C^\infty$.
For a covector or vector field the same regularity convention applies to its
components in the coordinate dual basis or coordinate basis, respectively.
Let $F$ be a
continuous symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$. Suppose that for every
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $q$ on $M$ whose support is a
compact subset of $U$,

$$\int_U F_{ab}(x)\,q^{ab}(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0,$$

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Write $;e$ for the induced
covariant derivative and raise indices with $g^{-1}$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Second Bianchi identity.** For all indices $a,b,c,d,e$,
$$R^a{}_{bcd;e}+R^a{}_{bde;c}+R^a{}_{bec;d}=0,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad R_{abcd;e}+R_{abde;c}+R_{abec;d}=0 .$$
Equivalently, the antisymmetrization over the last three slots vanishes:
$R^a{}_{b[cd;e]}=0$.

**(b) Contracted identities.** $\nabla^a\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
=\tfrac12\nabla_bS$, and consequently
$$\nabla^aG_{ab}=0\qquad\text{for every }b,$$
where $\nabla^aG_{ab}:=g^{ae}\nabla_eG_{ab}$. The conclusion is the vanishing
of the contracted divergence for each second index; it does not assert that
all components $\nabla_cG_{ab}$ vanish.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For an oriented smooth manifold $M^n$, possibly with boundary, and $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$, choose a smooth partition $(\rho_i)$ subordinate to connected interior or boundary charts $(U_i,\phi_i)$. For $n\geq1$ set
$$\int_M\omega=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\rho_i\omega).$$
Each product has compact support in its chart and only finitely many are nonzero, by [[lem-a-locally-finite-sum-is-finite-near-the-compact-support-of-a-form]]. For $n=0$ set
$$\int_M\omega=\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p).$$
$\Lambda^0T_p^*M\cong\mathbb R$ has two orientations; define $\varepsilon(p)=+1$ when $1$ is positive in the chosen orientation and $\varepsilon(p)=-1$ when $-1$ is positive.
A zero-manifold is discrete; the singleton open cover of a compact subset has a finite subcover. Thus this sum too is finite. Empty support or empty $M$ gives zero. Independence of the choices is discharged by [[thm-global-form-integration-is-independent-of-the-atlas-partition-and-refinement]].

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The compact-support integral on an oriented manifold is independent of the chart cover, coordinate maps, subordinate partition, and refinement. If $U\subset M$ is open and contains $\operatorname{supp}\omega$, with its restricted orientation, then $\int_U\omega|_U=\int_M\omega$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

derivations.claim: For a family in [A1], the top form $\omega_s=(R(g(s))-2\Lambda)\mathrm{vol}_{g(s)}-(R(g)-2\Lambda)\mathrm{vol}_g$ is supported in the common compact $K$. Define its relative action by [F6], even if the separate background integrals diverge. Fix a subordinate partition independently of $s$; only finitely many terms meet $K$, and each has compact support inside its chart. The uniform difference-quotient argument in the Maxwell supplier [F2] differentiates this finite sum. Clause (d) of [F1] gives its derivative density locally, and $\delta(-2\Lambda\mathrm{vol}_g)=\Lambda g_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$. The field $V$ is global because $\delta\Gamma$ is a tensor, and is supported in $K$. The compact divergence argument in [F2] now gives $\int_M\nabla_aV^a\mathrm{vol}_g=0$: apply chart FTC to each $\rho_iV$ and sum, with $\sum_i d\rho_i=0$ near $K$. Thus no single chart or enclosing finite singular chain is presumed. Multiplication by $c^3/(16\pi G_N)$ yields $\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$, as claimed.
Add [F2] and [F3]. Since $\frac{1}{2c}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}$, the total variation is exactly the expression in the Statement with $\kappa_E=8\pi G_N/c^4$.

If the action is stationary for every compactly supported $q^{ab}$, step 2.1 implies that the continuous symmetric coefficient $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})$ pairs to zero with every such $q$. Because $c,G_N>0$, its prefactor is nonzero; [F4] therefore gives the displayed field equation pointwise.

Conversely, if the displayed field equation holds pointwise, the coefficient in step 2.1 is zero everywhere, so its integral vanishes for every compactly supported $q$. This proves stationarity and the equivalence.

Take the covariant divergence of the field equation in step 3.1. By [F5], $
abla^aG_{ab}=0$ and $
abla^a(\Lambda g_{ab})=\Lambda
abla^ag_{ab}=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. Since $\kappa_E>0$, division gives $
abla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$. No PDE existence follows from this necessary compatibility identity.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, let $K\subseteq U$ be compact, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval with $0\in I$, and let $s\mapsto g(s)$, $s\in I$, be a family of
smooth Lorentzian metrics of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ such that

- $g(0)=g$ and $g(s)=g$ on $M\setminus K$ for every $s\in I$; and
- the components $g(s)_{ab}$ in the chart are smooth functions of $(s,x)$ on
  $I\times x(U)$ ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

Write $h_{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)_{ab}|_{s=0}$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field with support in $K$, and
$q^{ab}:=\partial_sg(s)^{ab}|_{s=0}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$). In particular any prescribed smooth compactly
supported inverse-metric direction $q$ is realized by $g+s h$ on a
sufficiently small interval, with $h_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$.

**(b) Variation of the Christoffel symbols.** The field
$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_s\Gamma(s)^{a}{}_{bc}|_{s=0}$ is a smooth
tensor field on $U$ and

$$\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}\bigl(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(c) Variation of the Ricci tensor (Palatini identity).**
$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\partial_s\operatorname{Ric}(s)_{bd}|_{s=0}$
satisfies

$$\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\nabla_a\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-\nabla_d\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}.$$

**(d) Variation of the curvature density.** With
$V^{a}:=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^{a}{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^{d}{}_{db}$ and
$w(s):=\sqrt{|\det(g(s)_{ab})|}$ the metric density of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]],

$$\partial_s\bigl(w(s)S(s)\bigr)\big|_{s=0}=w\,G_{ab}q^{ab}+\partial_a\bigl(wV^{a}\bigr).$$

**(e) Variation of the chart action integral.** For every constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, the function
$F(s):=\int_U\bigl[(S(s)-2\Lambda)w(s)-(S(0)-2\Lambda)w(0)\bigr]\,d^4x$ is the compactly supported chart action difference, differentiable at $0$, and

$$F'(0)=\int_U\bigl(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}\bigr)q^{ab}\,w\,d^4x,$$

where the integrand is compactly supported in $K$ and the integral is an
ordinary Riemann integral in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]).

**(f) Variation of the timelike length and particle action.** Let
$\gamma:[a,b]\to U$ and $H$ be as in
[[lem-gr-first-variation-of-proper-time]], so that $\gamma$ is $C^2$, future
timelike, parametrized with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-c^2$, the variation is $C^2$
with fixed endpoints and future timelike fibres, and $L(s)$ is the length
functional of that lemma. Then the first-variation formulas (1)-(3) of that
lemma hold verbatim. Consequently for every $m>0$ the particle action
$S_p(\gamma):=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}\,dt$ satisfies
$\partial_sS_p(H(s,\cdot))|_{s=0}=-mc\,L'(0)$, so within this class of curves
and variations $\gamma$ is stationary for $S_p$ if and only if
$D_t\gamma'=0$, i.e. if and only if $\gamma$ is a geodesic in its proper-time
parameter ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating $L(g,\varphi)\mathrm{vol}_g$ with an orientation-independent
scalar coefficient $L$ and the integral exists (or compact action differences
are used), define the reversed-orientation action by the same construction.
Reversing orientation replaces $\mathrm{vol}_g$ by $-\mathrm{vol}_g$ and
reverses the sign of integration of a fixed top form. These two signs cancel,
so both the action variation and the integral in the defining identity are
unchanged, as is its tensor $T$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold, let $g$ be a smooth symmetric nondegenerate
covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), and let $(U,x)$ be any smooth
chart, with indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$. Write $g_{ab}=g(\partial_a,\partial_b)$,
let $(g^{ab})$ be the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$, and define the strictly
positive chart weight $w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$. These are local
matrix constructions; no signature, time orientation or orientation is assumed.
A continuous covariant tensor field means a family of bilinear forms whose
chart components are continuous; smooth means that they are $C^\infty$.
For a covector or vector field the same regularity convention applies to its
components in the coordinate dual basis or coordinate basis, respectively.
Let $F$ be a
continuous symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$. Suppose that for every
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $q$ on $M$ whose support is a
compact subset of $U$,

$$\int_U F_{ab}(x)\,q^{ab}(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0,$$

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Write $;e$ for the induced
covariant derivative and raise indices with $g^{-1}$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Second Bianchi identity.** For all indices $a,b,c,d,e$,
$$R^a{}_{bcd;e}+R^a{}_{bde;c}+R^a{}_{bec;d}=0,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad R_{abcd;e}+R_{abde;c}+R_{abec;d}=0 .$$
Equivalently, the antisymmetrization over the last three slots vanishes:
$R^a{}_{b[cd;e]}=0$.

**(b) Contracted identities.** $\nabla^a\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
=\tfrac12\nabla_bS$, and consequently
$$\nabla^aG_{ab}=0\qquad\text{for every }b,$$
where $\nabla^aG_{ab}:=g^{ae}\nabla_eG_{ab}$. The conclusion is the vanishing
of the contracted divergence for each second index; it does not assert that
all components $\nabla_cG_{ab}$ vanish.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions: The supporting smooth Lorentzian geometry is under the published $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ tangent-bundle convention; no use of full AC is needed in these variational calculations. ([[def-countable-choice]])

citations.quote: Let $G$ be a topological group, as in [[def-topological-group]], with identity $1$. A **right principal $G$-bundle** is a continuous map $\pi:P\to B$ with a continuous right action $(p,g)\mapsto pg$, satisfying $p1=p$, $(pg)h=p(gh)$ and $\pi(pg)=\pi(p)$, together with equivariant bundle charts $\theta_i:\pi^{-1}(U_i)\cong U_i\times G$ over an open cover. Equivariance means $\theta_i(pg)=(b,ag)$ whenever $\theta_i(p)=(b,a)$. Charts use ordinary products as in [[def-locally-trivial-fiber-bundle]].

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ by $z=x+iy$ and set $U(1)=S^1:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$. Its topology is the subspace topology. Specify its smooth structure by the four charts

$$V_{x,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon x>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto y,\quad y\mapsto(\epsilon\sqrt{1-y^2},y),$$

and

$$V_{y,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon y>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto x,\quad x\mapsto(x,\epsilon\sqrt{1-x^2}),$$

for $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, with each coordinate range $(-1,1)$. They cover $S^1$; their transition maps are restrictions of the positive square-root branch and coordinate projections, hence are smooth by [[lem-emg-positive-square-root-smoothness]] and [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]. In these coordinates multiplication is the restriction of $(x,y)(u,v)=(xu-yv,xv+yu)$ and inversion is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$, so both are smooth; they are also continuous for the stated topology. Thus this is a smooth Lie group and, in particular, a topological group as required by [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].

Let $E:\mathbb R\to U(1)$ be $E(t)=e^{it}=(\cos t,\sin t)$; the Cartesian formula is [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The trigonometric derivative identities of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], iterated, show that $E$ is smooth in the $C^\infty$ sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: every derivative of either coordinate is $\pm\sin$ or $\pm\cos$, and these functions are continuous by [[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]. Surjectivity is [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]]. If $E(t)\in V_{x,\epsilon}$, the chart coordinate $\sin t$ has derivative $\cos t=x\ne0$; if $E(t)\in V_{y,\epsilon}$, the coordinate $\cos t$ has derivative $-\sin t=-y\ne0$. The smooth inverse-function theorem [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] therefore makes $E$ a diffeomorphism from some open interval about $t$ onto an open circle arc. Every smooth map from an open subset of $M$ to $U(1)$ consequently has, near each point, a smooth real phase lift obtained by composing with such a local inverse.

A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, take any smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. If $f$ and $\widetilde f$ are two lifts on a connected neighborhood, [[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]] gives $f-\widetilde f\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ pointwise; continuity makes this difference constant, so $df=d\widetilde f$. Thus the compatibility condition is independent of the chosen lift. The globally defined form $\lambda(g):=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ is real, and [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] together with [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] gives $\lambda(g)=df$ on every phase-lift neighborhood. Hence the equivalent lift-free condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The right principal $U(1)$-bundle convention is as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]: it has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts, with free and transitive action on each fibre. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts.

derivations.claim: On every triple overlap, $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ and integer $k$ give $g_{ij}^{k}g_{jk}^{k}=g_{ik}^{k}$, so the scalar transition data satisfy the cocycle. On any local phase-lift neighborhood, changing $f_{ij}$ by $2\pi n$ leaves $e^{ikf_{ij}}$ unchanged. Also $dA_j=dA_i+\kappa_0d^2f_{ij}=dA_i$ by [F2]; these local equalities patch because they hold near every point of each overlap, so $F$ is global.

Expanding the derivative gives $P_{j,a}=e^{ikf_{ij}}[\partial_a\varphi_i+ik(\partial_af_{ij})\varphi_i-i\lambda A_{i,a}\varphi_i-i\lambda\kappa_0(\partial_af_{ij})\varphi_i]$. The phase-derivative terms cancel because $\lambda\kappa_0=k$, so $P_{j,a}=e^{ikf_{ij}}P_{i,a}$. Hence $|\varphi|^2$ and $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ are independent of the local trivialization.

Complex conjugation and exchange of dummy indices show $\overline{g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b}=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$. Since $V$ is real-valued, $L_\varphi$ is a global real scalar. Its product with the oriented metric volume form is a real four-form, so compactly supported action differences have the well-defined integral supplied by [F3].

Adding the same real global one-form $\alpha$ to every $A_i$ leaves $A_j-A_i=\kappa_0df_{ij}$ unchanged. Therefore the prescribed connection variations retain the local transition data and remain in the same bundle sector.

In length-coordinate components, $[L_\varphi]=\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $[\mathrm{vol}_g]=\mathrm m^4$, while $[K_\varphi/c]=(\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1})/(\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})=\mathrm J\,\mathrm s\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Therefore $S_\varphi$ has units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts.
