Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Set $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. Let $P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle in the sense of [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]], with a fixed smooth connection. Choose local trivializations and normalized real connection potentials $A_i$ as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. On any overlap neighborhood admitting a smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$, write $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$. Use the dual representation $\rho_k(z):=z^{-k}$ and define charged scalar representatives by the global transition rule $\varphi_j=g_{ij}^{k}\varphi_i$, equivalently $e^{ikf_{ij}}\varphi_i$ on each phase-lift neighborhood; the connection rule there is

$$A_j=A_i+\kappa_0\,df_{ij}.$$

Here $\kappa_0>0$ is the chosen circle normalization with $[\kappa_0]=\mathrm{Wb}$, $k\in\mathbb Z$ is the representation weight, and $\lambda:=k/\kappa_0$ has units $\mathrm{Wb}^{-1}$. Because $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ and $k$ is an integer, the maps $g_{ij}^{k}$ satisfy the scalar transition cocycle. A charged scalar is a family of smooth local functions $\varphi_i$ satisfying this rule; all phase-lift calculations below are local, and no global phase lift is assumed. The constant $c>0$ is the length-to-time conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Define $F|_{U_i}:=dA_i$; the transition law gives $dA_j=dA_i$, so $F$ is a global curvature two-form. In a global real-potential model on a trivial bundle, one may instead take a global $A$ and any real $\lambda$; no charge quantization is imposed there.

In a local trivialization define the gauge-covariant derivative and its lower-index one-form by

$$P_a:=(D\varphi)_a:=\partial_a\varphi_i-i\lambda A_{i,a}\varphi_i.$$

The transition laws give $P_{j,a}=e^{ikf_{ij}}P_{i,a}$, since $\lambda\kappa_0=k$. For any charged covector $Q_b$ with the same phase transition, define the gauge- and metric-covariant derivative by $D_aQ_b:=\nabla_aQ_b-i\lambda A_aQ_b$ in a local trivialization; for a charged scalar $\eta$, set $D_a\eta:=\partial_a\eta-i\lambda A_a\eta$. Conjugate fields use the opposite gauge sign. Thus $D_aP_b$ is a well-defined charged covariant two-tensor, and $D_aP^a:=g^{ab}D_aP_b$. Consequently $|\varphi|^2$ and $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ are global scalar fields. Let $V:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth on an open set $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the range of $|\varphi|^2$, write $V'$ for its ordinary real derivative, and choose a positive normalization constant $K_\varphi>0$.

The kinetic scalar $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ is real because its complex conjugate equals itself by symmetry of $g^{ab}$. Put

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad S_\varphi:=-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M L_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

For SI dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[\varphi]=1$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[P_a]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[V]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[K_\varphi]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1}$; then $S_\varphi$ has units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$. These are formal dimensional assignments, not measured values or physical postulates. On noncompact $M$, the integral is used when finite; otherwise only differences between configurations agreeing outside a compact set are defined, so every variation below is a compactly supported integral.

Allowed first variations are compactly supported smooth complex-section variations $\delta\varphi$, compactly supported real global one-form variations $\alpha=\delta A$ added to every local $A_i$ (so the same bundle transition functions are retained), and compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$. The formula defines a classical mathematical functional; it asserts no quantum interpretation, value of $\hbar$, or material-response model.

Let $M$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable oriented four-manifold, and let $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ be a normalized circle-connection datum as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Use the set-sized-object and quotient convention of [[def-emg-set-size-and-class-schema]]. Then the chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal $U(1)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a global smooth real connection one-form $\omega$ on $P$. Its curvature is basic: there is a smooth closed two-form $f\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $d\omega=\pi^*f$ and $f|_{U_i}=da_i$. The local potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ satisfy $dA_i=F$, where $F=\kappa_0 f$ is global. For two connections on the same fixed bundle with the same transition functions, their local-form differences are restrictions of one global base one-form; adding a global one-form to all local representatives stays in that bundle sector.

**(a) Variation of the inverse metric; realizability.** $q^{ab}
=-g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$; conversely, for every smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h_0$ with compact support in $U$ there is $\lambda_0>0$ such
that for every $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the family $s\mapsto g+s\lambda h_0$
satisfies the hypotheses above on the parameter interval $(-1,1)$ (with
$K=\operatorname{supp}h_0$).

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected connection $\nabla$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle with a smooth connection and global curvature two-form $F$, using the local-potential and fixed-sector conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] and [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]]. Let $\Psi$ be a smooth matter configuration and let $S_m$ be a real differentiable functional of $(g,A,\Psi)$, where $A$ denotes the bundle connection, not necessarily a global one-form.

Fix a configuration at which the matter Euler–Lagrange variation vanishes, meaning $\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every smooth compactly supported matter-field variation. Suppose that for all compactly supported metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and all compactly supported connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ in the fixed bundle sector, the remaining first variation is

$$\delta S_m=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+\frac{1}{c}\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $c>0$, $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $j$ is a smooth vector field. Assume $S_m$ is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations and under simultaneous pullback along the local flow of every compactly supported smooth vector field, with the connection and matter field transported by the induced horizontal lift to $P$. Only the local variations at flow parameter $s=0$ are used. Then

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a T_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,$$

where $j_c:=g_{ca}j^a$. These are conditional variational identities; no Maxwell or Einstein field equation, existence theorem, or empirical premise is assumed.

For SI bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, and $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$. If $S_m$ is assigned action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, the displayed variation convention assigns $[T^m]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. These are formal dimensional assignments only; the lemma adopts no matter model or empirical law.

where $q^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}q_{cd}$ are the components of $q$ raised with the
inverse metric and the integral is the ordinary Riemann integral of the
continuous compactly supported function
$F_{ab}q^{ab}w$ in the chart coordinates
([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). Then
$F=0$ on $U$. Moreover, if $W$ is a continuous covector field on $U$ with
$\int_UW_a(x)\,q^a(x)\,w(x)\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth vector field $q$ on $M$
whose support is a compact subset of $U$, then $W=0$ on $U$.

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

derivations.claim: Let $\eta=\delta\varphi$ be a compactly supported complex section. Direct differentiation gives $\delta_\varphi L_\varphi=2\operatorname{Re}(g^{ab}\overline{D_a\eta}P_b+V'\overline\eta\varphi)$. The gauge-covariant product rule gives $\nabla_a(\overline\eta P^a)=\overline{D_a\eta}P^a+\overline\eta D_aP^a$, so [F3] removes the compact divergence and $\int\overline{D_a\eta}P^a\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\int\overline\eta D_aP^a\,\mathrm{vol}_g$. Multiplying by $-K_\varphi/(2c)$ yields the displayed scalar variation. If stationarity holds, then $\operatorname{Re}\int\overline\eta E_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g=0$ for all compactly supported $\eta$. In a positively oriented chart, for every compactly supported real vector field $q=q^a\partial_a$, its component $q^0$ is a real test function; choosing $\eta=q^0$ in the local scalar frame gives zero pairing of the covector $W_a=(\operatorname{Re}E_\varphi)\delta_a^0$ with $q$. [F5] implies $\operatorname{Re}E_\varphi=0$. Choosing instead $\eta=iq^0$ gives zero pairing for $W_a=(\operatorname{Im}E_\varphi)\delta_a^0$, so [F5] implies $\operatorname{Im}E_\varphi=0$. Thus $E_\varphi=0$ pointwise. Conversely, $E_\varphi=0$ makes the variation zero for every test section; hence stationarity is equivalent to $E_\varphi=0$.

At fixed $g,\varphi$, a real connection variation $\alpha_a$ gives $\delta_A P_a=-i\lambda\varphi\alpha_a$ and $\delta_A\overline{P_a}=+i\lambda\overline\varphi\alpha_a$. Their contraction is $\delta_A L_\varphi=-2\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a)\alpha_a$, so $\delta_A S_\varphi=\frac1c\int_MK_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a)\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g$. This is the stated current.

At fixed lower $A$ and fixed $\varphi$, the inverse-metric variation gives $\delta_gL_\varphi=\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)q^{ab}$. Combining this with [F2] in $S_\varphi=-K_\varphi(2c)^{-1}\int L_\varphi\mathrm{vol}_g$ yields $\delta_gS_\varphi=-\frac1{2c}\int_M\left[K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi\right]q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, the displayed Hilbert tensor.

The covariant derivative of $j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a)$ is $K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline{P_a}P^a+\overline\varphi D_aP^a)$. The first term is real; adding $V'|\varphi|^2$ inside the imaginary part changes nothing because $V'$ is real. Therefore $\nabla_a j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi(D_aP^a-V'\varphi))=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi E_\varphi)$.

Raise the first index of $T^\varphi$ and differentiate. Using [F6] to differentiate contractions and $\nabla_bL_\varphi=2\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P^a}D_bP_a)+2V'\operatorname{Re}(\overline\varphi P_b)$, the product rule gives $\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}\left(\overline{E_\varphi}P_b+\overline{P^a}(D_aP_b-D_bP_a)\right)$. In a local trivialization, symmetry of the Levi-Civita symbols and commutation of scalar partial derivatives give $D_aP_b-D_bP_a=-i\lambda F_{ab}\varphi$. Hence the second term is $-K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a)F_{ab}=F_{ba}j^a$, proving the stated off-shell stress identity.

If $E_\varphi=0$, steps 2.1–2.2 give $\nabla_aj^a=0$ and $\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=F_{ba}j^a$. The scalar functional is gauge invariant because $P_a$ changes by the same phase as $\varphi$, and is diffeomorphism invariant because its integrand is a scalar density; thus the general identity [F4] applies and gives the same raised-index exchange equation. This also checks the sign against the independent variational Noether route.

Use the scalar functional of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]] on a fixed smooth bundle sector, with $K_\varphi>0$, real $\lambda$, real smooth $V$, and smooth $\varphi,A,g$. Write $P_a:=D_a\varphi$ and define the gauge- and metric-covariant derivative of its one-form by

$$D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b,$$

with the conjugate derivative using $+i\lambda A_a$. For compactly supported variations, define

$$E_\varphi:=D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\,\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

Then the scalar-field variation is $\delta_\varphi S_\varphi=\frac{K_\varphi}{c}\operatorname{Re}\int_M\overline{\delta\varphi}\,E_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g$; stationarity in every compactly supported complex scalar direction is equivalent to $E_\varphi=0$. The connection and inverse-metric variations are

$$\delta_A S_\varphi=\frac1c\int_Mj^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta_gS_\varphi=-\frac1{2c}\int_MT^\varphi_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

The following off-shell identities also hold:

$$\nabla_a j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi E_\varphi),\qquad \nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_\varphi}P_b)+F_{ba}j^a.$$

In particular, the matter equation $E_\varphi=0$ implies current conservation and the exact Lorentz-force exchange identity $\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c$. No coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution or empirical matter model is asserted.

Under the formal SI assignments of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]], $j^a$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and $T^\varphi$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; this dimensional check is not an empirical claim.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

derivations.claim: Since $A=0$, $D_a=\partial_a$ and $D_aD^a=-c^{-2}\partial_t^2+\Delta$. The plane wave has $\partial_t^2\varphi=-\omega^2\varphi$ and $\Delta\varphi=-|\mathbf k|^2\varphi$, so $E_\varphi=(\omega^2/c^2-|\mathbf k|^2-m_s^2)\varphi=0$ by [A1].

The current formula [F1] gives $j^0=K_\varphi\lambda(\omega/c)|C|^2$ and $j^i=K_\varphi\lambda k_i|C|^2$. Thus $j=0$ when $\lambda=0$, while for $\lambda\ne0$ its temporal component is nonzero because $K_\varphi,\omega,|C|^2$ are positive.

In either case $F=dA=0$ and hence $\partial_aF^{a0}=0$. If $\lambda\ne0$, [F2] would require $0=-\mu_0j^0$ although $\mu_0j^0\ne0$ by step 1.2. Therefore the background scalar solution with nonzero coupling does not solve the sourced Maxwell equation; when $\lambda=0$, this particular current obstruction is absent.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For a compactly supported metric variation, write $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$, $h_{ab}=\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$, $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, and $V^a=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^d{}_{db}$, where $\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12g^{ad}(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc})$; curvature and Einstein tensors are as in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. The local density identity is

$$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a).$$

Fix constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard these as formal coefficients; their physical interpretation and units are not assumptions of this mathematical lemma. For smooth metric variations with compact support in the interior, at fixed bundle connection and fixed matter fields, consider the action difference

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_m,$$

where noncompact action values are used only through compactly supported differences, $F$ is the curvature of a fixed smooth bundle connection, and $S_m$ has Hilbert tensor $T^m$ in the convention of [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]. Let $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor supplied by the compact Maxwell variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], and set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. Then for every compactly supported inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$,

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M\left(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})\right)q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently, stationarity under all such metric variations is equivalent to

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}).$$

Any tensor fields satisfying this equation necessarily have $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. This is a compatibility condition, not a claim that the coupled field equations have a solution or that matter and Maxwell equations follow from metric stationarity.

For dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates one may assign $[R]=[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T^m]=[T^{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Then every action term has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $\kappa_E T$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These are formal assignments only; the lemma assumes no measured parameter value or physical field law.

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

derivations.claim: By [F3], choose nonnegative compactly supported dimensionless $\chi$ equal to one near the origin and dimensionless $\rho$ equal to one near zero. The factor $x^3/\ell$ gives $h_{ab}|_{x^3=0}=0$. At the boundary, $\partial_3 f=\chi/\ell$ and $\partial_\alpha f=0$ for $\alpha=0,1,2$; in particular, at the origin $\partial_3f=1/\ell$. Since $f$ is bounded and nonzero, $g_s=(1+sf)\eta$ has the same Lorentzian signature whenever $|s|<1/(2\|f\|_\infty)$. Thus the metric value is fixed at the boundary while its normal derivative is not.

At the flat background, substituting $h_{ab}=f\eta_{ab}$ into [F1] gives $\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12(\delta^a_c\partial_bf+\delta^a_b\partial_cf-\eta_{bc}\partial^af)$. Contracting the two terms in $V^a$ gives $\eta^{bd}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{db}=-\partial^af$ and $\eta^{ab}\delta\Gamma^d{}_{db}=2\partial^af$, hence $V^a=-3\partial^af$. On $x^3=0$, $V^3=-3\chi/\ell$.

Since $G_{ab}=0$, the linearized Einstein–Hilbert density is just $\partial_aV^a$ by [F1]. The tangential integrals vanish because $\chi$ is compactly supported, and the upper normal endpoint contributes zero because $\rho$ is compactly supported. The fundamental theorem of calculus on $x^3\in[0,\infty)$ therefore gives, after multiplying by the action coefficient, the boundary contribution $-\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_{x^3=0}V^3\,dx^0dx^1dx^2=\frac{3c^3}{16\pi G_N\ell}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\chi\,dx^0dx^1dx^2>0$. This is the outward flux for conormal $-dx^3$.

The nonzero first-variation boundary term in step 3.1 occurs despite $h_{ab}=0$ on $\partial H$. Therefore fixing only boundary metric values does not justify discarding the Einstein–Hilbert derivative flux.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, let $\mathcal X$ be a set, and let

$$S:\mathcal D\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$

be a real-valued functional defined on a subset $\mathcal D$ of the set of
pairs $(\tilde g,\varphi)$ with $\tilde g$ a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal X$. Fix $(\tilde g,\varphi)\in
\mathcal D$; below we always take $\tilde g=g$. The elements $\varphi$ are the
model's matter configurations; nothing about their nature is assumed here.
Assume that $\mathcal D$ admits every compactly supported metric direction at
$(g,\varphi)$: for each smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ with
compact support, there is $\varepsilon_h>0$ such that
$(g+s h,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon_h$. Since
$\mathcal D$ contains only pairs whose metric is Lorentzian, these admitted
linear families are Lorentzian throughout that interval. This condition makes every compactly
supported inverse-metric variation available as well, since
$h\mapsto -g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$ is a bijection on compactly supported smooth
symmetric tensor fields.

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating $L(g,\varphi)\mathrm{vol}_g$ with an orientation-independent
scalar coefficient $L$ and the integral exists (or compact action differences
are used), define the reversed-orientation action by the same construction.
Reversing orientation replaces $\mathrm{vol}_g$ by $-\mathrm{vol}_g$ and
reverses the sign of integration of a fixed top form. These two signs cancel,
so both the action variation and the integral in the defining identity are
unchanged, as is its tensor $T$.

Let $\Psi$ be a smooth matter configuration and let $S_m$ be a real differentiable functional of $(g,A,\Psi)$, where $A$ denotes the bundle connection, not necessarily a global one-form.

Fix a configuration at which the matter Euler–Lagrange variation vanishes, meaning $\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every smooth compactly supported matter-field variation. Suppose that for all compactly supported metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and all compactly supported connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ in the fixed bundle sector, the remaining first variation is

$$\delta S_m=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+\frac{1}{c}\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $c>0$, $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $j$ is a smooth vector field. Assume $S_m$ is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations and under simultaneous pullback along the local flow of every compactly supported smooth vector field, with the connection and matter field transported by the induced horizontal lift to $P$. Only the local variations at flow parameter $s=0$ are used. Then

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a T_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,$$

where $j_c:=g_{ca}j^a$. These are conditional variational identities; no Maxwell or Einstein field equation, existence theorem, or empirical premise is assumed.

For SI bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, and $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$. If $S_m$ is assigned action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, the displayed variation convention assigns $[T^m]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

For the gravitational sector, take Newton's gravitational constant $G_N>0$ with unit $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ and the cosmological constant parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ as primitive parameters of the selected model; no numerical value for either is used here. The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For a compactly supported metric variation, write $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$, $h_{ab}=\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$, $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, and $V^a=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^d{}_{db}$, where $\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12g^{ad}(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc})$; curvature and Einstein tensors are as in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. The local density identity is

$$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a).$$

Fix constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard these as formal coefficients; their physical interpretation and units are not assumptions of this mathematical lemma. For smooth metric variations with compact support in the interior, at fixed bundle connection and fixed matter fields, consider the action difference

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_m,$$

where noncompact action values are used only through compactly supported differences, $F$ is the curvature of a fixed smooth bundle connection, and $S_m$ has Hilbert tensor $T^m$ in the convention of [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]. Let $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor supplied by the compact Maxwell variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], and set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. Then for every compactly supported inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$,

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M\left(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})\right)q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently, stationarity under all such metric variations is equivalent to

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}).$$

Any tensor fields satisfying this equation necessarily have $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. This is a compatibility condition, not a claim that the coupled field equations have a solution or that matter and Maxwell equations follow from metric stationarity.

For dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates one may assign $[R]=[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T^m]=[T^{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Then every action term has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $\kappa_E T$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These are formal assignments only; the lemma assumes no measured parameter value or physical field law.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and let $c,\mu_0>0$ be fixed
real coefficients. The action density is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If a differentiable source-sector functional on the same variations satisfies
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

**(b) Metric variation.** For a smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse
metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

Adopt as a physical formulation principle of this framework, as an alternative
to postulating the field equations and the force law directly, the following
assumption about the functionals, variation classes and stationarity predicate
of [[def-em-field-action-definition]].

(i) [Field sector] A smooth field $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$ on the region $U$ of
clause (a) of that definition is dynamically admissible exactly when it is
stationary for the field action $S[A]$ under all compactly supported smooth
variations $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ in the sense of clause (b) of that
definition: $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$.

(ii) [Particle sector] For a prescribed external four-potential $A_\mu$ on a
neighbourhood of the image of a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline $X$,
the motion is dynamically admissible exactly when $X$ is stationary for the
particle functional $S_{\rm pt}$ of clause (c) of that definition under all
fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations.

This is an adopted assumption of the model, not a theorem, not a derivation
from the remaining postulates and not an empirical result. It asserts
stationarity only: it does not assert that a stationary configuration is a
local or global minimum, that stationary configurations exist or are unique,
that the action functional is uniquely determined or forced by symmetry, that
no other action formulation is possible, or that the two sectors can be
coupled into a single well-posed action for singular sources. No Noether
theorem, no symmetry-to-conservation machinery and no matter dynamics beyond
the prescribed potential are assumed.

The conditional deductions of this pair are: on the declared smooth classes,
(i) is equivalent to the inhomogeneous tensor field equation
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and, for potential-represented fields, to
the smooth-branch Maxwell equations, and (ii) is equivalent to the framework's
adopted four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$; both deductions are
recorded separately on this page and in
[[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]] and
[[pthm-em-particle-action-coupling]], and this postulate asserts neither.

For the action-based Einstein–Maxwell branch, choose one actual smooth matter
configuration space $\mathcal C$ on the spacetime of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle
$\pi:P\to M$, and a real differentiable functional $S_m[g,\omega,\Psi]$ on
its declared domain, where $\Psi\in\mathcal C$ and $\omega$ is a smooth
principal connection on that fixed bundle. Use a supplied cover and fixed
transition data with normalized real local connection representatives $a_i$;
on phase-lift neighborhoods their convention is
$a_j=a_i+df_{ij}$ when $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$. With the fixed normalization
$\kappa_0>0$ of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], the local expression for $\omega$
in a circle coordinate $z\in U(1)$ is $-iz^{-1}dz+a_i$. Define the physical local
potentials $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$. They obey
$A_j=A_i+\kappa_0df_{ij}$, and their local exterior derivatives patch to the
global physical curvature $F$, with $F|_{U_i}=dA_i=\kappa_0da_i$ and
$dF=0$. A global real potential is not assumed. The field class, transition
data, gauge action, matter equations, and compact variation class must be
specified for the chosen matter model.

If the selected matter model is given by a global physical potential
$A\in\Omega^1(M)$, use the trivial principal bundle $P=M\times U(1)$ with its
global trivialization and normalized representative $a=A/\kappa_0$; its
principal connection is locally $-iz^{-1}dz+a$. This is the trivial-bundle
global-potential branch, and the model may admit any real coupling when its
gauge transformations are specified by compactly supported real lifts. A
nontrivial bundle sector instead uses the stated local transition data and the
model's compatible matter-field transition rules.

The functional is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations
of the fixed bundle sector and under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms,
with the connection and matter fields transported together. In particular,
for every smooth compactly supported real gauge parameter $\chi$ with units
Wb, its group map is $g_\chi=e^{i\chi/\kappa_0}$; it acts by
$a_i\mapsto a_i+\kappa_0^{-1}d\chi$ and hence by
$A_i\mapsto A_i+d\chi$, together with the model's specified matter-field
transformation. For a compactly supported
vector field $\xi$, transport by the induced horizontal lift gives the
physical connection variation $\alpha_a=\xi^bF_{ba}$ used by
[[lem-emg-matter-noether-exchange]].

Adopt matter-field stationarity as part of this selected model:
$\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every admissible compactly supported matter variation.
For compactly supported inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and
fixed-sector compact physical connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$,
vary the local potentials by $A_i(s)=A_i+s\alpha|_{U_i}$, equivalently the
normalized representatives by $a_i(s)=a_i+s\kappa_0^{-1}\alpha|_{U_i}$.

citations.quote:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, curvature
convention and SI constants of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Choose the actual matter functional
$S_m[g,\omega,\Psi]$ and its fixed smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle
$\pi:P\to M$ from [[post-emg-selected-matter-action]]. In its fixed normalized
connection sector, the local representatives are $a_i$, the physical local
potentials are $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$, and their globally defined physical curvature
satisfies $F|_{U_i}=dA_i=\kappa_0da_i$ and $dF=0$. A global real potential is
not required. Write $R:=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ for the scalar
curvature of the metric-selected connection, with the curvature convention
of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For configurations where the action is
finite, or for compactly supported action differences on a noncompact
manifold, adopt

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}[g,\omega,\Psi] =\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g -\frac1{4\mu_0c}\int_M F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g +S_m[g,\omega,\Psi].$$

Adopt that a configuration is dynamically admissible in this branch exactly
when the first variation of this total action vanishes independently for
every smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variation, every
smooth compactly supported fixed-sector physical connection variation
$\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$, and every admissible compactly supported matter-field
variation. The connection variation changes $A_i$ by $\alpha|_{U_i}$,
equivalently changes $a_i$ by $\kappa_0^{-1}\alpha|_{U_i}$, while leaving the
bundle and transition data fixed; thus $\delta F=d\alpha$. If $M$ has a
physical boundary, only variations vanishing on a neighbourhood of that
boundary are included. This makes no claim about a Gibbons–Hawking–York or
other boundary action.

The earlier postulate [[post-em-stationary-action-model]] concerns its stated
flat electromagnetic and prescribed-potential particle sectors. It supplies
no unified matter–gravity action or coupled-solution theorem; the functional
above is an additional, explicitly adopted model. An equation-based
Einstein–Maxwell formulation is a separate alternative, not a premise of this
action branch.

All displayed coefficients are model parameters with the units and
interpretations in [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Compact support is essential:
the Einstein–Hilbert and Maxwell integrations by parts have boundary terms in
general. The postulate asserts neither that its stationary configurations exist
nor that the action describes nature.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and let $c,\mu_0>0$ be fixed
real coefficients. The action density is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If a differentiable source-sector functional on the same variations satisfies
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

**(b) Metric variation.** For a smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse
metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For a compactly supported metric variation, write $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$, $h_{ab}=\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$, $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, and $V^a=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^d{}_{db}$, where $\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12g^{ad}(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc})$; curvature and Einstein tensors are as in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. The local density identity is

$$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a).$$

Fix constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard these as formal coefficients; their physical interpretation and units are not assumptions of this mathematical lemma. For smooth metric variations with compact support in the interior, at fixed bundle connection and fixed matter fields, consider the action difference

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_m,$$

where noncompact action values are used only through compactly supported differences, $F$ is the curvature of a fixed smooth bundle connection, and $S_m$ has Hilbert tensor $T^m$ in the convention of [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]. Let $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor supplied by the compact Maxwell variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], and set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. Then for every compactly supported inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$,

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M\left(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})\right)q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently, stationarity under all such metric variations is equivalent to

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}).$$

Any tensor fields satisfying this equation necessarily have $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. This is a compatibility condition, not a claim that the coupled field equations have a solution or that matter and Maxwell equations follow from metric stationarity.

For dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates one may assign $[R]=[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T^m]=[T^{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Then every action term has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $\kappa_E T$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These are formal assignments only; the lemma assumes no measured parameter value or physical field law.

Let $M$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable oriented four-manifold, and let $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ be a normalized circle-connection datum as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Use the set-sized-object and quotient convention of [[def-emg-set-size-and-class-schema]]. Then the chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal $U(1)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a global smooth real connection one-form $\omega$ on $P$. Its curvature is basic: there is a smooth closed two-form $f\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $d\omega=\pi^*f$ and $f|_{U_i}=da_i$. The local potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ satisfy $dA_i=F$, where $F=\kappa_0 f$ is global. For two connections on the same fixed bundle with the same transition functions, their local-form differences are restrictions of one global base one-form; adding a global one-form to all local representatives stays in that bundle sector.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
By [F1], the connection variation of the total action is the sum of the
Maxwell variation and the selected matter variation in [F2]. Their displayed
integrals combine to
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{tot}}=(\mu_0c)^{-1}\int_M
(\nabla_aF^{ab}+\mu_0j^b)\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$. The local bump argument
and its converse are exactly the conditional equivalence in [F2], so
stationarity for every admissible $\alpha$ is equivalent to the sourced
Maxwell equation in the Statement.

Apply [F3] to the metric part of [F1]. For every admissible compact
symmetric inverse-metric variation, its first variation vanishes exactly when
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})$ pointwise.
The Maxwell tensor in [F3] is the tensor from the metric variation at fixed
lower $F_{ab}$; it is not an independently guessed source.

By the adopted stationarity clause in [F1], the matter-field variations
vanish exactly under the condition
$\delta_\Psi S_m[\zeta]=0$ for every allowed compactly supported $\zeta$.
This records the equations of the chosen functional without inventing a
matter equation for an unspecified $S_m$.

The three variation classes are independent. If the total action is
stationary for all of them, steps 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3 give each displayed
condition. Conversely, if all three conditions hold, each corresponding first
variation vanishes by those steps, and their sum is the first variation of
$S_{\mathrm{tot}}$; hence it vanishes for every allowed total variation.
Finally, [F4] gives $dF=0$ for every connection curvature in this model.
No existence of a stationary configuration is used.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and step 2.1: an empty spacetime restriction makes the tensor equations and all compactly supported variations vacuous in both stationarity directions; no stationary configuration is constructed.

Steps 1.1–1.3: zero variation directions give zero first variation; the equivalences still require every admissible direction. F=0 makes the Maxwell stress zero without removing the selected matter equation.

boundaries.reason: Statement: the independent metric, connection and matter variation classes are not a cardinality-indexed family; a single test variation is never asserted sufficient for stationarity.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and step 1.2: the metric variations are those of the Lorentzian action supplier and preserve nondegeneracy for small parameter; no degenerate metric or vanishing positive coupling is admitted.

Step 1.1 with A1: variations have compact interior support, or vanish near physical boundaries; the supplier integration by parts therefore contributes no endpoint/boundary term. No unrestricted boundary variation is claimed.
Steps 1.1–1.2 and A2: compact integration uses exactly the stated indexed AC_omega; the three variation equations apply to supplied fields and do not select a configuration from a solution set.
step 2.1: stationarity of independent compact variations implies each sector equation.
step 2.1: if each sector equation holds, every independent first variation and their sum vanish.

citations.quote:
Adopt the following physical field law for this Einstein–Maxwell model. Let $M$ be a smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ as in [[def-emg-geometry-units]], let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $F\in\Omega^2(U)$ be a smooth real electromagnetic two-form, and let $j$ be a smooth four-current vector field on $U$. Using the Levi-Civita connection $\nabla^g$ of $g$, the SI constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$, and the field/current conventions of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], postulate

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

This is the selected smooth vacuum constitutive law. The first equation is the homogeneous field equation; the second is the sourced field equation with the sign fixed by $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $j=(c\rho,J)$ in a positively oriented inertial tetrad. No global potential is assumed: although $F=dA$ implies $dF=0$ when a smooth potential exists, the postulate applies to the two-form itself and does not assert that such an $A$ exists globally.

The postulate adopts one curved-spacetime continuation as a physical model assumption. The flat Minkowski and special-relativity suppliers [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] fix the inherited SI, inertial, and flat-limit conventions; they do not impose a globally flat metric on $M$ or deduce this curved field law. General-relativity sources describe covariant Maxwell formulations in their own unit and sign conventions; those treatments motivate the chosen formulation but neither mathematical structure nor source authority proves that this is nature's law. No empirical result is adopted here.

The model has no magnetic-charge term and no material excitation pair such as $D,H$. It applies only to smooth $F$ and $j$ on the stated domain; point and sheet sources, distribution-valued fields, and products of distributions require separate definitions and are outside this postulate.

For the action-based Einstein–Maxwell branch, choose one actual smooth matter
configuration space $\mathcal C$ on the spacetime of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle
$\pi:P\to M$, and a real differentiable functional $S_m[g,\omega,\Psi]$ on
its declared domain, where $\Psi\in\mathcal C$ and $\omega$ is a smooth
principal connection on that fixed bundle. Use a supplied cover and fixed
transition data with normalized real local connection representatives $a_i$;
on phase-lift neighborhoods their convention is
$a_j=a_i+df_{ij}$ when $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$. With the fixed normalization
$\kappa_0>0$ of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], the local expression for $\omega$
in a circle coordinate $z\in U(1)$ is $-iz^{-1}dz+a_i$. Define the physical local

where $c>0$, $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $j$ is a smooth vector field. Assume $S_m$ is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations and under simultaneous pullback along the local flow of every compactly supported smooth vector field, with the connection and matter field transported by the induced horizontal lift to $P$. $$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a T_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,$$

where $j_c:=g_{ca}j^a$. These are conditional variational identities; no Maxwell or Einstein field equation, existence theorem, or empirical premise is assumed.

metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],

$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Write $;e$ for the induced
covariant derivative and raise indices with $g^{-1}$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

$$R^a{}_{bcd;e}+R^a{}_{bde;c}+R^a{}_{bec;d}=0,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad R_{abcd;e}+R_{abde;c}+R_{abec;d}=0 .$$

where $\nabla^aG_{ab}:=g^{ae}\nabla_eG_{ab}$. The conclusion is the vanishing

all components $\nabla_cG_{ab}$ vanish.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Apply [F3] using the smoothness and Maxwell equations in [F1]. This gives
$\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^{bc}j_c$ pointwise on $U$. The sign is fixed
by the sourced convention in [F1].

Because the matter fields are on shell and the action has the required
invariances, $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c$. This term is the force received by
the matter subsystem, not separate matter conservation.

Add the identities in steps 1.1 and 1.2. Their right sides are exact
opposites with the same raised-index convention, so
$\nabla_a(T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}+T_m^{ab})=0$.

If the pointwise Einstein equation in the Statement also holds, take its
covariant divergence. By [F5], $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$; metric compatibility gives
$\nabla^a(\Lambda g_{ab})=\Lambda\nabla^ag_{ab}=0$ because $\Lambda$ is
constant. By [F6], $\kappa_E>0$, so the field equation requires
$\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$. This agrees with step 2.1 after
lowering its free index and is only a compatibility condition; it does not
solve the field equations.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

For the gravitational sector, take Newton's gravitational constant $G_N>0$ with unit $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ and the cosmological constant parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ as primitive parameters of the selected model; no numerical value for either is used here. The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

Let $U$ be an open subset of the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold and use the metric, units, and electromagnetic conventions of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. A restricted smooth charged-dust configuration
consists of constants $m>0$ in kilograms and $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs, a
smooth future-directed vector field $U^a$ with $g_{ab}U^aU^b=-c^2$, and a
smooth scalar field $\nu:U\to(0,\infty)$. Put $u^a:=U^a/c$, so
$g_{ab}u^au^b=-1$, and at each $x\in U$ define its local rest space by
$H_x:=\{v\in T_xM:g_x(v,u_x)=0\}$. The restriction $\gamma_x:=g_x|_{H_x}$
is a positive-definite inner product. In any basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $H_x$
with linear coordinates $(y^1,y^2,y^3)$, its proper 3-volume density is
$dV_{\mathrm{rest}}=\sqrt{\det(\gamma_x(e_i,e_j))}\,|dy^1dy^2dy^3|$;
this density is independent of the chosen basis. The scalar $\nu(x)$ is the
proper number density measured in this rest space: the local particle-number
measure has density $\nu\,dV_{\mathrm{rest}}$. Thus $[\nu]=\mathrm{m^{-3}}$.
Define the rest-space projector $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+U^aU_b/c^2$.
The associated four-current and matter stress tensor are

$$j^a:=q\nu U^a,\qquad T_m^{ab}:=m\nu U^aU^b.$$

Their length-coordinate SI units are $[U^a]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$,
$[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T_m^{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The
single-velocity condition means that at every event in the model domain all
dust matter there is assigned the same vector $U_x$; a state with distinct
future unit timelike velocities at one event is outside this model. In this
item, a caustic or multistream breakdown is a point where the material
description can no longer be represented by smooth fields $\nu,U$ with
$0<\nu<\infty$ and one such velocity. The model domain is restricted to open
regions excluding those breakdown points. This is a scope convention, not a
claim that caustics are avoided or that the fields exist globally. As the
continuum closure of this model, adopt on the smooth solution domain

$$\nabla_a(\nu U^a)=0,\qquad m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U),$$

where $\nabla_UU^a:=U^b\nabla_bU^a$ and
$g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$, as in the external-charge convention of
[[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. The latter supplies
test-body sign and normalization context only; it proves neither the
continuum number equation nor a continuum or coupled PDE evolution law.

This definition applies only while $\nu,U,F,g$ remain smooth and the
single-velocity dust description is valid. It makes no claim that such
solutions exist globally or avoid caustics, and it does not assign a
distributional stress tensor to point particles.
