Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, curvature
convention and SI constants of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Choose the actual matter functional
$S_m[g,\omega,\Psi]$ and its fixed smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle
$\pi:P\to M$ from [[post-emg-selected-matter-action]]. In its fixed normalized
connection sector, the local representatives are $a_i$, the physical local
potentials are $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$, and their globally defined physical curvature
satisfies $F|_{U_i}=dA_i=\kappa_0da_i$ and $dF=0$. A global real potential is
not required. Write $R:=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ for the scalar
curvature of the metric-selected connection, with the curvature convention
of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For configurations where the action is
finite, or for compactly supported action differences on a noncompact
manifold, adopt

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}[g,\omega,\Psi] =\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g -\frac1{4\mu_0c}\int_M F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g +S_m[g,\omega,\Psi].$$

Adopt that a configuration is dynamically admissible in this branch exactly
when the first variation of this total action vanishes independently for
every smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variation, every
smooth compactly supported fixed-sector physical connection variation
$\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$, and every admissible compactly supported matter-field
variation. The connection variation changes $A_i$ by $\alpha|_{U_i}$,
equivalently changes $a_i$ by $\kappa_0^{-1}\alpha|_{U_i}$, while leaving the
bundle and transition data fixed; thus $\delta F=d\alpha$. If $M$ has a
physical boundary, only variations vanishing on a neighbourhood of that
boundary are included. This makes no claim about a Gibbons–Hawking–York or
other boundary action.

The earlier postulate [[post-em-stationary-action-model]] concerns its stated
flat electromagnetic and prescribed-potential particle sectors. It supplies
no unified matter–gravity action or coupled-solution theorem; the functional
above is an additional, explicitly adopted model. An equation-based
Einstein–Maxwell formulation is a separate alternative, not a premise of this
action branch.

All displayed coefficients are model parameters with the units and
interpretations in [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Compact support is essential:
the Einstein–Hilbert and Maxwell integrations by parts have boundary terms in
general. The postulate asserts neither that its stationary configurations exist
nor that the action describes nature.

Let $(M,g)$, the fixed smooth connection sector, the constants $c,G_N,\mu_0>0$,
constant $\Lambda$, and the selected matter functional $S_m$ be exactly those
of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]]. Write $F$ for the connection curvature,
$j$ and $T^m$ for the current and Hilbert tensor in the selected matter
variation, and define
$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Rg_{ab}$ using the Ricci and scalar
curvature contractions in the convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Also
set

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad \kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$

The homogeneous identity $dF=0$ holds because $F$ is the curvature of the
smooth connection in the fixed sector. The adopted configuration is stationary
under every admissible compactly supported metric, connection, and matter
variation if and only if all of the following hold:

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}),\qquad \delta_\Psi S_m[\zeta]=0\ \text{for every admissible compactly supported }\zeta.$$

The last clause is the selected matter model's Euler–Lagrange condition; an
explicit local matter equation cannot be given until $S_m$ is specified.
These are model deductions from the adopted action and smooth compact
variation hypotheses, not evidence that a coupled solution exists or that the
model describes nature.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use its metric-selected connection and curvature convention. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

Within this formulation, $c$, $G_N$, $\mu_0$, and $\Lambda$ are primitive model parameters: respectively, the time-to-length conversion parameter, the gravitational coupling parameter, the electromagnetic normalization parameter identified with vacuum permeability in the SI convention, and the coefficient of the cosmological term. Their values are not derived by this definition, and no numerical value or empirical exactness claim is made here. The coupling $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from $G_N$ and $c$. For the SI interpretation, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $G_N$ has units $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $\mu_0$ has units $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, $\kappa$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and $\Lambda$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. In a length-coordinate chart $x^0=ct$, metric components are dimensionless and curvature components have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

For a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, define

$$Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T^{\rm EM}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The electromagnetic stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor; in an orthonormal frame its components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ is a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, define $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$. By [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], these are $E_i/c$ and $B_i$ in the SI observer convention; both have units tesla.

For sign clarity only, a sourced extension would write $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$ for a smooth current vector $J$; the source-free system below is the case $J=0$.

The **source-free electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is the system for a smooth Lorentz metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ on $U$ given by

$$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$ is the Einstein tensor. A **spacelike initial hypersurface** is a smooth spacelike embedded three-manifold $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow U$ with induced Riemannian metric $h=i^*g$ and future unit normal $n$, using [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]. Its second fundamental form is $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ for tangent vectors $X,Y$. The notation $K=\tfrac12\mathcal L_nh$ requires an induced-metric family: locally near each $p\in\Sigma$, define $\Phi(t,q)=\gamma_{q,n_q}(t)$ by the ambient geodesic with initial position $q$ and initial tangent $n_q$. Smooth dependence of geodesics and the inverse function theorem give, after shrinking around $(0,p)$, a local diffeomorphism $\Phi:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times V\to U_p$; its slices remain spacelike after a further shrinking. Put $h_t:=\Phi_t^*g$ on $V$. In local slice coordinates $y^i$, differentiating $(h_t)_{ij}=g_{ab}(\Phi(t,y))\partial_i\Phi^a\partial_j\Phi^b$ at $t=0$ gives
$$\left.\partial_t(h_t)_{ij}\right|_{0}=n^c\partial_cg_{ab}\,\partial_i\Phi^a\partial_j\Phi^b+g_{cb}(\partial_i n^c)\partial_j\Phi^b+g_{ac}\partial_i\Phi^a(\partial_jn^c)=g(\nabla_{\partial_i}n,\partial_j\Phi)+g(\nabla_{\partial_j}n,\partial_i\Phi)=2K_{ij},$$
using metric compatibility, torsion-freeness and symmetry of $K$. Thus $\mathcal L_nh$ denotes only this initial derivative of the local induced-metric family; no global normal foliation or uniform time width is assumed. A hypersurface is a **Cauchy hypersurface in $U$** exactly when every inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ meets it at exactly one parameter value, that is, $\gamma^{-1}[i(\Sigma)]$ has exactly one element, using the causal-curve convention of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]. The local initial-data constructions require a spacelike initial hypersurface; they do not assume this global intersection property. The initial data are the induced $(h,K,e,b)$, where $e,b$ are the spatial fields just defined. No global electromagnetic potential is part of this definition.

In the SI convention the electromagnetic two-form has orthonormal-frame components in tesla, $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and every term of the Einstein equation has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. The equations define a mathematical model; they do not assert that the model describes nature or that arbitrary Cauchy data have a development.

Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty, smooth, oriented three-manifold without boundary. Let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b$ be smooth vector fields tangent to $\Sigma$. For data induced on an embedded spacelike slice $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$, let $n$ be its future unit normal, let $F$ be the smooth two-form of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], and define spatial covectors $\mathcal E,\mathcal B\in\Omega^1(\Sigma)$ by $\mathcal E(X):=F(X,n)$ and $\mathcal B(X):=-({\star_gF})(X,n)$ for $X\in T\Sigma$. Identify these with vector fields using the positive metric $h$: $e:=\sharp_h\mathcal E$ and $b:=\sharp_h\mathcal B$, so in any coordinates $e^i=h^{ij}\mathcal E_j$ and $b^i=h^{ij}\mathcal B_j$. Equivalently, $\mathcal E$ is the restriction of the observer electric covector $E/c$ and $\mathcal B$ the restriction of the observer magnetic covector $B$ of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. For an abstract data tuple not assumed to come from $F$, $e,b$ are simply the specified tangent vector fields. This fixes the convention without adding a potential or an existence assumption.

For the observer-covector comparison above, the smooth normal along $\Sigma$ has local smooth ambient extensions by [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]; shrinking and normalizing an extension gives an observer congruence to which [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]] applies. The restrictions $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ depend only on $n|_\Sigma$, so they are independent of the chosen extension.

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix to $h_{ij}$ and use $h$ to raise every spatial index. Let $D$ and $R(h)$ denote the Levi-Civita connection and scalar curvature of $h$, set $\tau:=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell}$, and choose the induced spatial orientation so $\operatorname{vol}_g=\theta^0\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h=-n^\flat\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h$ in a positively oriented normal coframe with $\theta^0(n)=1$. Define the spatial cross product by $h(e\times_hb,w)=\operatorname{vol}_h(e,b,w)$ for each tangent vector $w$.

For the fixed parameters $(\kappa,\Lambda,\mu_0)$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], the tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ is **constrained electrovacuum initial data** when

$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,$$

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\bigl(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2\bigr),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

Here the last display is an equality of covectors. The scalar-curvature form is the Gauss-Codazzi form of the normal projections in [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; the sign and $K$ convention are those of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness of a spacetime development.

For the periodic high-regularity class, use the dimensionless coordinate $\theta^i$ and length coordinate $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], for a fixed $L_0>0$. The arrays $h_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ are the length-coordinate covariant components with $h_{ij}\in H^{s+1}$ and $K_{ij}\in H^s$. The Sobolev components of $e,b$ are $e_A=h(e,\mathsf e_A)$ and $b_A=h(b,\mathsf e_A)$ in the canonical positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $\mathsf e_A$ specified there; thus $e_A,b_A\in H^s$. If $\mathsf e_A=E_A^i\partial_{X^i}$, their coordinate components are $e^i=E_A^i e_A$ and $b^i=E_A^i b_A$. The coefficients $E_A^i$ are smooth functions of the positive matrix $h_{ij}$; on the compact range of each such metric, [[lem-gr-smooth-composition-and-commutator-estimates]] puts them in $H^{s+1}$ and [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-algebra]] makes the coordinate components $H^s$ as well.

For these representatives define the spatial connection coefficients by $\Gamma(h)^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12h^{k\ell}(\partial_{X^i}h_{j\ell}+\partial_{X^j}h_{i\ell}-\partial_{X^\ell}h_{ij})$, with $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. On coordinate vector components put $D_i e^j=\partial_{X^i}e^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}e^k$ and $D_i b^j=\partial_{X^i}b^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}b^k$; on the covariant tensor $K$ put $D_iK_{jk}=\partial_{X^i}K_{jk}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ij}K_{\ell k}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ik}K_{j\ell}$. Define $R(h)$ by $R^a{}_{bij}=\partial_{X^i}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jb}-\partial_{X^j}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ib}+\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ic}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{jb}-\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jc}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{ib}$, followed by the Ricci and scalar contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Sobolev embedding gives $h\in C^{s-1}$ and $K,e,b\in C^{s-2}$; the uniform positive lower eigenvalue makes $h^{-1}$ well defined, and the smooth-composition and algebra suppliers give $\Gamma(h)\in H^s$, $R(h)\in H^{s-1}$, and $D K,D e,D b\in H^{s-1}$. Since $s\ge5$, these constraint terms have continuous representatives, and their displayed equalities mean pointwise equality of those representatives. In the SI interpretation, $K$ and $D$ carry one inverse-length factor, $R(h)$ and $\Lambda$ carry inverse-length squared, and the orthonormal components $e_A,b_A$ have units tesla; the factors $\kappa/\mu_0$ give matching units in the constraints. No numerical parameter values are assigned here.

**Data.** Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $K$. The normal convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Specify one fixed covariant matter model, consisting of a finite list of smooth tensor fields $\psi$, fixed equations $\mathcal E(g,\psi)=0$ and a fixed stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\psi)$, with pullback by local diffeomorphisms commuting with the equations and stress. Fix its complete smooth Cauchy data $d$: these determine all independent matter initial variables, not only the normal stress projections. Initial tensors with normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb R\nu\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_0(a\nu+X,b\nu+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. In a development, identify $a\nu+X$ with $an+dj(X)$.

An admissible fixed coupled model is one satisfying the complete initialization, hyperbolic reduction, recovery and comparison hypotheses of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]], or a specified independent local existence and uniqueness reduction such as the dust branch below. The same fixed model, complete data and admissibility conditions are used in every comparison and at every restart. Admissibility includes the applicability of its supplied complete-data local existence and geometric uniqueness theorem to the data realized on each spacelike restart surface of the compared solutions. This must be checked for the actual model and surface; it is not inferred from stress conservation. This class includes the following four concrete branches; they do not exhaust it.

1. **Vacuum:** no matter fields, $\mathcal T=0$, and empty matter data.
2. **Scalar field:** fix one smooth potential $V$ and one normalization $K_\phi>0$. The field is $\varphi$, its equation is $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$, its stress is the expression in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] clause (c), and its complete data are $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ with $\pi_0=n(\varphi)|_\Sigma$. The fixed potential has no sign restriction ([[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]).
3. **Strict barotropic fluid:** fix a smooth EOS $P:J\to\mathbb R$ on an open interval with $\epsilon+P(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<P'(\epsilon)<1$. The fields are $\epsilon\in J$ and future unit velocity $u$, the stress is $(\epsilon+P(\epsilon))u^\flat\otimes u^\flat+P(\epsilon)g$, and the equations are the continuity and Euler equations of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (c), with this fixed EOS. Complete data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, where $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(\nu+v_0)$. No small-tilt restriction is imposed ([[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]).
4. **Geodesic nonnegative dust:** the fields are an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and a smooth future unit timelike field $u$, including on $\{\varepsilon=0\}$. Set $\mathcal T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$ and require both $\nabla_u u=0$ and $u(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\nabla_a u^a=0$ everywhere. Complete data are $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$, with $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ and prescribed smooth future unit bundle velocity $U_0$, equivalently arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt. On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with its density parameter equal to $\varepsilon$. Through empty regions the geodesic velocity is separately prescribed and matched; conservation of stress alone is not substituted for this full system. For a fixed $c>0$, the mass-normalized theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] applies with $\rho_0=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and reconstructs $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$.

Require the constraints for the initial stress $T_0$ computed from this complete data on $\mathcal V$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\nu,\nu),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(\nu,\cdot).$$
These use the convention of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Equality of data includes equality of the model, constants, potential or EOS, and every component of $d$.

The local Cauchy-development and uniqueness suppliers for vacuum, scalar and strict fluid are the fixed-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] and the two concrete branch theorems above. Its harmonic route requires the same fixed extraction/reconstruction rules and smooth symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family for every compared physical solution, a positive time matrix on an admissible open state set, complete compatible initialization from $(h,K,d)$, propagation of auxiliary compatibility with recovery of the full matter equations on the reduced solution, and stress conservation on that reduced solution before Einstein recovery. These are the three explicit hypotheses of that theorem; conservation alone does not supply a Cauchy evolution law. Dust uses its independent common-flow/parallel-frame initialization, hyperbolic reduction, subsidiary recovery and uniqueness of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]], rather than being asserted to satisfy the harmonic metric-first-derivative matter contract. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried wherever these local theorems are invoked. Every additional fixed coupled model must supply the same complete-data local existence, admissibility, recovery and uniqueness obligations before it is used. This definition makes no local or global existence assertion.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. the smooth tensor fields $\psi$ of the fixed model over $M$;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,\mathcal T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $\mathcal E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $d$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$: the isometry carries the future cone of $N$ onto that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, with the natural pullback action on every listed tensor type (and the inverse differential on contravariant slots). Equality includes every listed field, including the prescribed dust velocity at zero density.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,d)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty connected smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, and smooth spatial vectors $e,b$. Fix the source-free Einstein–Maxwell model, its constants $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, orientation and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ convention as in [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. Assume the four constraints of [[thm-emg-gauss-codazzi-maxwell-constraints]] and reconstruct the complete initial two-form by $F(N,\mathsf e_i)=-e_i$, $F(\mathsf e_i,\mathsf e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$. Then there is a smooth connected time-oriented globally hyperbolic development $(M_{\max},g_{\max},F_{\max},\iota)$ into which every other smooth source-free Einstein–Maxwell development of these complete data embeds by a time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding fixing $\iota$ and carrying $F$ to $F_{\max}$. The maximal development is unique up to a unique such data-fixing isometry. This maximality is within the smooth globally hyperbolic development class for this fixed two-form model; it asserts no geodesic completeness, no maximality among rough or non-globally-hyperbolic extensions, and no global-in-time regularity estimate.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ by $z=x+iy$ and set $U(1)=S^1:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$. Its topology is the subspace topology. Specify its smooth structure by the four charts

$$V_{x,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon x>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto y,\quad y\mapsto(\epsilon\sqrt{1-y^2},y),$$

and

$$V_{y,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon y>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto x,\quad x\mapsto(x,\epsilon\sqrt{1-x^2}),$$

for $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, with each coordinate range $(-1,1)$. They cover $S^1$; their transition maps are restrictions of the positive square-root branch and coordinate projections, hence are smooth by [[lem-emg-positive-square-root-smoothness]] and [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]. In these coordinates multiplication is the restriction of $(x,y)(u,v)=(xu-yv,xv+yu)$ and inversion is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$, so both are smooth; they are also continuous for the stated topology. Thus this is a smooth Lie group and, in particular, a topological group as required by [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].

Let $E:\mathbb R\to U(1)$ be $E(t)=e^{it}=(\cos t,\sin t)$; the Cartesian formula is [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The trigonometric derivative identities of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], iterated, show that $E$ is smooth in the $C^\infty$ sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: every derivative of either coordinate is $\pm\sin$ or $\pm\cos$, and these functions are continuous by [[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]. Surjectivity is [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]]. If $E(t)\in V_{x,\epsilon}$, the chart coordinate $\sin t$ has derivative $\cos t=x\ne0$; if $E(t)\in V_{y,\epsilon}$, the coordinate $\cos t$ has derivative $-\sin t=-y\ne0$. The smooth inverse-function theorem [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] therefore makes $E$ a diffeomorphism from some open interval about $t$ onto an open circle arc. Every smooth map from an open subset of $M$ to $U(1)$ consequently has, near each point, a smooth real phase lift obtained by composing with such a local inverse.

A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, take any smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. If $f$ and $\widetilde f$ are two lifts on a connected neighborhood, [[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]] gives $f-\widetilde f\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ pointwise; continuity makes this difference constant, so $df=d\widetilde f$. Thus the compatibility condition is independent of the chosen lift. The globally defined form $\lambda(g):=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ is real, and [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] together with [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] gives $\lambda(g)=df$ on every phase-lift neighborhood. Hence the equivalent lift-free condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The right principal $U(1)$-bundle convention is as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]: it has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts, with free and transitive action on each fibre. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

Let $M$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable oriented four-manifold, and let $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ be a normalized circle-connection datum as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Use the set-sized-object and quotient convention of [[def-emg-set-size-and-class-schema]]. Then the chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal $U(1)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a global smooth real connection one-form $\omega$ on $P$. Its curvature is basic: there is a smooth closed two-form $f\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $d\omega=\pi^*f$ and $f|_{U_i}=da_i$. The local potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ satisfy $dA_i=F$, where $F=\kappa_0 f$ is global. For two connections on the same fixed bundle with the same transition functions, their local-form differences are restrictions of one global base one-form; adding a global one-form to all local representatives stays in that bundle sector.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth
time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, and let
$i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth spacelike Cauchy embedding. If
$F,\bar F\in\Omega^2(M)$ are smooth closed two-forms with
$i^*F=i^*\bar F$, then $F-\bar F$ is exact: there is a smooth
$\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ such that $d\alpha=F-\bar F$.

Here a closed form has zero exterior derivative, and exactness means being the
exterior derivative of a globally defined smooth form, as in
[[def-de-rham-cohomology]].

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), and let
$t$ be the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]]. Then
there exist a smooth function $T:M\to\mathbb R$ and, with $\nabla T$ the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], the
following hold.

**(a)** $T$ is a temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e): smooth,
$g(\nabla T,\nabla T)<0$ and $g(\nabla T,N)>0$ everywhere.

**(b)** Every level set $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy
hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a)
and (c)): it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and every inextendible
causal curve meets it in exactly one parameter value. In particular $T$ is
surjective.

**(c)** Along every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$T\to+\infty$, and along every inextendible past-directed causal curve
$T\to-\infty$.

**(d)** The vector field $X:=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is smooth,
future-directed timelike, satisfies $X(T)=1$, and is complete
([[def-complete-vector-field]]): every maximal integral curve of $X$ is
defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so by
[[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]] its
flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is a global smooth flow
([[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

**(e)** The map $\Psi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to M$, $\Psi(s,z):=\Phi(s,z)$, is
a diffeomorphism and $T(\Psi(s,z))=s$ for all $(s,z)$; equivalently $M$ is
foliated by the Cauchy hypersurfaces $S_c$, each flow line meeting each level
exactly once.

**(f)** Put $\beta:=-1/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$, a smooth positive function, and
$h_T:=g+\beta\,dT\otimes dT$. Then $g=-\beta\,dT\otimes dT+h_T$;
$h_T(X,\cdot)=0$; and $h_T$ restricted to $\ker dT$ is a smooth Riemannian
metric, so the decomposition $T_pM=\mathbb RX_p\oplus\ker dT_p$ is
$g$-orthogonal with $g(X,X)=-\beta$. Consequently the pullback of $g$ by the
diffeomorphism $\Psi$ has no mixed terms,
$$\Psi^*g=-(\beta\circ\Psi)\,ds^2+h,\qquad h_{(s,z)}(v,w):=g_{\Phi(s,z)}\bigl((d\Phi_s)_zv,(d\Phi_s)_zw\bigr),$$
a sum of a negative definite one-dimensional form and the smooth family of
Riemannian metrics induced on the levels.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[def-function]],
> [[def-natural-numbers]]) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** [[def-choice-function]] and
[[def-axiom-of-choice]] select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and [[def-countable-choice]] does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ ([[def-power-set]], [[def-cartesian-product]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]); a natural is the set of its predecessors ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense ([[def-chain]]). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Surjectivity is [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]]. Every smooth map from an open subset of $M$ to $U(1)$ consequently has, near each point, a smooth real phase lift obtained by composing with such a local inverse.

A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Thus the compatibility condition is independent of the chosen lift. The globally defined form $\lambda(g):=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ is real, and [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] together with [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] gives $\lambda(g)=df$ on every phase-lift neighborhood. Hence the equivalent lift-free condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The right principal $U(1)$-bundle convention is as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]: it has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts, with free and transitive action on each fibre. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. derivations.claim:
The four constraints and complete initial field-strength data are exactly
those of [F3]–[F4] with the fixed signature, SI constants, orientation, and
$K$ sign. The normalized local potential data [A2] place the magnetic
two-form in the supplied circle-bundle sector, while $e$ is independent
normal electric data. The zero-matter action choice [A1] specializes [F1]
and its field-equation interface [F2] to the source-free system [F3].

The constrained data in step 1.1 meet the exact smooth connected data
hypotheses of [F6], with precisely its Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
assumptions [F10]. Applying [F6] gives a smooth globally hyperbolic maximal
field-strength development $M_{\max}$, universal for all smooth globally
hyperbolic field-strength developments of these data and unique up to the
stated data-fixing isometry. This constructs the field-strength development;
its fixed-bundle connection realization is proved next.

The Cauchy slice $i_{\max}(\Sigma)$ in the development from step 2.1 and
its complete flow from [F9] provide the product map used in [F8]. Pull the
initial local connection data [A2] to that product and use [F7] to construct
its reference connection with curvature $\bar F$ restricting to $\beta_b$.
Since $F_{\max}$ is closed by [F3] and agrees with $\bar F$ on the initial
slice, [F8] gives a global one-form $\alpha$ with
$F_{\max}-\bar F=d\alpha$. Adding $\alpha/\kappa_0$ to the normalized local
connection forms retains their transition maps and changes the physical
curvature by $\kappa_0d(\alpha/\kappa_0)=d\alpha$, giving $F_{\max}$. Thus
the maximal field-strength development is realized in the supplied initial
bundle sector.

Let another smooth globally hyperbolic development have the same complete
data and be stationary for the adopted action. By [F2] and the zero-matter
choice [A1], it solves the source-free system [F3], so the universal
embedding from [F6] carries its metric and field strength into $M_{\max}$.
On its Cauchy product, pull back the same initial transition data; as in
step 3.1 they give a reference connection restricting to $\beta_b$. The
other solution's field is closed and has that same slice restriction, so [F8]
supplies one global exact adjustment and [F7] realizes it in the transported
initial bundle sector. By the development definition [F5], this proves
maximality within the stated smooth globally hyperbolic stationary class.

The uniqueness clause of [F6] gives exactly one data-fixing isometry
between any two maximal metric/field-strength developments. Connection
representatives need not be unique and are not additional fields in the
compared development. The definition [F5] imposes no geodesic-completeness
condition, so no such conclusion follows.

citations.quote:
Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty, smooth, oriented three-manifold without boundary. Let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b$ be smooth vector fields tangent to $\Sigma$. For data induced on an embedded spacelike slice $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$, let $n$ be its future unit normal, let $F$ be the smooth two-form of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], and define spatial covectors $\mathcal E,\mathcal B\in\Omega^1(\Sigma)$ by $\mathcal E(X):=F(X,n)$ and $\mathcal B(X):=-({\star_gF})(X,n)$ for $X\in T\Sigma$. Identify these with vector fields using the positive metric $h$: $e:=\sharp_h\mathcal E$ and $b:=\sharp_h\mathcal B$, so in any coordinates $e^i=h^{ij}\mathcal E_j$ and $b^i=h^{ij}\mathcal B_j$. Equivalently, $\mathcal E$ is the restriction of the observer electric covector $E/c$ and $\mathcal B$ the restriction of the observer magnetic covector $B$ of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. For an abstract data tuple not assumed to come from $F$, $e,b$ are simply the specified tangent vector fields. This fixes the convention without adding a potential or an existence assumption.

For the observer-covector comparison above, the smooth normal along $\Sigma$ has local smooth ambient extensions by [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]; shrinking and normalizing an extension gives an observer congruence to which [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]] applies. The restrictions $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ depend only on $n|_\Sigma$, so they are independent of the chosen extension.

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix to $h_{ij}$ and use $h$ to raise every spatial index. Let $D$ and $R(h)$ denote the Levi-Civita connection and scalar curvature of $h$, set $\tau:=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell}$, and choose the induced spatial orientation so $\operatorname{vol}_g=\theta^0\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h=-n^\flat\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h$ in a positively oriented normal coframe with $\theta^0(n)=1$. Define the spatial cross product by $h(e\times_hb,w)=\operatorname{vol}_h(e,b,w)$ for each tangent vector $w$.

For the fixed parameters $(\kappa,\Lambda,\mu_0)$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], the tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ is **constrained electrovacuum initial data** when

$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,$$

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\bigl(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2\bigr),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

Here the last display is an equality of covectors. The scalar-curvature form is the Gauss-Codazzi form of the normal projections in [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; the sign and $K$ convention are those of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness of a spacetime development.

For the periodic high-regularity class, use the dimensionless coordinate $\theta^i$ and length coordinate $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], for a fixed $L_0>0$. The arrays $h_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ are the length-coordinate covariant components with $h_{ij}\in H^{s+1}$ and $K_{ij}\in H^s$. The Sobolev components of $e,b$ are $e_A=h(e,\mathsf e_A)$ and $b_A=h(b,\mathsf e_A)$ in the canonical positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $\mathsf e_A$ specified there; thus $e_A,b_A\in H^s$. If $\mathsf e_A=E_A^i\partial_{X^i}$, their coordinate components are $e^i=E_A^i e_A$ and $b^i=E_A^i b_A$. The coefficients $E_A^i$ are smooth functions of the positive matrix $h_{ij}$; on the compact range of each such metric, [[lem-gr-smooth-composition-and-commutator-estimates]] puts them in $H^{s+1}$ and [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-algebra]] makes the coordinate components $H^s$ as well.

For these representatives define the spatial connection coefficients by $\Gamma(h)^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12h^{k\ell}(\partial_{X^i}h_{j\ell}+\partial_{X^j}h_{i\ell}-\partial_{X^\ell}h_{ij})$, with $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. On coordinate vector components put $D_i e^j=\partial_{X^i}e^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}e^k$ and $D_i b^j=\partial_{X^i}b^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}b^k$; on the covariant tensor $K$ put $D_iK_{jk}=\partial_{X^i}K_{jk}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ij}K_{\ell k}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ik}K_{j\ell}$. Define $R(h)$ by $R^a{}_{bij}=\partial_{X^i}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jb}-\partial_{X^j}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ib}+\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ic}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{jb}-\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jc}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{ib}$, followed by the Ricci and scalar contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Sobolev embedding gives $h\in C^{s-1}$ and $K,e,b\in C^{s-2}$; the uniform positive lower eigenvalue makes $h^{-1}$ well defined, and the smooth-composition and algebra suppliers give $\Gamma(h)\in H^s$, $R(h)\in H^{s-1}$, and $D K,D e,D b\in H^{s-1}$. Since $s\ge5$, these constraint terms have continuous representatives, and their displayed equalities mean pointwise equality of those representatives. In the SI interpretation, $K$ and $D$ carry one inverse-length factor, $R(h)$ and $\Lambda$ carry inverse-length squared, and the orthonormal components $e_A,b_A$ have units tesla; the factors $\kappa/\mu_0$ give matching units in the constraints. No numerical parameter values are assigned here.

Let $M$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable oriented four-manifold, and let $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ be a normalized circle-connection datum as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Use the set-sized-object and quotient convention of [[def-emg-set-size-and-class-schema]]. Then the chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal $U(1)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a global smooth real connection one-form $\omega$ on $P$. Its curvature is basic: there is a smooth closed two-form $f\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $d\omega=\pi^*f$ and $f|_{U_i}=da_i$. The local potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ satisfy $dA_i=F$, where $F=\kappa_0 f$ is global. For two connections on the same fixed bundle with the same transition functions, their local-form differences are restrictions of one global base one-form; adding a global one-form to all local representatives stays in that bundle sector.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty

Within this formulation, $c$, $G_N$, $\mu_0$, and $\Lambda$ are primitive model parameters: respectively, the time-to-length conversion parameter, the gravitational coupling parameter, the electromagnetic normalization parameter identified with vacuum permeability in the SI convention, and the coefficient of the cosmological term. $$\pi_a:=(D\varphi)_a:=\nabla_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi,$$

where $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is an arbitrary fixed coupling. Define $D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$, with the conjugate derivative using $+i\lambda A_a$, and $D_a\pi^a:=g^{ab}D_a\pi_b$. Let $\mathcal U\subset\mathbb R$ be open with $|\varphi|^2(M)\subset\mathcal U$, let $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U;\mathbb R)$, and fix $K_\varphi>0$. Define

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{\pi_a}\pi_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad S_\varphi:=-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M L_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where on a noncompact $M$ the integral is used when finite and otherwise only compactly supported action differences are used. The scalar equation, current vector, and scalar stress tensor are

$$D_a\pi^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi\pi^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\pi_a}\pi_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T_{ab}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}.$$

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad D_a\pi^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0.$$

The scalar is classical, and neither $K_\varphi$ nor $\lambda$ is tied to a Planck constant.

For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies
$$\mathcal I_M(d\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)).$$
For $n=0$ it is the finite signed sum $\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p)$. All assertions are choice-free: no partition on the entire manifold is required.

$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(y)\,dy=\int_{\mathbb R^n}h(x)\,dx.$$

Let $Q=\prod_{j<m}[a_j,b_j]$ be nondegenerate. For integrable
$f,g:Q\to\mathbb R$ and scalars $\alpha,\beta$, the function
$\alpha f+\beta g$ is integrable and its integral is

$|\int_Qf|\le\int_Q|f|$. If $a_r<c<b_r$, cutting $Q$ at the coordinate

derivations.claim: In a smooth chart, inversion of a nondegenerate $C^3$ matrix is $C^3$; the Christoffel formula therefore gives a $C^2$ connection and the curvature formula a $C^1$ tensor. Smooth coordinate changes preserve these regularities. The ordinary chain and product rules give $F,P\in C^1$, the stated continuous Euler–Lagrange expressions, and $C^1$ current and stress. Symmetry of $g^{-1}$ makes $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ real and $\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)$ symmetric; the Maxwell quadratic is also symmetric. The coordinate transformation laws follow by the chain rule, so all displayed equations compare global tensors. Commuting the continuous second partial derivatives of $A$ gives $dF=0$.

Let $K=\operatorname{supp}\omega$. Apply [F2] and multiply $\omega$ by its finitely many cutoffs. Each continuous coefficient has compact support strictly inside its chart, so zero extension is continuous and has a bounding rectangle; [F4] defines its finite integral. On a chart overlap the top-form coefficient transforms by the determinant of the smooth coordinate change. Its orientation sign converts that determinant to the absolute determinant, so [F3] gives the same signed integral in either chart. For two finite localizations $(\chi_i)$ and $(\tau_j)$, insert $\chi_i\omega=\sum_j\chi_i\tau_j\omega$ and the corresponding identity with $i,j$ exchanged. Every product has compact support in the chart intersection. Finite linearity from [F5] and the overlap identity make both sums equal to the same double sum. Thus $\mathcal I_M$ is well defined, linear and local. Empty support gives the empty sum zero.

Each action density has continuous coefficients. Configurations agreeing off a compact set have density difference supported in that set, including the curvature term, because their derivatives agree on its open complement. Step 1.2 therefore defines every stated relative action. For three mutually compactly differing configurations the density differences add on the union of their compact supports, so their relative actions add. On smooth fields the construction is precisely the same finite chart integral and the formulas in [F1]; hence it agrees with the original smooth relative action.

On the union $K$ of the three direction supports, nondegeneracy and the chosen time cone persist under a uniformly small perturbation: use finitely many chart neighborhoods of the compact set and take the minimum of their positive parameter bounds. The attained set $|\varphi|^2(K)$ is a compact subset of the open set $\mathcal U$, so uniform convergence of $|\varphi+\varepsilon\eta|^2$ keeps it inside $\mathcal U$ for small $\varepsilon$; outside $K$ nothing changes. The resulting metric is $C^3$ and the matter fields are $C^2$, with $\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$. The action densities and their parameter derivatives are continuous on compact parameter-chart rectangles. Consequently these directions are actual variations of the declared class, not only formal symbols.

A real $C^3$ function $\chi$ gives $A'=A+d\chi\in C^2$ and $\varphi'=e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi\in C^2$. The product rule gives $P'=e^{i\lambda\chi}P$ and $F'=F$, so the action density is unchanged. Pullback by a smooth orientation-preserving diffeomorphism also preserves the classical class and the density formulas. For compactly supported transformations, step 1.2 and [F3] give invariance of the relative action. These are mathematical invariances, not a physical adoption or a solution-existence theorem.

Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented four-manifold without boundary. Its smooth
structure is retained throughout. A **classical finite-regularity
trivial-potential configuration** consists of a time-oriented $C^3$
Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a global real $C^2$ one-form
$A$, and a global complex $C^2$ scalar $\varphi$. Fix
$c,G_N,\mu_0,K_\varphi>0$, $\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and
$V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U;\mathbb R)$ for an open
$\mathcal U\subset\mathbb R$ containing $|\varphi|^2(M)$. Set
$\kappa_E=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The curvature sign, length-coordinate convention
$x^0=ct$, and SI assignments are those of
[[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]]; only these formulas and
conventions are imported, not that item's smooth-field restriction.

The Levi-Civita connection and curvature here are defined by their coordinate
formulas for this $C^3$ metric. Define

$$F_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad P_a:=\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi,$$

$$\mathcal D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b,\qquad E_\varphi:=g^{ab}\mathcal D_aP_b-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,$$

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi,\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

Conjugate charged derivatives use the opposite gauge sign. All indices are
raised with $g^{-1}$. Thus $F,P$ are $C^1$, $j,T^\varphi,T^{\mathrm{EM}}$
are $C^1$, $E_\varphi$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}$ are continuous, and the
Einstein tensor $G$ is $C^1$. The **classical charged-scalar equations** are
the pointwise equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad E_\varphi=0,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}).$$

Here $dF=0$ already follows from $F=dA$ with $A\in C^2$. These are equations
for the declared classical fields; they do not assert existence, smoothness
improvement, or a weaker distributional theory.

For a continuous compactly supported real top form $\omega$, define
$\mathcal I_M(\omega)$ by a finite smooth cutoff localization near its
support and the signed Riemann integrals of the resulting chart
coefficients, extended by zero. The construction and its independence are
proved below. For a complex top form extend $\mathcal I_M$ by integrating
its real and imaginary parts separately. For a configuration
$X=(g,A,\varphi)$ put

$$\mathscr L(X):=\left[\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}(R(g)-2\Lambda)-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}L_\varphi\right]\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If $X_1=X_0$ outside a compact set, its **relative total action** is
$S(X_1;X_0):=\mathcal I_M(\mathscr L(X_1)-\mathscr L(X_0))$. The scalar
and Maxwell relative actions are defined by their respective summands. No
subtraction of divergent global integrals is intended. When the separate
global integrals are defined and finite, this agrees with their difference.

Allowed independent directions are smooth compactly supported symmetric
inverse-metric tensors $q^{ab}$, real one-forms $\alpha$, and complex scalars
$\eta$. Near zero parameter use

$$g_\varepsilon^{-1}=g^{-1}+\varepsilon q,\qquad A_\varepsilon=A+\varepsilon\alpha,\qquad\varphi_\varepsilon=\varphi+\varepsilon\eta.$$

The parameter interval is restricted to preserve signature, time orientation,
and the potential domain. Stationarity means that the derivative of the
relative total action vanishes for every such direction. These definitions
include the original smooth trivial-potential system as a subclass, with its
same action coefficients and tensors. They do not change the separate
nontrivial-circle-bundle formulation or impose an integer condition on the
real coupling $\lambda$.

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies
$$\mathcal I_M(d\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)).$$
For $n=0$ it is the finite signed sum $\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p)$. All assertions are choice-free: no partition on the entire manifold is required.
Every continuous real function on a closed nondegenerate rectangle $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge1$, is Riemann integrable.

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ and $B\subseteq\mathbb R^q$ be nondegenerate closed rectangles, and let $f:A\times B\to\mathbb R$ be Riemann integrable. Then the four lower and upper section-integral functions of [[def-sections-and-iterated-riemann-integrals]] are Riemann integrable and
$$\int_A\ell_B=\int_Au_B=\int_{A\times B}f=\int_B\ell_A=\int_Bu_A.$$

If the $B$-sections are integrable outside a content-zero set $N\subseteq A$, every bounded exceptionally completed function $h$ with $h(x)=\int_Bf_x$ for $x\notin N$ is integrable and
$$\int_{A\times B}f=\int_Ah.$$
The same assertion holds with the coordinate blocks exchanged. In particular, when every section in an order is integrable, the ordinary iterated integral in that order exists and equals the multiple integral. The theorem does not assert that every section of an integrable function is integrable.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

Let $Q=\prod_{j<m}[a_j,b_j]$ be nondegenerate. For integrable
$f,g:Q\to\mathbb R$ and scalars $\alpha,\beta$, the function
$\alpha f+\beta g$ is integrable and its integral is
$\alpha\int_Qf+\beta\int_Qg$. If $f\le g$, then
$\int_Qf\le\int_Qg$. Also $|f|$ is integrable and

values add to the integral over $Q$.

derivations.claim: Fix the compact support $K$ of the directions. Use [F2]'s finite smooth localization near $K$, independently of the variation parameter. In each chart the localized density difference and its parameter derivative are continuous on a fixed compact parameter-rectangle product: every density is a smooth algebraic expression in the nondegenerate metric, its derivatives through order two, and the matter fields through order one. The families in [F1] have the required joint derivatives. The one-variable fundamental theorem gives the difference quotient as the average of those parameter derivatives along the parameter segment. Uniform continuity on this compact product makes that quotient converge uniformly to the derivative at zero. Monotonicity and the absolute-value estimate [F6], compared with the constant $\sup_Q|f|$, give $|\int_Q f|\le\operatorname{vol}(Q)\sup_Q|f|$; this passes the limit through each finite Riemann integral. Thus the relative actions can be differentiated by differentiating their densities, even when the background global actions diverge.

Let $W$ be any compactly supported $C^1$ vector field. Write $w=\sqrt{|\det g|}$. The Christoffel formula and determinant derivative give $\Gamma^a{}_{ab}=\partial_b\log w$, hence $\nabla_aW^a\mathrm{vol}_g=\partial_a(wW^a)d^4x$ in a positive chart. For each finite cutoff $\chi_i$ in [F2], $w\chi_iW^a$ extends by zero to a $C^1$ compactly supported coefficient on a bounding rectangle. Its partial derivatives and all sections are continuous, so [F3]–[F5] integrate its coordinate divergence to zero: the opposite-face values vanish. Summing over $i$ gives the same result for $W$, because $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ and $\sum_i d\chi_i=0$ near its support. Therefore $\mathcal I_M((\nabla_aW^a)\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$ for this $C^1$ field. No smoothness approximation or unproved rough Stokes assertion is used.

Put $h_{ab}=\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$. Differentiation of $g^{ac}g_{cb}=\delta^a_b$ and of the determinant gives $\delta w=-	frac12wg_{ab}q^{ab}$. Differentiating the coordinate formula for the Christoffel symbols and collecting the terms containing $h$ gives $$\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}= rac12g^{ad}(
abla_bh_{cd}+
abla_ch_{bd}-
abla_dh_{bc}).$$ To differentiate Ricci, use $R_{ab}=\partial_c\Gamma^c{}_{ab}-\partial_b\Gamma^c{}_{ac} +\Gamma^c{}_{cd}\Gamma^d{}_{ab}-\Gamma^c{}_{bd}\Gamma^d{}_{ac}$. The differentiated quadratic terms are exactly the connection terms that complete the two derivatives to $\delta R_{ab}=
abla_c\delta\Gamma^c{}_{ab}-
abla_b\delta\Gamma^c{}_{ac}$. Metric compatibility in this coordinate connection then gives $$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a),\qquad V^a=g^{bc}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^c{}_{bc}.$$ All expressions exist classically: $g,h$ are $C^3$, $\delta\Gamma$ is $C^2$, and $V$ is a compactly supported $C^2$ vector field. Steps 1.1–1.2 therefore yield the Einstein–Hilbert first variation $c^3(16\pi G_N)^{-1}\mathcal I_M((G+\Lambda g)_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g)$.

At fixed metric, $\delta F_{ab}=\partial_a\alpha_b-\partial_b\alpha_a =2
abla_{[a}\alpha_{b]}$; torsion-freeness follows directly from symmetry of the Christoffel formula. Thus $\delta(F_{ab}F^{ab})=4F^{ab}
abla_a\alpha_b$. The $C^1$ compact vector $W^a=F^{ab}\alpha_b$ satisfies $
abla_aW^a=(
abla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b+F^{ab}
abla_a\alpha_b$. Steps 1.1–1.2 give $\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}=(\mu_0c)^{-1}\mathcal I_M((
abla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\mathrm{vol}_g)$. At fixed lower $F$, direct inverse-metric differentiation gives $\delta(F_{cd}F^{cd})=2F_{ac}F_b{}^c q^{ab}$. Combining it with $\delta w$ from step 2.1 gives $\delta_g S_{\mathrm{EM}}=-(2c)^{-1}\mathcal I_M(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g)$. This uses only $F\in C^1$ and the declared metric class.

For $\eta=\delta\varphi$, direct differentiation gives $\delta_\varphi L_\varphi=2\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\mathcal D_a\eta}P^a+V'\overline\eta\varphi)$. The product rule is $\nabla_a(\overline\eta P^a)=\overline{\mathcal D_a\eta}P^a+\overline\eta\mathcal D_aP^a$: the opposite gauge signs cancel. Its real and imaginary parts are $C^1$ compact vector fields. Integrating their divergence by step 1.2 yields $\delta_\varphi S_\varphi=(K_\varphi/c)\operatorname{Re}\mathcal I_M(\overline\eta E_\varphi\mathrm{vol}_g)$. At fixed $g,\varphi$, $\delta_A P_a=-i\lambda\varphi\alpha_a$, so $\delta_A L_\varphi=-2\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a)\alpha_a$, giving the claimed $j$. At fixed lower $A$ and fixed $\varphi$, $\delta_gL_\varphi=\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)q^{ab}$; the volume term then gives the displayed $T^\varphi$. These calculations require no derivative beyond $\varphi\in C^2$ and $A\in C^2$.

Add steps 2.1, 3.1 and 3.2. The equality $(2c)^{-1}=[c^3/(16\pi G_N)]\kappa_E$ gives exactly the total first variation in the Statement, with its three independent directions. Its coefficients are continuous; the metric coefficient is symmetric. To see that testing detects a nonzero continuous component, take a positive chart where that component has one strict sign. A nonnegative smooth bump supported inside that chart, positive on a smaller closed rectangle, has a strictly positive signed pairing with the component times $w>0$. Such a bump can be taken as $e^{-1/(r^2-|x|^2)}$ inside a coordinate ball and zero outside. The resulting integral is nonzero: on the smaller rectangle the continuous sign-adjusted coefficient has a positive lower bound $a>0$, so its integral is at least $a$ times that rectangle volume by [F6]. Cutting a containing rectangle along the smaller rectangle faces and using coordinate-slice additivity in [F6] shows the full integral is at least that positive value, since the integrand is nonnegative on the remainder. A one-form test isolates any connection component; diagonal and symmetrized off-diagonal metric tests isolate every symmetric component. Scalar tests $\eta=f$ and $\eta=if$ isolate the real and imaginary parts of $E_\varphi$. Therefore stationarity for all these tests forces all three coefficients to vanish pointwise. Conversely their pointwise vanishing makes every first variation zero. The identity $dF=0$ in [F1] supplies the remaining homogeneous equation.

The charged product rule gives $\nabla_a j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline{P_a}P^a+\overline\varphi\mathcal D_aP^a)$. The first contraction is real and $V'$ is real, giving the stated current identity. Differentiating $T^\varphi$ and using $\partial_b L_\varphi=2\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P^a}\mathcal D_bP_a)+2V'\operatorname{Re}(\overline\varphi P_b)$ gives $$\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}\left(\overline{E_\varphi}P_b+\overline{P^a}(\mathcal D_aP_b-\mathcal D_bP_a)\right).$$ The symmetric Christoffel terms cancel in the difference. Expanding $P=\partial\varphi-i\lambda A\varphi$ and commuting the continuous second scalar partial derivatives gives $\mathcal D_aP_b-\mathcal D_bP_a=-i\lambda F_{ab}\varphi$. Its contribution to the real part is $-K_\varphi\lambda F_{ab}\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a)=F_{ba}j^a$. This proves the two scalar off-shell identities using only first derivatives of $P$ and $C^2$ scalar partials.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

derivations.claim: Expanding the divergence equation and retaining only derivatives of the independent $\pi$ variables gives $g^{00}\partial_s\pi_0+g^{0i}\partial_s\pi_i+g^{i0}\partial_i\pi_0+g^{ij}\partial_i\pi_j$. Substitute $\partial_s\pi_i=\partial_i\pi_0-i\lambda A_i\pi_0-i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi$ from the compatibility equations. Since $g^{i0}=g^{0i}$, the derivative terms become $g^{00}\partial_s\pi_0+2g^{0i}\partial_i\pi_0+g^{ij}\partial_i\pi_j$; the substituted source terms contain no derivatives of $\pi$. Multiplying this row by $-1$ gives the top row of the stated principal system.

For each $k$, multiplying the $i$th compatibility equation by $g^{ki}$ gives time coefficient $g^{ki}\partial_s\pi_i$ and spatial coefficient $-g^{ki}\partial_k\pi_0$. Thus the complete $\pi$-block has exactly the displayed $A^0,A^k$. The time block is positive because $-g^{00}>0$ and $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite. Each spatial block is symmetric because $g^{ij}=g^{ji}$, including the off-diagonal entries $-g^{kj}$ and $-g^{jk}$. The same calculation applies separately to the real and imaginary parts.

The equations $\partial_s\varphi=\pi_0$ and $\partial_sA_i=F_{0i}$ contain no spatial derivatives of their evolved variables, so they append identity time blocks and zero spatial blocks. The connection terms in $D_a\pi^a$, the gauge terms, the potential term, and derivatives of the prescribed metric coefficients are zero-order terms once the first metric derivatives are included in the coupled first-order state. Smoothness of inversion on the stated metric domain and smoothness of $V$ on the attained open range make every coefficient map smooth there. By [L1] this verifies the coefficient definition, without asserting existence of a solution to the coupled system.
