its real and imaginary parts separately. For a configuration
$X=(g,A,\varphi)$ put

$$\mathscr L(X):=\left[\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}(R(g)-2\Lambda)-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}L_\varphi\right]\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If $X_1=X_0$ outside a compact set, its **relative total action** is
$S(X_1;X_0):=\mathcal I_M(\mathscr L(X_1)-\mathscr L(X_0))$. The scalar
and Maxwell relative actions are defined by their respective summands. No
subtraction of divergent global integrals is intended. When the separate
global integrals are defined and finite, this agrees with their difference.

Allowed independent directions are smooth compactly supported symmetric
inverse-metric tensors $q^{ab}$, real one-forms $\alpha$, and complex scalars
$\eta$. Near zero parameter use

$$g_\varepsilon^{-1}=g^{-1}+\varepsilon q,\qquad A_\varepsilon=A+\varepsilon\alpha,\qquad\varphi_\varepsilon=\varphi+\varepsilon\eta.$$

The parameter interval is restricted to preserve signature, time orientation,
and the potential domain. Stationarity means that the derivative of the
relative total action vanishes for every such direction. These definitions
include the original smooth trivial-potential system as a subclass, with its
same action coefficients and tensors. They do not change the separate
nontrivial-circle-bundle formulation or impose an integer condition on the
real coupling $\lambda$.
For finite $m\ge1$, open $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, compact $K\subseteq O$, $R\ge0$, and integer $s\ge5$, define the bounded admissible initial-state class

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $A^\mu,B$ ($\mu=0,1,2,3$) be a periodic symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ in the exact sense of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]: the coefficient maps are smooth, each $A^\mu$ is a real symmetric matrix, and $A^0$ is positive definite. Let $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there are $T>0$ and $C<\infty$, uniform over all $u_0\in\mathcal S_s(K,R)$ of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], such that the system

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ be a coordinate neighborhood in an oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, foliated by spacelike $s$-levels. Write
$$g=-\alpha^2ds^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i ds)(dx^j+\beta^j ds),\qquad \alpha>0,\qquad h=(h_{ij})>0,$$
and let $n=\alpha^{-1}(\partial_s-\beta^i\partial_i)$ be the future unit normal. On a smaller neighborhood choose a positively oriented orthonormal spatial frame $(\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ by Gram–Schmidt. Let $D$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$, define $\operatorname{div}_h v:=D_iv^i$ and $(\operatorname{curl}_h v)_i:=\epsilon_i{}^{jk}D_jv_k$, and define the spatial cross product by $(u\times v)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$ in this frame. For a smooth real two-form $F$, define the real spatial components $e_i:=F(\mathsf e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$, with $\epsilon_{123}=1$; thus $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$ in the adapted tetrad. Assume the source-free model of draft definition [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], whose actual equations are $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=0$; its draft status and manifest omission are recorded in [L1].

The six evolution equations for $(e,b)$ have principal part
$$n(e)-\operatorname{curl}_h b=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b),\qquad n(b)+\operatorname{curl}_h e=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b).$$
For a spatial covector $\xi$, let $C(\xi)v:=\xi^\sharp\times v$ in the oriented orthonormal frame. Set $\theta^0:=\alpha ds=-g(n,\cdot)$ and decompose any spacetime covector as $\zeta=\zeta(n)\theta^0+\zeta_\perp$, where $\zeta_\perp(n)=0$ and $|\zeta_\perp|_h$ is its spatial norm. The spatial principal block is the linear map on $\mathbb R^3\oplus\mathbb R^3$ defined by $S(\xi)(u,v)=(-C(\xi)v,C(\xi)u)$. It is real symmetric, has eigenvalues $0,0,|\xi|,|\xi|,-|\xi|,-|\xi|$, and satisfies $\|S(\xi)\|=|\xi|$. Therefore the principal symbol $P(\zeta)=\zeta(n)I_6+S(\zeta_\perp)$ is positive definite for every covector with $\zeta(n)>|\zeta_\perp|_h$. In the adapted coordinates its time matrix is $\alpha^{-1}I_6$, and every coordinate spatial matrix is symmetric. Derivatives of the frame and metric enter only as smooth lower-order coefficients depending on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,e,b)$; in a first-order metric state they are zero-order terms. The remaining two Maxwell equations are the constraints $\operatorname{div}_h e=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_h b=0$.

Let $U\subseteq I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ be a coordinate region with $x^0=s$ a length coordinate, and let $g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $U$. Write $g^{ab}$ for its inverse and $\Gamma^c{}_{ab}$ for its Levi–Civita coefficients. Assume throughout the region that

$$g^{00}<0,\qquad (g^{ij})_{i,j=1}^3\text{ is positive definite}.$$

Let $A_0=0$, let $A_i$ be real, let $F_{0i}$ be real, and let $\varphi$ be complex. Treat $\pi_0,\pi_i$ as independent complex variables, and set

$$D_a\pi_b:=\partial_a\pi_b-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\pi_c-i\lambda A_a\pi_b,$$

where $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $D_a\pi^a:=g^{ab}D_a\pi_b$. The temporal-gauge scalar first-order system is

$$\partial_s\varphi=\pi_0,\qquad \partial_sA_i=F_{0i},$$

$$\partial_s\pi_i-\partial_i\pi_0=-i\lambda A_i\pi_0-i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi,\qquad D_a\pi^a=V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi.$$

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in the periodic coefficient convention of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]. Use the three spatial compatibility equations to eliminate $\partial_s\pi_i$ from the scalar divergence equation. Then multiply the resulting scalar row by $-1$ and the compatibility rows by $g^{ki}$. For the variable block $(\pi_0,\pi_i)$, the resulting principal matrices are

$$A^0=\begin{pmatrix}-g^{00}&0\\0&g^{ij}\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^k=\begin{pmatrix}-2g^{0k}&-g^{kj}\\-g^{ik}&0\end{pmatrix}\quad(k=1,2,3).$$

The matrices on the complex variables mean the same real matrices on each real and imaginary component. They are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. The transport equations for $\varphi$ and $A_i$ add only identity time blocks and no spatial derivative blocks. All remaining coefficients depend smoothly on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,A,F,\varphi,\pi)$ wherever the stated metric inequalities and the open domain of $V$ hold. Thus this scalar-potential reduction is symmetric hyperbolic in the coefficient sense of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]].

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the imported Sobolev and finite-domain integration results. Let $\Sigma=\{s=0\}$ be a spacelike slice in a smooth time-coordinate region $U\subset I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with future unit normal $n$ and induced metric $h$. Use the global-potential system of [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] in temporal gauge $A_0=0$, including $\partial_sA_i=F_{0i}$ and the scalar first-order equations of [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]]. Treat $\pi_a$ and $F_{ab}$ as independent evolution variables. Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and $\mathcal D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$ for the charged derivatives of the model suppliers. In this item $D$ denotes only the spatial Levi-Civita derivative of $h$; thus $D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi$ on a scalar, while $\mathcal D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi-i\lambda A_i\varphi$.

Fix a smooth background metric $\bar g$ and define

$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc}\bigr)$$

as in [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Let $D$ be the Levi–Civita derivative of $h$, let $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, and put $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK$. Define the scalar and magnetic-potential residuals

$$C_i:=\pi_i-\partial_i\varphi+i\lambda A_i\varphi,\qquad B_{ij}:=F_{ij}-(\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i).$$

Assume the reduced scalar, sourced Maxwell, and harmonic-reduced Einstein evolution equations hold on $U$. The metric is in the admissible region of [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]], with $g^{00}<0$ and positive definite $(g^{ij})$. The Maxwell field-strength evolution equations are the normal contractions $\iota_n(dF)=0$ and $\iota_n(d\star_gF-\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$, with the algebraic current source added to the Maxwell block. If $\partial_s=\alpha n+\beta^i\partial_i$, their coordinate-time contractions can contain shift multiples of the all-spatial residuals; no coordinate-time residual is set to zero before those spatial constraints are recovered. Assume initially

$$C_i=0,\qquad B_{ij}=0,\qquad D_i b^i=0,\qquad D_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad H|_\Sigma=0,$$

where in a positively oriented future orthonormal frame $F_{0i}=-e_i$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$, $\epsilon_{123}=1$, and $j^0=-n_aj^a$. Assume also the total-stress Einstein constraints

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma),$$

where $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(X):=h^{ij}(D_{\partial_i}K)(\partial_j,X)$. The momentum constraint is an equality of covectors, independent of the choice of spatial coordinates or orthonormal frame.

For the metric first-order state $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$, require their initial values to equal the corresponding metric derivatives.

Then on a neighborhood of every initial point:

1. $C_i=0$ and $B_{ij}=0$ persist, so $\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi$ and $F=dA$.
2. The scalar equation gives $\nabla_a j^a=0$, and the sourced Maxwell evolution together with the two initial Gauss constraints gives $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$.
3. Before Einstein-equation recovery, $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab})=0$.
4. The metric first-order derivative variables remain derivatives of the metric, and harmonic gauge propagates; hence the reduced Einstein equation is the full Einstein equation.

These statements hold for smooth solutions. They also hold for the classical finite-regularity system of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]], with $g\in C^3$, $A,\varphi\in C^2$ and the evolved $F,\pi\in C^2$ supplied at periodic Sobolev order $s\ge5$. Smooth underlying coordinates and background are retained; smoothness of the physical fields is not inferred.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be an open set carrying a fixed smooth **background metric**
$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel
symbols in any chart are $\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the same symbol
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ denotes those of $g$. Let $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Reduced Einstein equation.** The **reduced Einstein equation** for the
pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

**(d) Einstein residual.** The **Einstein residual** of a pair $(g,T)$ is the
smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$
with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

**(e) Constraint equations.** If $g$ is defined on a neighborhood of a spacelike
hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and
$E(\mathfrak n,e_i)$ on $\Sigma$; that these are the normal and
normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

The definition introduces the objects only. The principal part of (b), its
first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction, the identity expressing $E$ through
$H$, the wave equation satisfied by $H$ and the propagation of the constraint
residuals are proved in [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]],
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]],
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] and
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1}$, its first and second
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives, $\bar g$ and the background curvature. Thus the
coefficients depend on the full second jet of the linearization metric. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix constants $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and a prescribed smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on the chart domain. Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}$. Second covariant derivatives include their derivative-slot connection. These known background-curvature terms are zeroth order in the first-order state and vanish for the flat coordinate background. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(x,u,T;\kappa,\Lambda,\bar g)\Bigr],$$
where the source is smooth in the first-order metric state and the prescribed matter data, with no derivatives of $T$, and includes $2\kappa(T_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}T_{cd})g_{ab})+2\Lambda g_{ab}$. The resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric. More generally, in a coupled reduction one may substitute a specified smooth algebraic stress map $T_{ab}=\mathcal T_{ab}(x,u,z)$, symmetric in $a,b$, where $z$ is a specified additional first-order matter state ranging in an open Euclidean set. This keeps the same metric principal matrices; symmetric hyperbolicity of the combined metric-matter system requires a separate check of the matter equations.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$ be an integer, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $k\ge4$ be an integer and let
$u,v\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $|\gamma|\le k-2$ the weak derivative $D^\gamma u$ has a
continuous representative and
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|D^\gamma u(x)|\le C_k\|u\|_{H^k},$$
with $C_k$ depending only on $k$;

**(b)** the pointwise product $uv$ of the continuous representatives lies in
$H^k$ and
$$\|uv\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|u\|_{H^k}\,\|v\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** if $\varphi\in C^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and
$w\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, then $\varphi w\in H^k$ and
$$\|\varphi w\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|\varphi\|_{C^k}\,\|w\|_{H^k}.$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables

The associated **classical charged-scalar Einstein–Maxwell system** is

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice $\mathrm{DC}$ ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix an integer $s\ge5$, constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $K_\varphi>0$, $\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and a real $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U)$ on an open $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the attained values of $|\varphi|^2$. Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and $\mathcal D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$ for the charged derivatives of the model suppliers. In this item $D$ denotes only the spatial Levi-Civita derivative of $h$; thus $D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi$ on a scalar, while $\mathcal D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi-i\lambda A_i\varphi$.

For the periodic Cauchy result let $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Prescribe a real symmetric metric $h\in H^{s+1}$ whose continuous representative satisfies $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$, a symmetric tensor $K\in H^s$, spatial vector fields $e,b\in H^s$, a global real spatial one-form $A_\Sigma\in H^s$, a complex scalar $\varphi_0\in H^{s+1}$, and an independent complex scalar normal derivative $\pi_n\in H^s$. All Sobolev spaces are real componentwise spaces with complex fields split into real and imaginary parts, as in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Let $n$ be the future unit normal and let $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ be any positively oriented $h$-orthonormal spatial frame. The associated initial two-form $F_\Sigma$ is defined invariantly by

$$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X),\qquad F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)\quad(X,Y\in T\Sigma).$$

Thus, writing $e_i=h(e,\mathfrak e_i)$ and $b_i=h(b,\mathfrak e_i)$, its frame components are $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,n)=e_i$ and $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,\mathfrak e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$, with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$. Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ and the product comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma$ near the initial slice. The harmonic-gauge vector is $H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc})$; prescribe the following initial metric jet relative to this fixed smooth background:

$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\quad g_{00}=-1,\quad g_{0i}=0,\quad \partial_0g_{ij}=2K_{ij},\quad \partial_0g_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK,\quad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}h^{k\ell}(\Gamma(h)^j{}_{k\ell}-\Gamma(\gamma)^j{}_{k\ell}).$$

$$D_i b^i=0,\qquad D_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma),$$

where $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)=h^{ij}(D_{\partial_i}K)(\partial_j,X)$, $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$, and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$. The constraint expressions are interpreted using their continuous representatives at the stated Sobolev orders. On the reduced coordinate domain require $g^{00}<0$ and the inverse spatial block $(g^{ij})$ to be positive definite. The real first-order state consists of the metric variables $(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi})$ relative to a fixed smooth background, the six Maxwell variables $(e_i,b_i)$, the three potential components $A_i$, and the real and imaginary parts of $\varphi,\pi_0,\pi_i$. Then there is $T_*>0$ and a local solution on $(-T_*,T_*)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ of the full Einstein, sourced Maxwell, and classical charged-scalar equations. Its first-order metric and matter state has the $L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ regularity of [[thm-emg-symmetric-hyperbolic-research-supplier]]; the metric satisfies $g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$ and $\partial_0g\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$, while $F,\pi,A_i\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented four-manifold without boundary. Its smooth
structure is retained throughout. A **classical finite-regularity
trivial-potential configuration** consists of a time-oriented $C^3$
Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a global real $C^2$ one-form
$A$, and a global complex $C^2$ scalar $\varphi$. Fix
$c,G_N,\mu_0,K_\varphi>0$, $\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and
$V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U;\mathbb R)$ for an open
$\mathcal U\subset\mathbb R$ containing $|\varphi|^2(M)$. Set
$\kappa_E=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The curvature sign, length-coordinate convention
$x^0=ct$, and SI assignments are those of
[[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]]; only these formulas and
conventions are imported, not that item's smooth-field restriction.

The Levi-Civita connection and curvature here are defined by their coordinate
formulas for this $C^3$ metric. Define

$$F_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad P_a:=\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi,$$

$$\mathcal D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b,\qquad E_\varphi:=g^{ab}\mathcal D_aP_b-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,$$

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi,\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

Conjugate charged derivatives use the opposite gauge sign. All indices are
raised with $g^{-1}$. Thus $F,P$ are $C^1$, $j,T^\varphi,T^{\mathrm{EM}}$
are $C^1$, $E_\varphi$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}$ are continuous, and the
Einstein tensor $G$ is $C^1$. The **classical charged-scalar equations** are
the pointwise equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad E_\varphi=0,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}).$$

Here $dF=0$ already follows from $F=dA$ with $A\in C^2$. These are equations
for the declared classical fields; they do not assert existence, smoothness
improvement, or a weaker distributional theory.

For a continuous compactly supported real top form $\omega$, define
$\mathcal I_M(\omega)$ by a finite smooth cutoff localization near its
support and the signed Riemann integrals of the resulting chart
coefficients, extended by zero. The construction and its independence are
proved below. For a complex top form extend $\mathcal I_M$ by integrating
its real and imaginary parts separately. For a configuration
$X=(g,A,\varphi)$ put

$$\mathscr L(X):=\left[\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}(R(g)-2\Lambda)-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}L_\varphi\right]\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If $X_1=X_0$ outside a compact set, its **relative total action** is
$S(X_1;X_0):=\mathcal I_M(\mathscr L(X_1)-\mathscr L(X_0))$. The scalar
and Maxwell relative actions are defined by their respective summands. No
subtraction of divergent global integrals is intended. When the separate
global integrals are defined and finite, this agrees with their difference.

Allowed independent directions are smooth compactly supported symmetric
inverse-metric tensors $q^{ab}$, real one-forms $\alpha$, and complex scalars
$\eta$. Near zero parameter use

$$g_\varepsilon^{-1}=g^{-1}+\varepsilon q,\qquad A_\varepsilon=A+\varepsilon\alpha,\qquad\varphi_\varepsilon=\varphi+\varepsilon\eta.$$

The parameter interval is restricted to preserve signature, time orientation,
and the potential domain. Stationarity means that the derivative of the
relative total action vanishes for every such direction. These definitions
include the original smooth trivial-potential system as a subclass, with its
same action coefficients and tensors. They do not change the separate
nontrivial-circle-bundle formulation or impose an integer condition on the
real coupling $\lambda$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by

> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[def-function]],
> [[def-natural-numbers]]) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** [[def-choice-function]] and
[[def-axiom-of-choice]] select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and [[def-countable-choice]] does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ ([[def-power-set]], [[def-cartesian-product]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]); a natural is the set of its predecessors ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense ([[def-chain]]). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Let $t_0\le T$, let $u,a,b:[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $u,b\ge0$, and suppose

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t b(s)u(s)\,ds.$$

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

derivations.claim:
Since $\varphi\equiv0$, every derivative of $\varphi$ is zero and
$P_a=\mathcal D_a\varphi=0$. Hence
$E_\varphi=\mathcal D_aP^a-V'(0)\varphi=0$ and
$j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a)=0$. Also
$g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2)=V(0)=0$, so the defining formula gives
$T^\varphi_{ab}=0$.

Substitution of $j=0$ and $T^\varphi=0$ into [F1] leaves exactly
$\nabla_aF^{ab}=0$, $dF=0$, and
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}$, the displayed
assumptions. Thus the zero extension solves the full classical model. For
compatible zero-scalar Cauchy data, take the local development supplied by the
evolution theorem. In its admissible coordinates, the scalar equation for
$(\varphi,\partial_0\varphi,\partial_i\varphi)$ has the positive wave time
block $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},(g^{ij}))$; the metric and potential are
given classical coefficients. The gauge terms and
$V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi$ are homogeneous in the scalar variables along this
solution, with bounded coefficient functions on a compact cylinder. Multiplying
the real and imaginary wave systems by their energy variables and integrating
by parts gives $E'\le CE$; on the torus there is no boundary, and on a local
ball choose a shrinking side speed larger than the ratio of the spatial
matrix norm to the positive time-matrix lower bound, so its side flux is
nonnegative. The initially zero scalar and covariant normal derivative, with
the charged spatial compatibility and temporal gauge, give zero ordinary
scalar Cauchy data. Hence [F2], in both time directions, gives
$\varphi=\pi=0$ in the local development. This establishes the zero branch
also for finite-Sobolev data; it uses no smooth geometric uniqueness for
nonsmooth fields. For smooth data the evolution theorem's smooth geometric
uniqueness additionally identifies this branch up to its stated isometry and

Adopt the following physical field law for this Einstein–Maxwell model. Let $M$ be a smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ as in [[def-emg-geometry-units]], let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $F\in\Omega^2(U)$ be a smooth real electromagnetic two-form, and let $j$ be a smooth four-current vector field on $U$. Using the Levi-Civita connection $\nabla^g$ of $g$, the SI constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$, and the field/current conventions of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], postulate

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

This is the selected smooth vacuum constitutive law. The first equation is the homogeneous field equation; the second is the sourced field equation with the sign fixed by $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $j=(c\rho,J)$ in a positively oriented inertial tetrad. No global potential is assumed: although $F=dA$ implies $dF=0$ when a smooth potential exists, the postulate applies to the two-form itself and does not assert that such an $A$ exists globally.

The postulate adopts one curved-spacetime continuation as a physical model assumption. The flat Minkowski and special-relativity suppliers [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] fix the inherited SI, inertial, and flat-limit conventions; they do not impose a globally flat metric on $M$ or deduce this curved field law. General-relativity sources describe covariant Maxwell formulations in their own unit and sign conventions; those treatments motivate the chosen formulation but neither mathematical structure nor source authority proves that this is nature's law. No empirical result is adopted here.

The model has no magnetic-charge term and no material excitation pair such as $D,H$. It applies only to smooth $F$ and $j$ on the stated domain; point and sheet sources, distribution-valued fields, and products of distributions require separate definitions and are outside this postulate.

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be an open set star-shaped about $p\in D$, meaning $p+t(x-p)\in D$ for every $x\in D$ and $0\le t\le1$. Let $F=\frac12F_{ab}\,dx^a\wedge dx^b$ be a smooth real closed two-form on $D$. Use Einstein summation over coordinate indices $a,b,c\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. Define

$$
A_b(x):=\int_0^1 t(x-p)^aF_{ab}(p+t(x-p))\,dt.
$$

Then $A=A_b\,dx^b$ is a smooth real one-form on $D$ and $dA=F$. More generally, if $\alpha=\alpha_a dx^a$ is a smooth closed one-form on $D$, then

$$
\chi(x):=\int_0^1(x-p)^a\alpha_a(p+t(x-p))\,dt
$$

is smooth and $d\chi=\alpha$. The first formula gives a local potential for every smooth closed two-form in a star-shaped coordinate chart; it does not assert global exactness.

citations.quote:
For $b\in\mathbb R$, let $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, $r=(x^2+y^2+z^2)^{1/2}$, and define the smooth real two-form

$$
F_b:=\frac{b}{r^3}\left(x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy\right).
$$

Give $M$ its canonical Minkowski metric

$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2,$$

of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the time orientation selected by the smooth timelike vector field $N:=\partial_{x^0}$, and the product orientation $o:=dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$. Thus $(M,g,N,o)$ is the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold required by [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its underlying product smooth structure and orientation are the standard ones on this open subset of $\mathbb R^4$.

Use the standard Euclidean inner product and norm on the spatial $\mathbb R^3$ factor in all spatial dot products and radii below.

On the locus $x^2+y^2>0$, define dimensionless polar coordinates by $x=r\sin\theta\cos\phi$, $y=r\sin\theta\sin\phi$, $z=r\cos\theta$, where $0<\theta<\pi$ and $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$. There $d\phi=(x\,dy-y\,dx)/(x^2+y^2)$; only this differential, not a global real-valued angle, is used on the north-south overlap. The displayed north and south potential formulas are interpreted on angular coordinate neighborhoods and extended across their respective axes as verified in step 2.2.

In a fixed $x^0$-slice, write $S^2:=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:|u|_2=1\}$, where $|u|_2=(u_1^2+u_2^2+u_3^2)^{1/2}$, and give it the outward orientation: its area form is $\omega_u(v,w):=\det(u,v,w)$ for tangent vectors $v,w\in T_uS^2$. This is a compact smooth sphere; compactness follows from closedness and boundedness by [[thm-heine-borel-rn]].

Let $U_N=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r+z>0\}$ and $U_S=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r-z>0\}$; these two open sets cover $M$. Then $dF_b=0$ and its flux through the unit sphere with outward orientation is $4\pi b$. If $b\ne0$, $F_b$ has no global one-form potential on $M$. On $U_N$ and $U_S$,

$$
A_N=b(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad A_S=-b(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi
$$

are smooth local potentials with $dA_N=dA_S=F_b$, and $A_S-A_N=-2b\,d\phi$ on the overlap. For a chosen normalization $\kappa_0>0$, these local forms define the normalized circle-connection data of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] precisely when the transition $g_{NS}=e^{-2ib\phi/\kappa_0}$ is single-valued, equivalently $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$. For a smooth loop $g(e^{i\phi})=e^{i\chi(\phi)}$, its winding is $[\chi(2\pi)-\chi(0)]/(2\pi)$, with both circles oriented by increasing angle. Existence of a smooth phase lift, integrality of its endpoint change, and independence of the lift are proved in the phase-lift construction below. The transition winding has sign $-2b/\kappa_0$ in the stated north-to-south convention, while $\int_{S^2}F_b/(2\pi\kappa_0)=2b/\kappa_0$. This is an exact condition for this chosen circle normalization, not a claim that every classical real flux is quantized. When $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$, the compatible two-set data also produce a smooth principal circle-bundle connection, using the actual set-size interface in [A1] and the gluing statement of [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]].

There is also a flat example with nontrivial holonomy. On $M_0=\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb R^2$ with product smooth structure, take $S^1=U(1)$ with the smooth structure defined above. Write $w\in S^1$ for the base-circle coordinate and let $\nu=-i w^{-1}dw$ be its global real angular one-form, normalized by $\int_{S^1}\nu=2\pi$. For dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$, set $A=\kappa_0 a\,\nu$. On the product bundle $P_0=M_0\times U(1)$ with projection $\pi(x,z)=x$ and right action $(x,z)\cdot\zeta=(x,z\zeta)$, use $\omega=\vartheta+a\pi^*\nu$, where $z\in U(1)$ is the fibre coordinate and $\vartheta=-i z^{-1}dz$ is its real angular form. Holonomy means the fibre multiplier of the horizontal lift around the indicated base loop; gauge trivial means gauge-equivalent to $\vartheta$ under a smooth bundle map $G_u(x,z)=(x,z u(x))$ covering the identity. Then $F=dA=0$ but holonomy around the circle is $e^{-2\pi ia}$, so this connection is gauge trivial exactly when $a\in\mathbb Z$. If $b$ and $\kappa_0$ are assigned physical units, both are measured in webers; the ratio $2b/\kappa_0$ is dimensionless. No general classification of circle bundles is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and no boundary. Write $\Omega^k(M)$ for the smooth real sections of $\Lambda^kT^*M$. The classical electromagnetic field type is a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$. In length-coordinate charts its components have SI unit tesla; its integral over an oriented smooth two-surface has unit weber. The exterior derivative is denoted $d$. A field is **closed** when $dF=0$. Closedness is a field condition, not the same condition as having a global potential.

For an open set $U\subseteq M$, a **local potential** for $F$ on $U$ is a smooth real one-form $A_U\in\Omega^1(U)$ satisfying $dA_U=F|_U$. It is a **global potential** when $U=M$. In a length-coordinate chart the components of $A_U$ have unit tesla metre. This classical real-field description chooses $F$ itself and requires no bundle or global $A$.

An **optional circle-normalized connection sector** adds the mathematical data of a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a connection, using the local-potential and circle-data conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Here $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. Concretely, supply a countable open cover $\{U_i\}$ and smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$ satisfying $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$. On overlap pieces with smooth real lifts $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$, the normalized local connection one-forms $a_i$ satisfy $a_j=a_i+df_{ij}$; in local fibre angles the convention is $\theta_j=\theta_i-f_{ij}$, so $d\theta_i+a_i$ patches. The local curvature forms $da_i$ agree. Fix an independent constant $\kappa_0>0$ with unit weber, and set $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ and $F|_{U_i}=\kappa_0da_i$. Thus $a_i$ has component unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in length coordinates, while $A_i$ has component unit tesla metre. Choosing $P$ and $\kappa_0$ is extra model data; no claim is made that every smooth closed real $F$ is the curvature of such a fixed-normalization connection.

The selected **topological sector** is the fixed pair consisting of the bundle $P$ and the normalization $\kappa_0$; its connection is data on that fixed bundle. Changing $P$ or $\kappa_0$ selects a different sector.

In a trivialization, a **gauge transformation** is a single-valued smooth map $h:U\to U(1)$; its local real lifts may differ by integer multiples of $2\pi$. A connection on a trivial bundle is **gauge trivial** when one such global map takes its normalized connection form to zero. For a closed piecewise-$C^1$ loop $\gamma$ lying in a trivialization, horizontal transport is defined by $\dot\theta=-a(\dot\gamma)$; the endpoint fibre rotation is its **holonomy**. When $a$ is one global one-form along the loop this is $\exp(-i\int_\gamma a)$. These definitions introduce no quantum state or quantum phase. The constant $\kappa_0$ is not identified with Planck's constant or a unit of electric charge.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, possibly with boundary. For $k\ge1$, $c\in C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ and $\omega\in\Omega^{k-1}(M)$, define integration over a chain by the finite linear sum of its simplex integrals. Then
$$\int_c d\omega=\int_{\partial c}\omega.$$
The zero chain has integral zero. In degree zero the boundary is zero; no degree-minus-one form is required by this statement.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real field with the SI conventions of [[def-emg-topological-sector]]. Assume the smooth branch of the adopted curved Maxwell postulate [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]] applies on $M$, with no singular source in its domain. Only its homogeneous clause $dF=0$ is used below; no Einstein equation or coupled solution is asserted.

If $U\subseteq M$ is a nonempty star-shaped coordinate domain with chart image $V\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ star-shaped about a point $p$ (that is, $p+t(x-p)\in V$ for every $x\in V$ and $0\le t\le1$), then $F|_U$ has a smooth local potential. Use a length-coordinate chart for the following formula; its coordinates have unit metre. The components can be taken to be

$$A_\nu(x)=\int_0^1 t(x-p)^\mu F_{\mu\nu}(p+t(x-p))\,dt.$$

For an explicit global example, take $M_* =\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$ with Minkowski metric $-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, and $x^0,x,y,z$ measured in metres. Let $r>0$ be spatial radius, let $\theta,\phi$ be dimensionless spherical angles, and for $b\in\mathbb R$ with unit weber set

$$F_b=b\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi.$$

For each fixed $(x^0,r)$, let $S^2_r$ have its outward orientation, let $N,S$ be its north and south poles, and set $U_N=S^2_r\setminus\{S\}$, $U_S=S^2_r\setminus\{N\}$, and $O=U_N\cap U_S$. The corresponding open patches in $M_*$ are $\widetilde U_N=\{r+z>0\}$ and $\widetilde U_S=\{r-z>0\}$, whose restrictions to each $S^2_r$ are $U_N$ and $U_S$. The angular coordinate $\phi$ is defined modulo $2\pi$ on $O$, while $d\phi$ is a global one-form there. The form $F_b$ is smooth and closed on $M_*$, with outward sphere flux $\int_{S^2_r}F_b=4\pi b$. For $b\ne0$ it has no global smooth one-form potential on $M_*$. It has local north/south potentials

$$A_N=b(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad A_S=-b(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi.$$

For the fixed circle normalization $\kappa_0>0$ of [[def-emg-topological-sector]], these patch as the stated normalized $U(1)$ connection exactly when $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$: on the overlap, $A_S-A_N=-2b\,d\phi$ and the transition is $g_{NS}(\phi)=\exp(-2ib\phi/\kappa_0)$. This integrality is a restriction of the selected connection sector; the classical real-field description permits every real $b$.

There is also a flat-connection example on the smooth base $M_0=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times S^1\times\mathbb R^2$. Write $w\in S^1\subset\mathbb C$ for the circle coordinate and $\nu=-iw^{-1}dw$ for its global angular one-form, normalized by $\int_{S^1}\nu=2\pi$. For dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$, the global one-form $A=\kappa_0a\,\nu$ has $F=dA=0$, while its normalized connection has holonomy $e^{-2\pi ia}$ around the positive circle. It is gauge trivial for integer $a$ and is not gauge trivial for noninteger $a$. On an angle chart $w=e^{i\phi}$, $\nu=d\phi$. This is a classical connection statement on a smooth base, not a claim about a quantum phase or an Einstein solution. The punctured point in the sphere example is outside the field domain; no physical magnetic monopole or quantum electric-charge quantization is asserted.

derivations.claim: For $b=\kappa_0/2$, the flux formula in [F1] gives $4\pi(\kappa_0/2)=2\pi\kappa_0$, and the transition coefficient is $2b/\kappa_0=1$, so $g_{NS}(\phi)=e^{-i\phi}$ returns to $1$ after a full $2\pi$ turn. Its degree is $-1$ for the stated north-to-south orientation, hence its absolute winding is one.

For $b=\kappa_0/(2\sqrt2)$, the normalized flux number is $2b/\kappa_0=1/\sqrt2$, which lies strictly between $0$ and $1$ and therefore is not an integer. The endpoint value $g_{NS}(2\pi)=e^{-2\pi i/\sqrt2}$ is not $g_{NS}(0)=1$, so this patch data do not define the selected circle connection; the real closed two-form itself remains admitted in the classical sector of [F1].
If $b=0$, then $F_b=0$, $A_N=A_S=0$, the transition is the constant map $1$, and the global potential $A=0$ exists. Thus the nonzero-flux obstruction in [F1] does not apply at this endpoint.

For the flat case $A=\kappa_0a\,d\phi$, substituting $a=1/2$ into [F1] gives holonomy $e^{-\pi i}=-1$, which differs from the zero connection's holonomy $1$ and is invariant under single-valued gauge transformations. At $a=1$, the holonomy is $1$ and $h(\phi)=e^{-i\phi}$ is single-valued because $h(\phi+2\pi)=h(\phi)$; its local lift changes the connection by $-d\phi$, removing $d\phi$. Therefore zero curvature need not mean gauge triviality, while this integer flat connection is gauge trivial.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TM)$ be smooth, and fix constants
$c,\mu_0>0$. Assume
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, equivalently
$d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. A finite smooth singular $k$-chain means
a finite formal real linear combination of smooth singular $k$-simplices,
with the boundary operation of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]].

For a finite smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$, define its charge by

$$Q(\Sigma):=\frac1c\int_\Sigma\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then:

**(a) Gauss charge formula.** For every such $\Sigma$,

$$Q(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_{\partial\Sigma}\star_gF.$$

Consequently, if $\partial\Sigma=0$, then $Q(\Sigma)=0$. This is the
compact-cycle neutrality constraint for a smooth everywhere-defined sourced
field.

**(b) Bounding-surface restriction.** For every finite smooth singular
three-chain $V$, the magnetic flux through its boundary vanishes:

$$\int_{\partial V}F=0.$$

The equation $dF=0$ does not imply that the flux through every closed
two-cycle is zero; this item gives a zero-flux conclusion only when the cycle
is the boundary of a finite smooth chain in the field domain. Likewise, the
electric flux formula in (a) identifies charge with flux only for a bounding
surface.

**(c) Charge balance.** If a finite smooth singular four-chain $C$ satisfies
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for three-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$Q(\Sigma_2)-Q(\Sigma_1)=-Q(B).$$

Equal charge on the two slices therefore requires zero net side flux. No
asymptotic charge or flux at infinity is asserted; noncompact limits require
separate convergence and boundary-flux hypotheses.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose geodesics
and exponential map are those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Point-normal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there is a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ such that, in the components of this chart,

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0,\qquad \partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}.$$

The construction starts from any chart around $p$ and is finite: no frame field
on $U$ and no global trivialization of $TM$ is used.

**(b) Exponential charts.** For every $p\in M$ and every $g_p$-orthonormal
basis $e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$ there is a star-shaped open neighborhood
$W\subseteq T_pM$ of $0$ on which $\exp_p$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open
$U_p\ni p$, and the chart

$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U_p\longrightarrow\mathbb R^4,$$

where $\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ is the coordinate isomorphism of the basis,
satisfies $u(p)=0$ and the same three normal-form identities at $p$ as in (a).
Moreover every geodesic through $p$ has, in the chart $u$, the form
$u(\gamma(t))=(t-t_0)\,k$ for a constant $k\in\mathbb R^4$ whenever
$\gamma(t_0)=p$, $k=\psi(\gamma'(t_0))$, and
$(t-t_0)\gamma'(t_0)\in W$. Thus the portion represented by its radial initial
vector in $W$ is a straight coordinate ray through the origin. This claim is
not made for a later portion of a geodesic that may return to $U_p$ after its
radial initial vector has left $W$. No assertion is made about the second
derivatives of the metric at $p$: the construction is first order and does not
make a neighborhood of $p$ isometric to Minkowski space.

Every symmetric bilinear form on a finite-dimensional real vector space is congruent to exactly one normal form

$$\operatorname{diag}(I_p,-I_q,0_r),\qquad p+q+r=\dim V.$$

Equivalently, the numbers of positive, negative, and zero diagonal entries are independent of the diagonalizing basis.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

derivations.claim:
By [A1], $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The sign identity in
[F1] gives $d*F=\mu_0i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$. Apply $d$ and use $d^2=0$ to get
$d(i_j\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$ since $\mu_0>0$. By the proved density-divergence
identity [F5], this is $(\nabla_aj^a)\mathrm{vol}_g=0$. The volume form is
nowhere zero, so $\nabla_aj^a=0$.

At $p$, put $W=n(p)^\perp$. Every $v\in T_pM$ has the orthogonal
decomposition $v=-g_p(v,n(p))n(p)+(v+g_p(v,n(p))n(p))$; the second term is
orthogonal to $n(p)$. The summands intersect only in zero because
$g_p(n(p),n(p))=-1$, so $T_pM=\mathbb R n(p)\oplus W$ and $\dim W=3$. The
restriction of $g_p$ to $W$ is nondegenerate: a vector in its radical is
orthogonal to both $W$ and $n(p)$, hence to all of $T_pM$, and must be zero.
The first summand has inertia $(0,1,0)$, while $g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$;
[F4] therefore gives inertia $(3,0,0)$ on $W$, so $g_p|_W$ is positive
definite. Choose a basis $w_1,w_2,w_3$ of $W$ and set
$e_1=w_1/\sqrt{g_p(w_1,w_1)}$. Set
$v_2=w_2-g_p(w_2,e_1)e_1$; linear independence gives $v_2\ne0$, and direct
substitution gives $g_p(v_2,e_1)=0$. Set $e_2=v_2/\sqrt{g_p(v_2,v_2)}$.
Next set $v_3=w_3-g_p(w_3,e_1)e_1-g_p(w_3,e_2)e_2$. Independence gives
$v_3\ne0$, and $g_p(v_3,e_1)=g_p(v_3,e_2)=0$ by orthonormality of $e_1,e_2$.
Positive definiteness makes all three denominators positive; set
$e_3=v_3/\sqrt{g_p(v_3,v_3)}$. If needed, reverse $e_3$ so
$(n(p),e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is positively oriented. This is a $g_p$-orthonormal
basis. By [F3], its exponential chart is point-normal and has time axis
$n(p)$; restrict the chart to its intersection with the open domain
$\mathcal D$. Use its component functions
$\widehat E_i=-cF_{0i}$ and

coefficient $(dF)_{123}=0$ is

$\partial_t\widehat{\mathbf B}+\nabla\times\widehat{\mathbf E}=0$.

The remaining four coefficients of $d*F=\mu_0i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ are

abla\cdot\widehat{\mathbf E}=\mu_0cho$ and

For a finite smooth spacelike chain $\Sigma$, [F2] applies to the sourced equation from step 1.1 and states
$Q(\Sigma)=c^{-1}\int_\Sigma i_j\mathrm{vol}_g=(\mu_0c)^{-1}\int_{\partial\Sigma}*F$. The coefficient and orientation are those fixed in [A1] and [F1]; no limiting surface is used.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and no boundary. Write $\Omega^k(M)$ for the smooth real sections of $\Lambda^kT^*M$. The classical electromagnetic field type is a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$. In length-coordinate charts its components have SI unit tesla; its integral over an oriented smooth two-surface has unit weber. The exterior derivative is denoted $d$. A field is **closed** when $dF=0$. Closedness is a field condition, not the same condition as having a global potential.

For an open set $U\subseteq M$, a **local potential** for $F$ on $U$ is a smooth real one-form $A_U\in\Omega^1(U)$ satisfying $dA_U=F|_U$. It is a **global potential** when $U=M$. In a length-coordinate chart the components of $A_U$ have unit tesla metre. This classical real-field description chooses $F$ itself and requires no bundle or global $A$.

An **optional circle-normalized connection sector** adds the mathematical data of a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a connection, using the local-potential and circle-data conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Here $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. Concretely, supply a countable open cover $\{U_i\}$ and smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$ satisfying $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$. On overlap pieces with smooth real lifts $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$, the normalized local connection one-forms $a_i$ satisfy $a_j=a_i+df_{ij}$; in local fibre angles the convention is $\theta_j=\theta_i-f_{ij}$, so $d\theta_i+a_i$ patches. The local curvature forms $da_i$ agree. Fix an independent constant $\kappa_0>0$ with unit weber, and set $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ and $F|_{U_i}=\kappa_0da_i$. Thus $a_i$ has component unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in length coordinates, while $A_i$ has component unit tesla metre. Choosing $P$ and $\kappa_0$ is extra model data; no claim is made that every smooth closed real $F$ is the curvature of such a fixed-normalization connection.

The selected **topological sector** is the fixed pair consisting of the bundle $P$ and the normalization $\kappa_0$; its connection is data on that fixed bundle. Changing $P$ or $\kappa_0$ selects a different sector.

In a trivialization, a **gauge transformation** is a single-valued smooth map $h:U\to U(1)$; its local real lifts may differ by integer multiples of $2\pi$. A connection on a trivial bundle is **gauge trivial** when one such global map takes its normalized connection form to zero. For a closed piecewise-$C^1$ loop $\gamma$ lying in a trivialization, horizontal transport is defined by $\dot\theta=-a(\dot\gamma)$; the endpoint fibre rotation is its **holonomy**. When $a$ is one global one-form along the loop this is $\exp(-i\int_\gamma a)$. These definitions introduce no quantum state or quantum phase. The constant $\kappa_0$ is not identified with Planck's constant or a unit of electric charge.

For $b\in\mathbb R$, let $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, $r=(x^2+y^2+z^2)^{1/2}$, and define the smooth real two-form

$$
F_b:=\frac{b}{r^3}\left(x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy\right).
$$

Give $M$ its canonical Minkowski metric

$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2,$$

of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the time orientation selected by the smooth timelike vector field $N:=\partial_{x^0}$, and the product orientation $o:=dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$. Thus $(M,g,N,o)$ is the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold required by [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its underlying product smooth structure and orientation are the standard ones on this open subset of $\mathbb R^4$.

Use the standard Euclidean inner product and norm on the spatial $\mathbb R^3$ factor in all spatial dot products and radii below.

On the locus $x^2+y^2>0$, define dimensionless polar coordinates by $x=r\sin\theta\cos\phi$, $y=r\sin\theta\sin\phi$, $z=r\cos\theta$, where $0<\theta<\pi$ and $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$. There $d\phi=(x\,dy-y\,dx)/(x^2+y^2)$; only this differential, not a global real-valued angle, is used on the north-south overlap. The displayed north and south potential formulas are interpreted on angular coordinate neighborhoods and extended across their respective axes as verified in step 2.2.

In a fixed $x^0$-slice, write $S^2:=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:|u|_2=1\}$, where $|u|_2=(u_1^2+u_2^2+u_3^2)^{1/2}$, and give it the outward orientation: its area form is $\omega_u(v,w):=\det(u,v,w)$ for tangent vectors $v,w\in T_uS^2$. This is a compact smooth sphere; compactness follows from closedness and boundedness by [[thm-heine-borel-rn]].

Let $U_N=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r+z>0\}$ and $U_S=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r-z>0\}$; these two open sets cover $M$. Then $dF_b=0$ and its flux through the unit sphere with outward orientation is $4\pi b$. If $b\ne0$, $F_b$ has no global one-form potential on $M$. On $U_N$ and $U_S$,

$$
A_N=b(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad A_S=-b(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi
$$

are smooth local potentials with $dA_N=dA_S=F_b$, and $A_S-A_N=-2b\,d\phi$ on the overlap. For a chosen normalization $\kappa_0>0$, these local forms define the normalized circle-connection data of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] precisely when the transition $g_{NS}=e^{-2ib\phi/\kappa_0}$ is single-valued, equivalently $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$. For a smooth loop $g(e^{i\phi})=e^{i\chi(\phi)}$, its winding is $[\chi(2\pi)-\chi(0)]/(2\pi)$, with both circles oriented by increasing angle. Existence of a smooth phase lift, integrality of its endpoint change, and independence of the lift are proved in the phase-lift construction below. The transition winding has sign $-2b/\kappa_0$ in the stated north-to-south convention, while $\int_{S^2}F_b/(2\pi\kappa_0)=2b/\kappa_0$. This is an exact condition for this chosen circle normalization, not a claim that every classical real flux is quantized. When $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$, the compatible two-set data also produce a smooth principal circle-bundle connection, using the actual set-size interface in [A1] and the gluing statement of [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]].

There is also a flat example with nontrivial holonomy. On $M_0=\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb R^2$ with product smooth structure, take $S^1=U(1)$ with the smooth structure defined above. Write $w\in S^1$ for the base-circle coordinate and let $\nu=-i w^{-1}dw$ be its global real angular one-form, normalized by $\int_{S^1}\nu=2\pi$. For dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$, set $A=\kappa_0 a\,\nu$. On the product bundle $P_0=M_0\times U(1)$ with projection $\pi(x,z)=x$ and right action $(x,z)\cdot\zeta=(x,z\zeta)$, use $\omega=\vartheta+a\pi^*\nu$, where $z\in U(1)$ is the fibre coordinate and $\vartheta=-i z^{-1}dz$ is its real angular form. Holonomy means the fibre multiplier of the horizontal lift around the indicated base loop; gauge trivial means gauge-equivalent to $\vartheta$ under a smooth bundle map $G_u(x,z)=(x,z u(x))$ covering the identity. Then $F=dA=0$ but holonomy around the circle is $e^{-2\pi ia}$, so this connection is gauge trivial exactly when $a\in\mathbb Z$. If $b$ and $\kappa_0$ are assigned physical units, both are measured in webers; the ratio $2b/\kappa_0$ is dimensionless. No general classification of circle bundles is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].
