citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For an oriented embedded sphere $S$ on which the integrals converge, define its geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

Use the SI quantities, coordinate convention, and primitive/derived distinction of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], and the zero-cosmological-constant geometric electrovac flux normalization of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. This definition is the model-local parameter map for the RN and KN ansatz families; it is not a claim that nature contains an object with these parameters.

Take $G_N>0$, $c>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ as the gravitational and electromagnetic constants used by this coupled model, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Let $m_*>0$ be a selected SI mass parameter in kg, $J\in\mathbb R$ a selected angular-momentum parameter in kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, $Q_e\in\mathbb R$ a selected electric charge parameter in C, and $\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$ a selected magnetic flux in Wb through an oriented sphere. These are the chosen SI inputs of this parametrization; this role is local to the solution families and is not a universal ontology for mass, angular momentum, or charge.

For the geometric flux integrals below, retain the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention explicitly stated by [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. No arbitrary-index choice principle or magnetic-charge quantization is added.

Set

$$\alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad \mathcal F:=\alpha F,$$

where $F$ is the SI electromagnetic two-form of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and $\mathcal F$ is its geometric normalization. In length coordinates $F_{ab}$ has unit T, $\mathcal F_{ab}$ has unit m$^{-1}$, and $\alpha$ has unit T$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$. For an oriented sphere $S$, write the geometric flux parameters as

$$q_e:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$

The SI electric-flux convention is $Q_e=\varepsilon_0c\int_S\star_gF$, and the magnetic quantity used here is the flux $\Phi_B=\int_S F$. Thus

$$q_e=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c}Q_e=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad q_m=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi}\Phi_B.$$

The second equality in the electric formula uses the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$. Both $q_e$ and $q_m$ have units of length; $q_m$ is a flux parameter and is not assigned a universal SI magnetic-charge convention. If one separately chooses the convention $Q_m:=\Phi_B/\mu_0$ with unit A m, then the same definition reads $q_m=\sqrt{G_N\mu_0/(4\pi c^4)}\,Q_m$; this optional relabeling adds no new physical assumption or quantization rule.

For the metric parameters, set

$$M:=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad a:=\frac{J}{m_*c},\qquad Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2.$$

Here $M$, $a$, $q_e$, and $q_m$ are derived length parameters, while $m_*$, $J$, $Q_e$, $\Phi_B$, $G_N$, $c$, and $\mu_0$ are the selected inputs of this map. The dimensionless metric coefficients use $M/r$, $a/r$, and $Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2/r^2$. Horizon radii, areas, angular velocities, and surface gravities are further derived quantities of a specified solution, not additional primitive inputs.

These parameter identifications do not establish that $M$ equals an ADM or Komar mass, or that $J$ equals an ADM or Komar angular momentum; such identifications need their own global hypotheses and proofs. They supply no empirical values for $G_N$ or $\mu_0$, no measured black-hole parameters, no global potential in a nonzero magnetic-flux sector, and no claim of charge quantization. The source treatments use differing signatures, charge normalizations, and natural or Gaussian unit conventions; the SI formulas above are fixed by the stated local conventions and are not copied without conversion.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

For the gravitational sector, take Newton's gravitational constant $G_N>0$ with unit $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ and the cosmological constant parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ as primitive parameters of the selected model; no numerical value for either is used here. The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $M$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ and the curvature convention of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Take a smooth real
two-form $F$ on $U$. For each application, fix one explicitly named smooth
classical matter-model instance
$$\mathcal M=(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m).$$
For each admitted pair $(g,F)$, $\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ is a specified set of
smooth matter-field configurations on $U$, including their field bundles and
regularity; $\mathcal E_m[g,F;\Psi]$ is the explicit system of equations and
constraints that defines the admissible configurations; and
$\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and $\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$ are specified maps from
those configurations to, respectively, smooth vector fields and smooth
symmetric covariant two-tensors on $U$. For an admissible configuration
$\Psi\in\mathcal C_m[g,F]$, set $j:=\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and
$T^m:=\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$. A consuming item must name the selected model and
state the exact field variables, equations, constraints, regularity, and
additional domain or initial-data hypotheses it uses. Those matter equations
and constraints are premises of that model instance; they are not supplied or
proved by this postulate. In particular, arbitrary independent smooth $j$ and
$T^m$ are not a matter-model instance merely because their types match.

There is also a named zero-matter instance $\mathcal M_0$: its configuration
set is the singleton $\{*\}$, it has no matter-field variables or additional
constraints, and $\mathsf J_0(*)=0$, $\mathsf T_0(*)=0$. Whenever a use sets

$$q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A,\qquad q_m(S_A(r))=0.$$

On the smooth product $\mathcal M_J:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J_r\times S^2$,

topology ([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]) and standard smooth
sphere structure with induced unit round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$
([[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]).
Orient $S^2$ by its outward unit normal: for $p\in S^2$ and

Set

$$q_e:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$

$$\Phi_\lambda(T,R,\omega)=(x^0=T/\lambda,\ r=L+\lambda R,\ \omega),\qquad (T,R,\omega)\in\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2.$$

$$g_\lambda=-\frac{R^2}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT^2+\frac{(L+\lambda R)^2}{R^2}\,dR^2+(L+\lambda R)^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_\lambda=-\frac{L}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT\wedge dR.$$

spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim: For almost every $y$, differentiate the product in the $z$ coordinate: $$\partial_z\bigl(z e^{-\beta H(z,y)}\bigr)=e^{-\beta H(z,y)}-\beta z\partial_zH(z,y)e^{-\beta H(z,y)}.$$ The absolute value of the right side is bounded by $(1+\beta|z\partial_zH|)e^{-\beta H}$, which is integrable by [A1].

Integrate this identity on $[-R,R]\times Y$. Absolute integrability and [F1] justify integrating first in $z$ and then in $y$, so $$\int_{[-R,R]\times Y}e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)-\beta\int_{[-R,R]\times Y}z\partial_zH e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)=\int_Y\bigl(R e^{-\beta H(R,y)}+R e^{-\beta H(-R,y)}\bigr)\,d\nu(y)=B_R.$$

The integrand in the first term is nonnegative and integrable, while the second integrand is absolutely integrable by [A1]. Their restrictions to $[-R,R]\times Y$ converge pointwise almost everywhere to the full integrands and are dominated by those integrable functions. Applying [F2] to both terms and using [A2] gives $Z-\beta\int z\partial_zH e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)=0$. Divide by $\beta Z>0$ to obtain the stated identity.

For finite $a<b$, integrate the same derivative over $[a,b]\times Y$. The boundary evaluation is $$\int_Y\bigl(b e^{-\beta H(b,y)}-a e^{-\beta H(a,y)}\bigr)\,d\nu(y)=Z_{[a,b]}-\beta\int_{[a,b]\times Y}z\partial_zH e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y).$$ Dividing by $\beta Z_{[a,b]}$ and rearranging yields the displayed finite-endpoint formula.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

The **Liouville density** $d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^n|/n!$ is the positive
density associated with the symplectic volume form. In each cotangent chart it
has coordinate density $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Given any finite
constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\Gamma_N$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

For a partition of the particle labels into species classes of sizes
$N_1,\ldots,N_s$, let $G:=S_{N_1}\times\cdots\times S_{N_s}$ act on
$Q_N=Q^N$ by permuting factors within each class and on $T^*Q_N$ by the
cotangent lift. In canonical coordinates each lift permutes corresponding
$q$ and $p$ coordinates, so it preserves $\omega_N$, $\Lambda_N$ and $m_N$.
Let $\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be
the orbit map, equip the orbit set with the quotient sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}:=\{B\subseteq\Gamma_N/G:\Pi_N^{-1}(B) \text{ is Borel in }\Gamma_N\},$$
and define the **quotient reference measure** by
$$\bar m_N(B):=\frac{1}{\prod_{a=1}^s N_a!}\,m_N(\Pi_N^{-1}(B)).$$
This is a measure because inverse images preserve complements and countable
disjoint unions and $m_N$ is countably additive. The stated invariance makes
it the normalized quotient pushforward. It is a measurable quotient;
no smooth quotient structure at configurations with stabilizers is asserted.
For one species the factor is $1/N!$.

The quotient factor here is mathematical counting data. A physical postulate
determines when labels are operationally indistinguishable and how the
reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.

Let $m,n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n}$ be open, and let
$F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$.  Suppose $(a,b)\in U$, $F(a,b)=0$, and the
**partial derivative in the second block**

$$D_yF(a,b):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\qquad D_yF(a,b)v:=DF(a,b)(0,v),$$

is invertible.  Put similarly $D_xF(a,b)u:=DF(a,b)(u,0)$.  Then there are open
neighbourhoods $P$ of $a$ and $Q$ of $b$, and a unique $C^1$ map
$\varphi:P\to Q$, such that

$$F(x,y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\varphi(x)\qquad((x,y)\in P\times Q).$$

After shrinking $P,Q$ if necessary, $D_yF(x,\varphi(x))$ is invertible and

$$D\varphi(x)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x))^{-1}D_xF(x,\varphi(x)).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

On a $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold, every Hamiltonian local flow
preserves the Liouville volume form $\Omega=\omega^n/n!$.

If $T$ preserves $\mu$ and $f:X\to[0,\infty]$ is measurable, then $\int f\circ T\,d\mu=\int f\,d\mu$, allowing infinity. If $f$ is integrable real or complex valued, $f\circ T$ is integrable and the same equality holds. Conversely, for a measurable self-map, equality for every measurable indicator implies measure preservation.

Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space ([[def-metric-space]]), let $A \subseteq X$ be
nonempty and let $x, y \in X$. Then

$$|d(x,A) - d(y,A)| \le d(x,y),$$

with $d(\cdot,A)$ the distance to a nonempty set ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
Thus the real-valued function $u \mapsto d(u,A)$ changes by at most $d(u,v)$
between $u$ and $v$: it is **$1$-Lipschitz**.

Let $\mathcal P$ be a pi-system on $X$ and let $\mathcal A=\sigma_X(\mathcal P)$. If finite measures $\mu$ and $
u$ on $(X,\mathcal A)$ agree on $\mathcal P$ and satisfy $\mu(X)=
u(X)$, then $\mu=
u$ on $\mathcal A$.

The total-mass equality is separate because this library's pi-system convention does not require $X\in\mathcal P$.

Assume the choice principles carried by the cited topology results:
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the Lindelof step and the Axiom of Choice for the
metrization corollary. Then every topological manifold is regular, metrizable,
and paracompact.

derivations.claim: In a canonical open phase domain $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ with $m_N=c_Ndz$, hypotheses [A1]–[A2] match the published Euclidean theorem [F2]. It yields the graph-partition measure, the coarea identity, and finite positive mass on each nonempty regular level. Multiplying both the volume measure and every shell measure by the same positive constant $c_N$ preserves the identity and leaves $P_E$ unchanged.

For a compact cotangent energy band, choose finitely many canonical charts whose smaller coordinate neighborhoods cover the band and whose closures lie inside the charts. In chart coordinates, $b(s)=e^{-1/s}$ for $s>0$ and $b(s)=0$ for $s\le0$ is smooth. For a coordinate ball of squared radius $R^2$ centered at $z_0$, $b(R^2-|z-z_0|^2)$ is a smooth bump, positive on the ball and zero outside its closure. Choose finitely many such balls whose smaller concentric balls cover the band and whose closures lie inside charts. Dividing the bumps by their positive sum near the band gives a finite partition $\sum_a\chi_a=1$ on a neighborhood of the band. This uses only a finite subcover. Refine it so that one fixed $\partial_iH$ is nonzero on each chart support. By [F3], each local level is a graph $z_i=h_a(y,E)$. The map $(y,E)\mapsto(y,h_a(y,E))$ has absolute Jacobian $|\partial_Eh_a|=|\partial_iH|^{-1}$, so [F4] and [F5] give the coarea identity for $f\chi_a$. Implicit differentiation gives $\partial_yh_a=-\partial_yH/\partial_iH$, hence $$\sqrt{1+|\nabla_yh_a|^2}=|\nabla_zH|/|\partial_iH|.$$ Thus the chart term is exactly the displayed weighted area integral. Cotangent coordinate changes have block Jacobian $$\begin{pmatrix}Dq&0\\ *&Dq^{-\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix},$$ whose determinant has absolute value one; therefore the Liouville density and the chart integrals agree on overlaps. Summing the finite partition proves the coarea identity and partition independence on the cotangent band.

The shell is a closed subset of a compact inverse band, hence compact. A finite set of graph charts with $|\nabla_zH|$ bounded away from zero gives $\mu_E(1)<\infty$. A nonempty shell contains a graph patch with a nonempty open coordinate domain and positive continuous chart density, so $\mu_E(1)>0$.

Along a Hamiltonian trajectory, $\frac{d}{dt}H(\Phi_tz)=dH(X_H)(\Phi_tz)=\omega_N(X_H,X_H)=0$; therefore the flow preserves energy. [F7] preserves the Liouville volume form. In canonical charts its density is $c_Ndz$, so form preservation makes the absolute coordinate Jacobian one; [F4] then proves measure preservation on each chart. Refine the finite source and target chart covers of the compact band into disjoint Borel pieces on which each chart representation of $\Phi_t$ applies, and sum the COV identities to obtain preservation of $m_N$ on the band. By [F7]'s integral-invariance clause, the coarea identity in step 2.1 gives, for continuous compactly supported $f$ and $q\in C_c(J)$, $$\int_Jq(E)\mu_E(f\circ\Phi_t)\,dE=\int_{\Gamma_N}q(H(z))f(\Phi_tz)\,dm_N =\int_{\Gamma_N}q(H(z))f(z)\,dm_N=\int_Jq(E)\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$

On any compact subinterval of $J$, use finitely many graph charts as in step 2.1. The derivatives $|\partial_iH|$ have a positive lower bound on their compact chart supports, and the chart domains, $f$ and $\Phi_t$ are bounded there. Thus the graph integrands have one finite integrable majorant. [F6] gives continuity of both $E\mapsto\mu_E(f\circ\Phi_t)$ and $E\mapsto\mu_E(f)$ on that subinterval. Their difference integrates to zero against every compactly supported continuous $q$ by step 3.2. If it were nonzero at one energy, continuity would give a neighborhood where it has one strict sign; a nonnegative continuous bump $q$ supported there would make the integral nonzero. Hence the two shell integrals agree for every regular $E\in J$.

Fix a closed subset $F$ of a shell. In the compatible band metric from [F9], $F$ is closed and the shell is compactly contained in the band interior. Choose $\delta>0$ so the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of the shell lies in the band, and let $\eta(z)=\max(0,1-\mathrm{dist}(z,\Sigma_E)/\delta)$. It is a continuous cutoff equal to one on the shell and supported in the band. The functions $g_k(z)=\eta(z)\max(0,1-k\,\mathrm{dist}(z,F))$ converge pointwise on the shell to $\mathbf1_F$ and are bounded by one. Apply the equality proved in step 4.1 to each $g_k$, then [F6] for the finite shell measures gives equality of $\mu_E$ and its flow pushforward on every closed subset. Both measures have the same finite total mass by step 3.1; closed sets form a generating $\pi$-system. Apply [F8] and divide by $\mu_E(1)>0$ from step 3.1. Thus $P_E$ is invariant for every such regular energy.

The diagonal chart map $F$ has absolute Jacobian $\prod_j\ell_jp_{0j}=A^n$, so [F4] transforms $c_Ndq\,dp$ into $\widehat c_NdQ\,dP$. Applying the graph substitution of step 2.1 in the new coordinates gives its displayed formula with $\widetilde H$ and $\widehat c_N$; changing charts back by [F4] gives exactly the same localized shell integrals. Direct substitution in $\lambda=\sum_jp_jdq^j$ and $\omega_N=\sum_jdq^j\wedge dp_j$ proves the two pullback formulas. The canonical equations $\dot q^j=\partial_{p_j}H$, $\dot p_j=-\partial_{q^j}H$ follow by contracting $X_H$ into that form. Since $\partial_{P_j}\widetilde H=p_{0j}\partial_{p_j}H$ and $\partial_{Q^j}\widetilde H=\ell_j\partial_{q^j}H$, division of the two velocity components by $\ell_j$ and $p_{0j}$ proves the stated $A^{-1}$ factors in the unchanged parameter $t$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\exp(x):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{\iota(n!)}, \qquad e:=\exp(1),$$
provided by the all-real convergence proved in [[lem-exponential-series-has-infinite-radius]]. Here $n!\in\mathbb N$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], $\iota(n!)$ is its nonzero real image ([[def-canonical-natural]], [[lem-of-naturals-positive]]), and powers and series are those of [[def-integer-power]] and [[def-series]].

This is a real power series centred at $0$ ([[def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence]]). No logarithm, irrational power, or differential equation enters the definition.

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

For every real $x$, $\exp(x)>0$ and
$$\exp(-x)=\frac1{\exp(x)}.$$

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

Let $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N,m_N)$ be a sigma-finite phase-reference measure
space from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; the cotangent construction uses
the stated Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). A **statistical state** is a probability measure
$P$ on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$, meaning a countably additive measure with
$P(\Gamma_N)=1$ ([[def-measure]]). A **density** of $P$ relative to $m_N$ is a
measurable $\rho:\Gamma_N\to[0,\infty]$ such that
$$P(A)=\int_A\rho\,dm_N\quad(A\in\mathcal F_N),\qquad \int_{\Gamma_N}\rho\,dm_N=1.$$
Equivalently, $P=\rho\,m_N$ in the definition of a measure with density
([[def-measure-with-density]]); integration against that density has the
meaning supplied by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]]. A state need not
have a density.

An **observable** is a real-valued measurable function
$A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]).
Its expectation $\langle A\rangle_P:=\int A\,dP$ is used only when $A$ is
integrable, that is, $\int|A|\,dP<\infty$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Its
variance is
$$\operatorname{Var}_P(A):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)^2\,dP$$
when $A^2$ is integrable. For square-integrable $A,B$, their covariance is
$$\operatorname{Cov}_P(A,B):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)(B-\langle B\rangle_P)\,dP.$$
These expressions are finite under the stated square-integrability
hypotheses. Indeed, $P(\Gamma_N)=1$ makes $1\in L^2(P)$ with norm $1$.
By [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]],
$\int|A|\,dP\le(\int A^2\,dP)^{1/2}$, so the mean of a square-integrable
observable exists. If $a=\langle A\rangle_P$, then
$|A-a|^2\le2A^2+2a^2$ makes $A-a$ square-integrable; the same argument
applies to $B-b$. A second application of that inequality gives
$\int|(A-a)(B-b)|\,dP\le\|A-a\|_2\|B-b\|_2<\infty$.
Thus both the variance and covariance integrals above are well-defined.

If $P=\rho m_N$ and the integrals are defined, these expectations equal
$\int A\rho\,dm_N$ by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]].

A **macrostate map** is a measurable map
$M:(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)\to(Y,\mathcal G)$. Its induced state on $Y$ is
the pushforward $M_*P(B):=P(M^{-1}(B))$. The measure of a macrocell and an
entropy assigned to that macrostate are additional constructions; they are
not identical to the expectation or variance of a microscopic observable.

derivations.claim: For each fixed $\theta\in\Theta$, choose a compact neighborhood $K$ of $\theta$. The bound in [A1] implies $\int we^{\theta\cdot X}dm<\infty$. On $\{w>0\}$ the integrand is strictly positive by [F3]; since this set is the countable union of the sets $\{we^{\theta\cdot X}\ge1/k\}$, at least one has positive measure. Hence $Z(\theta)>0$ as well as finite.

For coordinate $a$, choose a compact neighborhood $K$ of $\theta$ containing every $\theta+se_a$ with $|s|\le\epsilon$. The mean-value theorem and chain rule [F2] bound the difference quotient by $w|X_a|\sup_{|s|\le\epsilon}e^{(\theta+se_a)\cdot X}$. Since $|X_a|\le1+\sum_c|X_c|^2$, [A1] bounds this entire supremum pointwise by the single integrable $G_K$. Thus [F1] gives $\partial_aZ=\int wX_ae^{\theta\cdot X}dm$. Applying the same argument to the first derivative, with $|X_aX_b|\le(|X_a|^2+|X_b|^2)/2$, gives $\partial_b\partial_aZ=\int wX_aX_be^{\theta\cdot X}dm$. The same local envelopes and [F1] give continuity of these derivatives, hence $Z\in C^2$.

By [F3], dividing the first-derivative formula by $Z>0$ gives $\partial_a\log Z=\langle X_a\rangle_\theta$. Differentiating once more yields $$\partial_b\partial_a\log Z=\frac{\int X_aX_bwe^{\theta\cdot X}dm}{Z} -\frac{\int X_awe^{\theta\cdot X}dm\int X_bwe^{\theta\cdot X}dm}{Z^2} =\langle X_aX_b\rangle-\langle X_a\rangle\langle X_b\rangle.$$ This is the covariance in [F4]. For $v\in\mathbb R^r$ its quadratic form is $\langle(v\cdot(X-\langle X\rangle))^2\rangle\ge0$, proving positive semidefiniteness.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ be a cotangent phase space
from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]], with $\dim Q_N=n$, and let $J\subseteq
\mathbb R$ be open. Let $H\in C^2(\Gamma_N,\mathbb R)$ satisfy
$dH\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and suppose $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact for every compact
$K\subset J$. Use the real canonical cotangent coordinates
$z=(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ of
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; this mathematical theorem assigns no
physical units to these coordinates.

For a compact regular energy band, take a finite smooth partition of unity
$\{\chi_a\}$ subordinate to canonical cotangent charts. In a chart where
$\partial_iH\ne0$, write the local energy graph as $z_i=h_a(y,E)$ and define
the **weighted shell measure** on nonnegative Borel $f$ by
$$\mu_E(f):=c_N\sum_a\int f(y,h_a(y,E))\chi_a(y,h_a(y,E))|\partial_iH(y,h_a(y,E))|^{-1}\,dy,$$
where $c_N>0$ is the constant density of the reference measure in canonical
coordinates. Then this definition is independent of the chosen finite chart
partition and equals the chart expression
$$\mu_E(f)=c_N\int_{\Sigma_E}f(z)|\nabla_zH(z)|^{-1}\,dA_z,$$
with $\Sigma_E:=H^{-1}(\{E\})$ and Euclidean area in each real
canonical chart. For every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in
$H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_{\Gamma_N}f\,dm_N=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
If $\Sigma_E$ is nonempty, then $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$ and
$P_E:=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. If a Hamiltonian flow map is a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band and preserves that band,
then $P_E$ is invariant under that map for every such regular $E$. Critical
levels and noncompact inverse bands are outside this statement. For its
invariance clause, fix a compatible metric on a compact band whose interior
contains the shell; such a metric exists by
[[thm-topological-manifolds-are-metrizable-and-paracompact]].

The same shell measure can be computed after a fixed numerical coordinate
normalization. Choose positive real scales $\ell_j,p_{0j}$ with a common
product $\ell_jp_{0j}=A>0$, and put
$$q^j=\ell_jQ^j,\qquad p_j=p_{0j}P_j,\qquad F(Q,P)=(q,p),\qquad \widetilde H=H\circ F.$$
The reference density becomes $\widehat c_N\,dQ\,dP$ with
$\widehat c_N=c_NA^n$. The graph and weighted-area formulas above then use
$\widetilde H$, its gradient and Euclidean area in $(Q,P)$, and
$\widehat c_N$, with the same energy variable $E$. They describe the
pullback of $\mu_E$, not a different shell law. The pulled-back forms are
$$F^*\lambda=A\sum_jP_j\,dQ^j,\qquad F^*\omega_N=A\sum_jdQ^j\wedge dP_j.$$
For a Hamiltonian trajectory parameterized by its original $t$, the equations
in these coordinates are
$$\frac{dQ^j}{dt}=A^{-1}\partial_{P_j}\widetilde H,\qquad \frac{dP_j}{dt}=-A^{-1}\partial_{Q^j}\widetilde H.$$
This chart normalization does not rescale $H$, $E$ or $t$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of

base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its

same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many

covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints

preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover

supplier.

no physical unit to it.

reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure

space from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; the cotangent construction uses

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

derivations.claim: For $x>0$, set $h(x)=x-1-\log x$. By [F1], $h'(x)=1-1/x$, which is negative for $0<x<1$ and positive for $x>1$; hence $h(x)\ge h(1)=0$, with equality only at $x=1$. On $\{p>0\}$ put $x=q/p$ to obtain $p\log(p/q)\ge p-q$. The negative part of the left integrand is integrable: where $q>p$, writing $x=q/p>1$ gives $p\log(q/p)=q(\log x)/x\le q$, since $h(x)\ge0$ implies $\log x\le x-1$ and $(x-1)/x\le1$. Therefore its integral is well-defined as an extended real number, and $$D(p\Vert q)\ge\int_{\{p>0\}}(p-q)\,dm =1-\int_{\{p>0\}}q\,dm\ge0.$$

If $D=0$, both nonnegative gaps in the last inequalities vanish: $q$ has no mass on $\{p=0\}$, and $h(q/p)=0$ $p$-almost everywhere. The strict equality case in step 1.1 gives $q=p$ on $\{p>0\}$, hence $p=q$ almost everywhere. Conversely, if $p=q$ almost everywhere then the defining integrand is zero and $D=0$.

In the Gibbs case, [F2] and [A2] give $\log q=-\beta H-\log Z$ $p$-almost everywhere, so all terms below are integrable and $$D(p\Vert q)=\int p\log p\,dm+\beta\langle H\rangle_p+\log Z =\beta\left(\langle H\rangle_p+\beta^{-1}\int p\log p\,dm-F\right).$$ Since $S[p]=-k\int p\log p\,dm$ and $\beta^{-1}=kT$, the middle term is $-TS[p]$. Nonnegativity and the equality condition follow from steps 1.1 and 2.1.

For a fixed $N$, controls $\lambda$, measurable classical Hamiltonian
$H_{N,\lambda}:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ and the declared
physical reference measure $m_N^{\rm phys}$ of
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], choose $T>0$ and
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in J$^{-1}$ using the SI temperature convention of
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. If
$$0<Z_N(\beta,\lambda):=\int_{\Gamma_N}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}<\infty,$$
adopt the canonical state with density
$$\rho_{\beta,\lambda}=Z_N(\beta,\lambda)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}$$
relative to $m_N^{\rm phys}$. Set $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. Normalizability
is a required condition on the chosen model; bounded-below energy alone does
not imply it. This probability law is an adopted preparation, not a
consequence of deterministic mechanics or evidence of laboratory
equilibration.

For a declared classical model with $N_a$ operationally indistinguishable
particles of each species $a$, label those particles by
$\{(a,i):1\le i\le N_a\}$ on the auxiliary labelled cover, and let
$S_{N_a}$ denote the permutation group of that species' finite label set.
The product group $G=\prod_a S_{N_a}$ acts on the labelled phase space
$\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ by the cotangent lifts of within-species permutations. Let
$\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be its measurable orbit map from
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. Choose $a_0>0$ as a fixed primitive
reference parameter with action units J s; [[def-cm01-units]] supplies its
dimension, not its value or the choice of this parameter. Here $d$ is the
number of spatial dimensions and $N=\sum_aN_a$. No numerical value or
identification of $a_0$ with Planck's constant is imposed.

Use the weighted labelled lift
$$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,d\Lambda_N =\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,dq\,dp$$
on $\Gamma_N$, where $d\Lambda_N$ is the Liouville density and the last
expression is its coordinate density in canonical charts, with coordinates
read in SI numerical units. The coordinate volume $dq\,dp$ has action
dimension $(\mathrm{J\,s})^{dN}$, so the reference is dimensionless. The
physical quotient reference is
$$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(B):=m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(\Pi_N^{-1}(B))\qquad(B\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}).$$
Thus $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on the labelled cover $\Gamma_N$, and
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}=(\Pi_N)_*m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on
$\Gamma_N/G$; with $c_N=a_0^{-dN}$, the latter is exactly the normalized
quotient reference of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]].

Physical observables for indistinguishable particles are measurable
$G$-invariant functions $A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$, equivalently measurable
functions $\bar A$ on the quotient with $A=\bar A\circ\Pi_N$. For every such
observable with an integrable expectation, its integral against
$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ equals the quotient integral against
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$. A labelled density represents a physical state on
the quotient only if it is invariant under $G$ almost everywhere with respect
to $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$; an invariant representative may then be used. In
particular, an indistinguishable-particle Hamiltonian must be invariant under
these permutations (or agree almost everywhere with its permuted versions
when only its Gibbs density is at issue). A label-specific coordinate
statistic on the lift is not itself a quotient observable. Under a
permutation-invariant state its marginal law
can instead be interpreted as the law of a uniformly selected particle within
the same species, or of a uniformly selected coordinate of the same type
within that species. Symmetric sums and averages within each species are
quotient observables.
Calculations of labelled momentum components in
[[pthm-csm-canonical-momentum-equipartition]] use this symmetric labelled
lift, and their permutation-invariant kinetic sums and averages are physical
observables.

If labels are operationally distinguishable, omit the corresponding
permutation factor and use the labelled phase space directly. The convention
is part of the preparation and reference model; it is not deduced from
Hamiltonian mechanics. Whether a quantity is represented by a gauge-dependent
canonical momentum or by a gauge-invariant mechanical momentum is fixed by the
stated model and gauge convention. No quantum exchange law, actual preparation
mechanism, or empirical indistinguishability test is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

The **Liouville density** $d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^n|/n!$ is the positive
density associated with the symplectic volume form. In each cotangent chart it
has coordinate density $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Given any finite
constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on the Borel sigma-algebra of $\Gamma_N$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

For a partition of the particle labels into species classes of sizes
$N_1,\ldots,N_s$, let $G:=S_{N_1}\times\cdots\times S_{N_s}$ act on
$Q_N=Q^N$ by permuting factors within each class and on $T^*Q_N$ by the
cotangent lift. In canonical coordinates each lift permutes corresponding
$q$ and $p$ coordinates, so it preserves $\omega_N$, $\Lambda_N$ and $m_N$.
Let $\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be
the orbit map, equip the orbit set with the quotient sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}:=\{B\subseteq\Gamma_N/G:\Pi_N^{-1}(B) \text{ is Borel in }\Gamma_N\},$$

$$\bar m_N(B):=\frac{1}{\prod_{a=1}^s N_a!}\,m_N(\Pi_N^{-1}(B)).$$
This is a measure because inverse images preserve complements and countable
disjoint unions and $m_N$ is countably additive. The stated invariance makes
it the normalized quotient pushforward. It is a measurable quotient;

For one species the factor is $1/N!$.

determines when labels are operationally indistinguishable and how the
reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

The product group $G=\prod_a S_{N_a}$ acts on the labelled phase space
$\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ by the cotangent lifts of within-species permutations. Let
$\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be its measurable orbit map from
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. Choose $a_0>0$ as a fixed primitive
reference parameter with action units J s; [[def-cm01-units]] supplies its
dimension, not its value or the choice of this parameter. Here $d$ is the
number of spatial dimensions and $N=\sum_aN_a$. No numerical value or
identification of $a_0$ with Planck's constant is imposed.

Use the weighted labelled lift
$$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,d\Lambda_N =\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,dq\,dp$$
on $\Gamma_N$, where $d\Lambda_N$ is the Liouville density and the last
expression is its coordinate density in canonical charts, with coordinates
read in SI numerical units. The coordinate volume $dq\,dp$ has action
dimension $(\mathrm{J\,s})^{dN}$, so the reference is dimensionless. The
physical quotient reference is
$$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(B):=m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(\Pi_N^{-1}(B))\qquad(B\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}).$$
Thus $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on the labelled cover $\Gamma_N$, and
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}=(\Pi_N)_*m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on
$\Gamma_N/G$; with $c_N=a_0^{-dN}$, the latter is exactly the normalized
quotient reference of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]].

Physical observables for indistinguishable particles are measurable
$G$-invariant functions $A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$, equivalently measurable
functions $\bar A$ on the quotient with $A=\bar A\circ\Pi_N$. For every such
observable with an integrable expectation, its integral against
$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ equals the quotient integral against
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$. A labelled density represents a physical state on
the quotient only if it is invariant under $G$ almost everywhere with respect
to $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$; an invariant representative may then be used. In
particular, an indistinguishable-particle Hamiltonian must be invariant under
these permutations (or agree almost everywhere with its permuted versions
when only its Gibbs density is at issue). A label-specific coordinate
statistic on the lift is not itself a quotient observable. Under a
permutation-invariant state its marginal law
can instead be interpreted as the law of a uniformly selected particle within
the same species, or of a uniformly selected coordinate of the same type
within that species. Symmetric sums and averages within each species are
quotient observables.
Calculations of labelled momentum components in
[[pthm-csm-canonical-momentum-equipartition]] use this symmetric labelled
lift, and their permutation-invariant kinetic sums and averages are physical
observables.

If labels are operationally distinguishable, omit the corresponding
permutation factor and use the labelled phase space directly. The convention
is part of the preparation and reference model; it is not deduced from
Hamiltonian mechanics. Whether a quantity is represented by a gauge-dependent
canonical momentum or by a gauge-invariant mechanical momentum is fixed by the
stated model and gauge convention. No quantum exchange law, actual preparation
mechanism, or empirical indistinguishability test is asserted.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$ for the three independent *dimension symbols* of length, duration and mass. A **dimension** is an element of the free abelian group generated by $\ell,\tau,\mu$, that is, a triple $(a,b,c)\in\mathbb Z^3$ written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}$; **products and inverses** of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, so that $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\cdot\ell^{a'}\tau^{b'}\mu^{c'}=\ell^{a+a'}\tau^{b+b'}\mu^{c+c'}$ and $(\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c})^{-1}=\ell^{-a}\tau^{-b}\mu^{-c}$. The **dimensionless** dimension is $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}$, abbreviated $1$.

**(b) The dimension map.** The conventions assign to the quantities of the framework a **dimension** $[X]$, subject to the rules

$$[XY]=[X][Y],\qquad [X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1},\qquad \left[\frac{dX}{du}\right]=[X][u]^{-1},$$

and to the requirement that a sum $X+Y$ is meaningful only when $[X]=[Y]$, in which case $[X+Y]=[X]$. The third rule applies to a differentiable dependence of a quantity $X$ on a quantity $u$ and covers iterated differentiation, so that $[d^{2}X/du^{2}]=[X][u]^{-2}$. The assignment is part of the conventions: the rules above are consistency requirements on it, not physical laws and not theorems.

**(c) Reference units.** The **metre** is the reference unit of length, the **second** the reference unit of duration and the **kilogram** the reference unit of mass. A quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\,\mathrm s^{b}\,\mathrm{kg}^{c}$: its value is a real multiple of that unit, and the conventions fix how the numerical value of a quantity is read (a coordinate value alone is a real number, and the unit declaration attaches its dimension). The coordinates of an adapted chart of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]] are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinate components $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; the slice distance $d_{g}$ of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]] between simultaneous events is read in metres.

**(d) Typed quantity conventions.** The following constructions specify the quantities whose dimensions are recorded here, without adopting their dynamics. Fix a positive integer $N$, a nondegenerate open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with time parameter $t$ in seconds, position curves $x_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ with components in metres, and constant parameters $m_i>0$ in kilograms, for $1\le i\le N$. Derivatives and integrals have the meanings of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. These are conditional numerical constructions in a fixed spatial coordinate system; whether they represent a particular system is a separate model assumption.

1. **Velocity and acceleration** are the maps $w_i=x_i':I\to\mathbb R^3$ and $a_i=x_i'':I\to\mathbb R^3$, of dimensions $\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $\ell\tau^{-2}$ componentwise.
2. The **mass operator** is the linear map $\mathsf M:(\mathbb R^3)^N\to(\mathbb R^3)^N$, $\mathsf M(z_1,\ldots,z_N)=(m_1z_1,\ldots,m_Nz_N)$, with dimension $\mu$; the **momentum** of label $i$ is $p_i=m_iw_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$, with component dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$.
3. A **force input** is a specified map $F:I\times O\times\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$, where $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ is open, its arguments are time, positions and velocities, and each output component has dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$. No regularity or equation equating $F$ with $\mathsf M x''$ is adopted here. A later model must state both if needed.
4. For a specified scalar **potential energy** map $U:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ of dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$ and a tuple $x(t)\in O$, the **kinetic energy** is $T(t)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^N m_i\sum_{j=1}^3(w_i(t))_j^2$, and the **mechanical energy** is $E(t)=T(t)+U(t,x(t))$. Both are real-valued and have dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$; no conservation or applicability to every interaction is asserted.
5. Given a scalar map $L:I\times O\times\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R$ of the energy dimension and $t_0<t_1$ in $I$, assume $t\mapsto L(t,x(t),w(t))$ is integrable on $[t_0,t_1]$. Its **action on this curve segment** is the real number $S[x;t_0,t_1]=\int_{t_0}^{t_1}L(t,x(t),w(t))\,dt$, with dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$ (the integration convention multiplies the integrand's dimension by duration). No variational principle is imposed.
6. Relative to the chosen spatial origin, define the **angular momentum** $J_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ by $J_i(t)=x_i(t)\times p_i(t)$, where for $r,s\in\mathbb R^3$ the operation is explicitly $r\times s=(r_2s_3-r_3s_2,r_3s_1-r_1s_3,r_1s_2-r_2s_1)$. Its components have dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the chosen coordinates; dimensions alone assert no transformation or conservation law.
7. A **rotation matrix** here means a real $3\times3$ matrix $R$ satisfying $R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3$ and $\det R=1$; its entries are dimensionless. A radian angle is an arc length divided by its positive radius, hence dimensionless. A generalized coordinate means a component of a specified local coordinate chart on a configuration space; each such component has its own declared dimension, and only quantities of equal dimension are added.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any constant or parameter of a model is fixed by this item: in particular no mass, length or duration of any concrete system is asserted, and no measured value is recorded. Two numerical values that are equal but carry different dimensions are not thereby the same quantity. Where a treatment or a later item suppresses a dimensionful constant by a natural-unit convention, that convention is read as shorthand for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored, and it changes no dimension fixed here.

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

If $f,g\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$, then

$$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_2\|g\|_2.$$

Equality holds if and only if at least one of $f,g$ is zero almost everywhere,
or there is a constant $c>0$ with

$$|f|^2=c\,|g|^2\qquad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.$$

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Write $\beta_n$ for the restriction of $\lambda_n$ to
the Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Then $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is exactly the
completion domain of $(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n), \beta_n)$
([[def-completion-of-a-measure-space]]), and $\lambda_n$ is the completed measure
there. Explicitly,

$$E \in \mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n) \iff E = A\cup N \text{ for some } A, Z \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^n) \text{ with } N \subseteq Z \text{ and } \beta_n(Z) = 0,$$

and then $\lambda_n(E) = \beta_n(A)$.

derivations.claim: Since $C_N$ is compact, it is Borel. Fix $M>0$ with $|U_C|\le M$. Approximate $U_C$ on $C_N$ by its dyadic step functions, whose errors are at most $2^{-k}$. By [F6] and Countable Choice, replace their countably many Lebesgue-measurable level sets by Borel sets agreeing outside a common Borel null set $Z$. Clip the resulting Borel step functions to $[-M,M]$; their pointwise limsup is a bounded Borel function $V$ equal to $U_C$ off $Z$. Measurability of this limsup follows from countable unions and intersections of its level sets. Set $$\widetilde U_C(q):=\frac1{N!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_N}V(\sigma q).$$ The finite average is Borel, bounded and exactly permutation-invariant. Since $U_C$ is invariant, the average equals it outside the Borel null set $\bigcup_\sigma\sigma^{-1}Z$; these coordinate permutations preserve Lebesgue measure by [F3]. Extend by $+\infty$ off the Borel set $C_N$. The resulting $H$ is Borel on the phase space. The exceptional configuration set times $\mathbb R^n$ is null: intersect the momentum factor with each bounded integer box, apply [F2], then take the countable union. Hence the Borel density and the completed-Lebesgue density formed from $U_C$ agree almost everywhere and give the same probability on the completed phase-reference sigma-algebra. The same argument compares any two representatives.

Factor $e^{-\beta H}=e^{-\beta U(q)}\prod_j e^{-\beta p_j^2/(2m)}$ on $C_N\times\mathbb R^n$; it is zero outside this region. By [F1]–[F2], $$Z=\frac{1}{N!a_0^n}\left(\int_{C_N}e^{-\beta U_C(q)}dq\right) \left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{n/2}.$$ Boundedness of $U_C$, positive finite configuration volume, and positive finite Gaussian factors imply $0<Z<\infty$, so the adopted preparation is normalized.

The factorized density makes the momentum marginal the product of densities proportional to $e^{-\beta p_j^2/(2m)}$, independent of $q$. Set $a=\beta/(2m)$ and integrate $\frac{d}{dp}(p e^{-ap^2})=e^{-ap^2}-2ap^2e^{-ap^2}$ over $\mathbb R$; the boundary term vanishes since $p e^{-ap^2}\to0$ at both ends. Dividing by the positive Gaussian integral gives $\langle p_j^2\rangle=1/(2a)=m/\beta$. Applying [F5] to $p_j$ and $1$ under the normalized marginal gives $\langle|p_j|\rangle\le\langle p_j^2\rangle^{1/2}<\infty$; since the density is even its centered mean is zero. The product form proves independence. Summing the $n$ quadratic contributions proves both equipartition identities.

For a fixed $N$, controls $\lambda$, measurable classical Hamiltonian
$H_{N,\lambda}:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ and the declared
physical reference measure $m_N^{\rm phys}$ of
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], choose $T>0$ and
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in J$^{-1}$ using the SI temperature convention of
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. If
$$0<Z_N(\beta,\lambda):=\int_{\Gamma_N}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}<\infty,$$
adopt the canonical state with density
$$\rho_{\beta,\lambda}=Z_N(\beta,\lambda)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}$$
relative to $m_N^{\rm phys}$. Set $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. Normalizability
is a required condition on the chosen model; bounded-below energy alone does
not imply it. This probability law is an adopted preparation, not a
consequence of deterministic mechanics or evidence of laboratory
equilibration.

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,m)$ be a sigma-finite measure space, let $w\ge0$ be
measurable with $m(\{w>0\})>0$, let $r\ge1$ and let
$X=(X_1,\ldots,X_r):\Omega\to\mathbb R^r$ be measurable and finite, and let
$\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be open. For
each compact $K\subset\Theta$, assume an integrable $G_K$ satisfies
$$w(x)e^{\theta\cdot X(x)}\left(1+\sum_a|X_a(x)|^2\right)\le G_K(x)\quad(\theta\in K).$$
Then $Z(\theta)=\int w e^{\theta\cdot X}\,dm$ is finite, strictly positive
and $C^2$, and the probability density $\rho_\theta=Z(\theta)^{-1}we^{\theta\cdot X}$
satisfies
$$\partial_a\log Z=\langle X_a\rangle_\theta,\qquad \partial_a\partial_b\log Z=\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X_a,X_b).$$
In particular, the Hessian of $\log Z$ is positive semidefinite.

derivations.claim: Apply [F2] with scalar statistic $X=H$ and parameter $\theta=-\beta$. Then $\partial_\beta\log Z=-\langle H\rangle=-U$, and $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}(H)$. Differentiating the first identity gives $\partial_\beta U=-\operatorname{Var}(H)$.
Since $d\beta/dT=-1/(k_BT^2)$, the chain rule yields $\partial_TU=(-\operatorname{Var}(H))(-1/(k_BT^2)) =\operatorname{Var}(H)/(k_BT^2)$. A variance is an integral of a square, so it is nonnegative.

units J per particle under the SI convention
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. For $N\ge1$, let $\Gamma_N$ and its reference
measure be those of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]]. Define
the vacuum sector by $\Gamma_0=\{*\}$ with sigma-algebra
$\mathcal F_0=\{\varnothing,\{*\}\}$, reference mass
$m_0^{\mathrm{phys}}(\{*\})=1$, particle number $N=0$, and vacuum Hamiltonian
$H_0(*)=0$. On the disjoint union $\mathcal G:=\bigsqcup_{N=0}^\infty\Gamma_N$,
use the sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathcal G}:=\{A\subseteq\mathcal G:A\cap\Gamma_N\in\mathcal F_N\text{ for every }N\ge0\},$$
where $\mathcal F_N$ is the declared measurable structure on sector $N$, and
the reference measure
$$m^{\mathrm{phys}}(A):=\sum_{N=0}^\infty m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(A\cap\Gamma_N).$$
Let each $H_N$ for $N\ge1$ be measurable
and let
$$\Xi(\beta,\mu):=\sum_{N=0}^\infty\int_{\Gamma_N} e^{-\beta(H_N-\mu N)}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}$$
satisfy $0<\Xi<\infty$. Adopt the joint state with density
$\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta(H_N-\mu N)}$ on sector $N$. The finiteness condition is
part of the model; it requires control of the sector sum and is not implied
by each finite-sector partition function being finite. Particle-exchange
preparation is an assumption, not a deduction from fixed-$N$ dynamics. Under
the vacuum convention above, the $N=0$ contribution to $\Xi$ is exactly one.

Fix $N$, dimension $d$, $T>0$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ as in

$P_{\rm ext}>0$ in J m$^{-d}$, a fixed dimensionless shape
$Q_1\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ that is Lebesgue measurable with $|Q_1|_d=1$, and
a positive volume reference $V_0$ in m$^d$. Write
$y=(y_1,\ldots,y_N)\in Q_1^N$, take $dy$ to be product Lebesgue measure on
$Q_1^N$, and take $dp$ to be Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^{dN}$. Identify
the position domain at volume $V>0$ by $q_i=V^{1/d}y_i$. The Jacobian is
$V^N$, which is the full position-volume factor because $|Q_1|_d=1$. Adopt
the joint reference
$$d\nu_N=\frac{dV}{V_0}\,\frac{V^N\,dy\,dp}{N!a_0^{dN}},$$
where $a_0>0$ is the action reference in J s. For the chosen Hamiltonian
$H_N(V,y,p)$, assume
$$0<\Delta_N:=\int_0^\infty\!\int e^{-\beta(H_N(V,y,p)+P_{\rm ext}V)}\,d\nu_N<\infty.$$

with fixed counts $N_a$, replace it by $\prod_aN_a!$ as in

unless it is explicitly included in the Hamiltonian, and does not claim a
smooth wall dynamics.
