Only finitely many summands are nonzero. This is the cell form used in the continuum pressure arguments.

Let $d\geq1$ and let $\phi$ be a regular potential with a nonnegative nonincreasing envelope $\psi:[R_0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, where $R_0<\infty$ and $\int_{R_0}^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr<\infty$. Thus $|\phi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ for $|x|_\infty\geq R_0$. For $g>2R_0$ set
$$\eta(g)=g^d\psi(g)+\int_g^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr.$$
Then $\eta(g)\to0$ and
$$\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{d-1}\psi(mg)\leq 2^{d-1}g^{-d}\eta(g).$$
Moreover, there is a choice $g(\ell)>0$, for all sufficiently large real $\ell$, such that $g(\ell)\to\infty$, $g(\ell)/\ell\to0$, and
$$\left(\frac{\ell}{g(\ell)}\right)^d\eta(g(\ell))\longrightarrow0.$$
For every fixed finite configuration and all sufficiently large periods $L$, the noncoincident periodic-image tail $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d,\ |k|_\infty\geq K_0}|\phi(x-y+Lk)|$ is absolutely convergent. The tail of the cell envelope $\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ over all sufficiently large integer offsets is summable. This lemma is a deterministic tail estimate; it uses no superstability or thermodynamic-limit conclusion.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB, and the superstable regular interaction of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For integers $N_L$ with $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)$ be the $1/N_L!$-normalized positional partition on the periodized cube, with the image convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Then
$$L^{-d}\log Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the same rate as the free cube. Let $C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L}$ be the periodic exact-$N_L$ canonical law and $R_{L,\omega}$ its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. For any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, these empirical fields concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$. Writing $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ for this minimizer set, the concentration means $(C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L})^*\{\omega:R_{L,\omega}\notin U\}\to0$ for every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of it. Here outer probability is as defined in [[lem-tdmath-canonical-empirical-field-conditioning]], and equals ordinary probability for measurable events. A singleton minimizer gives convergence in probability in this outer-probability sense in $\tau_L$.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let
$$\mathcal H_c:=\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega): I(P)\leq c\},\qquad c\in[0,\infty),$$
where $I$ and the local-tame topology $\tau_L$ are defined by [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. Then $\mathcal H_c$ is compact and sequentially compact in $\tau_L$. This is a pure measure-theoretic compactness theorem for simple locally finite configurations relative to the independent unit-intensity Poisson reference; it makes no thermodynamic-limit or physical claim.

Assume AC and let $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, with this class defined in [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], be stationary for the translations of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. For a bounded Borel set $G$, write $P_G$ and $Q_G$ for the restrictions of $P$ and the unit-intensity Poisson reference $Q$ to configurations in $G$. For $L>0$, put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and
$$D_L:=D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
Then the specific relative entropy density
$$I(P):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D_L}{L^d}$$
exists in $[0,+\infty]$ and satisfies
$$I(P)=\sup_{m\in\mathbb N,\ m\geq1}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})}{m^d}.$$
If $I(P)<\infty$, every bounded Borel restriction has finite relative entropy. This is an information functional relative to the specified unit-intensity Poisson law; changing the reference changes its value.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. Use the stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, the specific relative entropy $I(P)$, the intensity $\rho(P)$, and the positional energy density $\Phi(P)=\mathcal E(P)$ defined in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are established below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Use the model and dimensionless energy $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Let $L_n\to\infty$, $V_n=L_n^d$, and integers $N_n$ satisfy $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$, where $\rho$ is an interior attainable density for the positional canonical rate. Fix $b>0$. Assume $F_b(\rho)$ is the periodic exact-particle log-partition rate supplied by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]] for every $b'$ in a neighborhood of $b$, and is differentiable at $b$. Write $C_n^{\rm ph}$ for the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical law, and define
$$e_b(\rho)=-\partial_bF_b(\rho)+\frac{d\rho}{2b}.$$
Then, for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that
$$C_n^{\rm ph}\!\left(\left|\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le 2e^{-c_\varepsilon V_n}\quad(n\ge n_0).$$
Consequently there is a nonincreasing sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the full phase band
$$A_n=\{N=N_n,\ |\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)|\le\delta_n\}$$
has $C_n^{\rm ph}(A_n)\to1$. It has positive finite phase-reference measure for all sufficiently large $n$. This constructs a controlled shrinking window; it makes no claim about every prescribed shell width or an exact energy surface.

Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. Positions $x=q/\ell_0$ are dimensionless numerical coordinates; write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. The dimensionless positional energy $U_{L,bc}$ is the physical pair energy divided by $E_0$, with $bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$ and the exact image convention above. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. On an $N$-point configuration, attach one momentum $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ to each point and use the symmetric product reference $r^{\otimes q}$ with $r(dp)=dp/p_*^d$. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite; the factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on the torus, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are torus-translation invariant.

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the cube $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and the translation $T_x$ defined in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. For a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, let $\omega^{(L)}=\{q+Lk:q\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ be its periodic continuation. Define its **periodized empirical field**
$$R_{L,\omega}:=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}\delta_{T_x\omega^{(L)}}\,dx.$$
The integral is the push-forward of normalized Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ under $x\mapsto T_x\omega^{(L)}$. For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$, define its **empirical-field barycenter** as the probability mixture
$$\bar C_L(B)=\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(B)$$
for every measurable configuration event $B$. By [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], for a nonnegative measurable test $f$, the mixture identity holds with values in $[0,+\infty]$. For a signed local tame $f$ from [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], the finite expectation formula
$$\bar C_L(f)=\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(f)=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}E_{C_L}[f(T_x\omega^{(L)})]\,dx$$
is asserted when $\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(|f|)<\infty$. In particular $E_{C_L}N<\infty$ suffices: if a bounded support $A$ is contained in a box of side $a$, then $N_A(T_x\omega^{(L)})\leq (\lceil a/L\rceil+2)^dN(\omega)$ uniformly in $x$. The growth bound $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ therefore gives absolute integrability. For stationary laws write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}\in[0,+\infty]$, with finite intensity meaning $\rho(P)<\infty$; this agrees with the finite-intensity convention in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. This is a spatial average over the finite box, not the raw finite-volume law viewed at a fixed origin.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $L>0$ and a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ with $N(\omega)=N$, the measure $R_{L,\omega}$ of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] is a stationary probability law of finite intensity and
$$\rho(R_{L,\omega})=\frac{N}{L^d}.$$
For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$, its empirical-field barycenter $\bar C_L$ is also a stationary probability law of finite intensity and $\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}N/L^d$.

Assume AC, fix $d\geq1$ and $\lambda>0$, and let $Q_\lambda$ be the configuration law of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Define the intensity measure on Borel sets by $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A):=E_{Q_\lambda}N_A$, where $N_A=\omega(A)$ and the nonnegative expectation may be infinite. For pairwise disjoint bounded Borel sets $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the restrictions $\omega|_{A_1},\ldots,\omega|_{A_r}$ are independent, each count $N_{A_j}$ has Poisson law with mean $\lambda|A_j|$, and the joint law of counts on any finite disjoint family is the product of those Poisson laws. In particular, $Q_\lambda$ is invariant under every translation $T_x$, and $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A)=\lambda|A|$ for every Borel $A$. For every bounded Borel $A$ and real $a$, its count also has the exact exponential moment
$$E_{Q_\lambda}e^{aN_A}=\exp\!\left(\lambda|A|(e^a-1)\right).$$

derivations.claim:
Put D_n=D(M_n^ph || C_n^ph), and let B_n be the positional marginal. The conditional chain rule gives
$$D_n=D(B_n||C_n^pos)+E_{B_n}D(b_n(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_n}),$$
so D(B_n||C_n^pos)≤D_n by the conditional chain rule [F8]. The canonical positional density relative to full Poisson probability Q_Λn is 1_{N=N_n} exp(-bU_n,per)/Z_Q,n^pos, where Z_Q,n^pos=exp(-V_n)Z_n,N_n^pos. Integrating the log likelihood against B_n gives
$$D(B_n||Q_{\Lambda_n})+bE_{B_n}U_{n,per}=D(B_n||C_n^{pos})-\log Z_{Q,n}^{pos}\le D_n-\log Z_{Q,n}^{pos}.$$
By [F1] and [F4], V_n^-1 log Z_Q,n^pos→F_b(ρ)-1; hence the right side divided by V_n has limsup at most 1-F_b(ρ).

On the full shell from [F7], $U_{n,\mathrm{per}}=\mathcal H_n-\sum K\leq V_n(e_b+\delta_n)$. Combining this with the cell bound [F2] yields $E_{B_n}\sum_iN_{C_i}^2/V_n\leq A^{-1}(e_b+\delta_n+B N_n/V_n)$, uniformly bounded. Because $L_n$ is an integer, its torus is tiled by $V_n$ unit cells; torus translation invariance makes all $E_{B_n}N_{C_i}^2$ equal, so each is bounded by the preceding sum divided by $V_n$. Cauchy–Schwarz then gives a uniform bound $E_{B_n}N_{C_i}N_{C_j}\leq C$ for every pair of cells. For the negative interaction, each bounded-distance cell has only finitely many neighboring cells and each pair term has negative part at most $2B_0$ by [F2]; for the remaining offsets, [F3] bounds absolute pair energy by the summable envelope $\Psi$. Summing these bounds with $E_{B_n}N_{C_i}N_{C_j}\leq C$ gives $E_{B_n}U_{n,\mathrm{per}}^-=O(V_n)$. The shell upper bound on $E U_{n,\mathrm{per}}$ then gives $E_{B_n}U_{n,\mathrm{per}}^+=O(V_n)$ and hence $E_{B_n}|U_{n,\mathrm{per}}|=O(V_n)$.

Let $\widetilde g_n=\widetilde g(L_n)$ be the real corridor width supplied by [F3] at $L_n$, and set $g_n=\lceil\widetilde g_n\rceil$. Then $g_n\to\infty$ and $g_n/L_n\to0$, and $a_n=L_n+g_n$ is an integer. Independently sample a configuration with law $B_n$ in each cube of side $L_n$ on the lattice $a_n\mathbb Z^d$, leave the intervening corridors empty, and choose the lattice origin uniformly in $[0,a_n)^d$. Translating the origin preserves its uniform law and only relabels the independent, identically distributed tiles, so $P_n$ is translation-stationary; it is locally finite because bounded sets meet finitely many finite tiles. Put $\rho_n=N_n/V_n$. Its intensity is $N_n/a_n^d=\rho_nV_n/a_n^d\to\rho$. For a fixed local-tame test $f$ supported in a bounded set $A$, choose $r$ larger than its coordinate diameter. The random phase puts $A$ wholly inside an occupied tile with probability at least $(L_n-2r)^d/a_n^d\to1$. On this event torus translation invariance of $B_n$ gives exactly its local law. For any Borel set $E\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$, torus invariance and the exact count $N_n$ give
$$E_{B_n}N_E=\frac1{V_n}\int_{\mathbb T_{L_n}^d}E_{B_n}N_{E+y}\,dy=\frac{N_n|E|}{V_n}.$$
The first equality uses invariance; for each fixed configuration, the integral in the numerator sums over its $N_n$ points, and each point lies in $E+y$ for a set of translations of measure $|E|$. Apply this identity to each occupied portion of $A$ on the bad phase set; gap portions contain no points. The phase-averaged expectation of $(1+N_A)$ on that set is at most its probability times $1+\rho_n|A|$. Since $|f|\leq C(1+N_A)$ and $\rho_n$ is bounded, $P_n(f)-B_n(f)\to0$.

Fix $n$ and a lattice phase, and restrict to a large observation cube. Its intersections with complete occupied tiles have independent laws $B_n$; its gap pieces are empty; and only $O_n(\text{surface area})$ tile intersections meet the observation boundary. The Poisson restrictions on these disjoint pieces are independent by [F10]. For each complete occupied tile, the relative entropy is $D(B_n\Vert Q_{\Lambda_{L_n}})$; restriction contraction [F8] bounds each boundary-tile contribution by this same finite value. An empty gap piece $G$ has entropy $D(\delta_{\varnothing}\Vert Q_G)=-\log Q_G(\varnothing)=|G|$. Product additivity follows by iterating the chain rule [F8]. Convexity in the first law [F8] shows that averaging over the uniform phase does not increase the bound. Divide by observation volume and let the cube grow: the complete-tile density tends to $a_n^{-d}$, the gap-volume density to $(a_n^d-L_n^d)/a_n^d$, and the boundary contribution to zero. The specific-entropy limit exists by [F5], so
$$I(P_n)\leq\frac{D(B_n\Vert Q_{\Lambda_{L_n}})+a_n^d-L_n^d}{a_n^d}.$$
For the energy comparison, assign half of each pair term to each endpoint cell. Step 2.1 gives a uniform pair-count bound $E N_{C_i}N_{C_j}\leq C$ and an $O(V_n)$ bound on the expected total positive energy. Fix $R>R_0$. Periodic-image pairs of torus separation at most $R$ that are absent from the free-tile energy cross a tile face; their endpoints lie in a boundary strip of width $R+1$ containing $O(RL_n^{d-1})$ unit cells. The negative contribution per such cell is bounded by the finite number of near offsets, the lower bound $\phi\geq-2B_0$ from [F2], and the pair-count bound; the positive contribution per cell is bounded by the total positive-energy estimate and torus invariance. Thus the expected absolute fixed-range discrepancy divided by $V_n$ is $O(R/L_n)$. For remaining pairs, [F3] bounds the expected absolute energy per volume by $C\sum_{|k|_\infty>R-c_d}\Psi(k)$, tending to zero as $R\to\infty$. Cross-tile pairs have separation at least $g_n$; the same bound with $R=g_n$ tends to zero as $g_n\to\infty$. Therefore the stationary block law's positional energy density satisfies $\Phi(P_n)=E_{B_n}U_{n,\mathrm{per}}/a_n^d+o(1)$. Combining the entropy bound, step 1.1, and $a_n^d/V_n\to1$ gives
$$\limsup_n[I(P_n)+b\Phi(P_n)]\leq1-F_b(\rho).$$
Here the gap fraction vanishes because $g_n/L_n\to0$.

Stability gives $\Phi(P_n)\geq-B_0\rho(P_n)$, so step 4.1 bounds $I(P_n)$. Compactness [F5] supplies a convergent subsequence from every subsequence. If $P$ is a cluster point, intensity is continuous in $\tau_L$ because the unit-cell count is a local-tame test, hence $\rho(P)=\rho$. Lower semicontinuity and step 4.1 give $I(P)+b\Phi(P)\leq1-F_b(\rho)$. Subtract $\alpha\rho$ and apply the variational lower bound and exact minimum [F6]; $P$ must attain the grand variational minimum. The singleton hypothesis forces $P=P_*$. Thus every cluster point is $P_*$, compactness gives $P_n\to P_*$, and step 3.1 gives $B_n[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every local-tame $f$. By [F9], $\bar B_n$ is stationary with intensity $N_n/V_n$, and torus invariance gives $\bar B_n(f)=B_n[f]$; therefore $\bar B_n\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$. For the exact-$N_n$ canonical law $C_n^{\rm pos}$, [F4] says its periodized empirical field $R_{L_n,\omega}$ converges in outer probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$. For a local-tame $f$ with $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$, [F9] makes $X_n:=R_{L_n,\omega}(f)$ measurable and gives $|X_n|\leq c(1+N_n|A|/V_n)$, uniformly in $n$. Thus $X_n\to P_*(f)$ in probability and the variables are uniformly bounded; for each $\epsilon>0$, $|E X_n-P_*(f)|\leq\epsilon+(M+|P_*(f)|)\Pr(|X_n-P_*(f)|>\epsilon)$ for a common bound $M$, so $E X_n\to P_*(f)$. Torus translation invariance and [F9] identify $E X_n=C_n^{\rm pos}[f]$. Hence the exact-$N_n$ canonical positional local expectations also converge to $P_*$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. Positions $x=q/\ell_0$ are dimensionless numerical coordinates; write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. The dimensionless positional energy $U_{L,bc}$ is the physical pair energy divided by $E_0$, with $bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$ and the exact image convention above. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. On an $N$-point configuration, attach one momentum $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ to each point and use the symmetric product reference $r^{\otimes q}$ with $r(dp)=dp/p_*^d$. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite; the factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on the torus, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are torus-translation invariant.

$$P_{\rm Leb}(α,b)=F_b(ρ)+αρ,$$
where $P_{\rm Leb}$ is the grand pressure per numerical volume with Lebesgue $1/N!$ normalization. Let the positional grand variational minimizer of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]] at activity $\exp(\alpha)$ and inverse temperature $b$ be the singleton $\{P_*\}$. Then $\bar B_n$ converges to $P_*$ in $\tau_L$, equivalently $B_n[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every local-tame $f$; also $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every such $f$. Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$. For $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, let $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$. These are left-closed, right-open cells. For every $x\in\mathbb R^d$, [[lem-integer-part]] supplies the unique integers $i_j$ with $i_j\le x_j<i_j+1$, so $x$ belongs to exactly one $C_i$. The cells are Borel products of closed/open ray intersections and have volume one by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], whose statement covers this face convention. A finite configuration in $C_i$ is a finite subset of distinct points. Encode it by its cardinality $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and its uniquely lexicographically increasing list of local coordinates $(x_1-i,\ldots,x_n-i)\in([0,1)^d)^n$. Pad the code after its first $n$ coordinates with the zero vector. For fixed $n$, the strictly increasing lists form a Borel subset of $([0,1]^d)^n$, since lexicographic strict order is a finite union of coordinate-equality and coordinate-inequality conditions. Thus all codes form a Borel subset of $\mathbb N_0\times([0,1]^d)^{\mathbb N}$. Each factor $[0,1]^d$ is Polish as a closed subspace of complete $\mathbb R^d$ with a countable dense rational grid; $\mathbb N_0$ with its discrete metric is Polish. The ambient space is Polish by [[cor-countable-products-and-g-delta-subspaces-of-polish-spaces-are-polish]] (and is completely metrized by [[lem-standard-complete-metric-on-a-countable-product]]), so [[lem-borel-subspaces-admit-polish-presentations]] makes the cell space $E_i$ standard Borel. By [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]], its sigma-algebra is generated by the counts $N_B$ for Borel $B\subseteq C_i$.

Use $e^t:=\exp(t)$ for real $t$, with $\exp$ defined by [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]; for a real measurable function $f$, $e^f$ means the pointwise composition $\exp\circ f$. For $\lambda>0$, give a cell configuration with $n$ points probability $\exp(-\lambda)\lambda^n/n!$ for its count. The probabilities sum to $\exp(-\lambda)\exp(\lambda)=\exp(0)=1$ by the exponential power series and [[thm-exponential-addition-formula]]. Conditional on count $n$, take the $n$-fold product of normalized Lebesgue measure on $C_i$, restrict it to the complement of the collision diagonals, and push it forward by lexicographic sorting. The product exists by the finite product-measure theorem; each collision diagonal is null by Tonelli and the fact that Lebesgue measure gives every singleton measure zero, so the restricted measure still has mass one. Sorting is Borel on the finitely many permutation regions of the no-collision set. This defines a law $\pi_{i,\lambda}$ on $E_i$; for $n=0$, use the empty product and the empty configuration. The product sigma-algebra is generated by the cell-coordinate sigma-algebras, each generated by counts on Borel subsets of its bounded cell by [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]]. Conversely every bounded-region count is a finite sum of these cell counts, since a bounded set meets finitely many cells. Identify each $\omega\in\Omega$ with the simple locally finite counting measure obtained by uniting its finite cell configurations. For a bounded Borel set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, write $N_A(\omega)=\omega(A)$ and $|A|$ for its Lebesgue measure. Define translation by $T_x\omega(A)=\omega(A-x)$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$. This item is a mathematical reference construction and makes no physical claim.

Let $\Omega$ be the positional configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. The **marked configuration space** $\Omega^{\rm mark}$ consists of marked point sets $\xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ with spatial projection $q=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\exists p\in\mathbb R^d,\ (x,p)\in\xi\}$ that is simple and locally finite, and with exactly one mark $p_x$ paired to each $x\in q$. Its sigma-algebra is generated by the marked counts $N_{A\times C}(\xi)=\#\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in A,\ p\in C\}$ for bounded Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. The positional projection is $\pi(\xi)=q\in\Omega$. For a bounded Borel set $\Delta$, the **marked local restriction** is $\xi_\Delta=\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in\Delta\}$ with the induced count sigma-algebra; write $N_\Delta(\xi)=\#\xi_\Delta$. A **marked-local observable on $\Delta$** is a real measurable function of $\xi_\Delta$; it is bounded when its supremum norm is finite.

Let $d\geq1$, $L>0$, and $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$. A finite marked configuration consists of a finite simple set of positions $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$ and a mark map $p:q\to\mathbb R^d$, as in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Its **marked periodic continuation** is
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:=\{(x+Lk,p_x):x\in q,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}.$$
The spatial positions in this set are distinct: if $x+Lk=y+Lj$ for $x,y\in[0,L)^d$, then coordinatewise $x-y=L(j-k)$ forces $j=k$ and $x=y$. Every bounded spatial region meets finitely many lattice translates of the finite set $q$, so the continuation has a locally finite spatial projection.

For a bounded Borel set $\Delta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, define its **marked local restriction** by
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}|_\Delta:=\{(y,p_x)\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:y\in\Delta\}.$$
This is an element of $\Omega^{\rm mark}$, with the induced sigma-algebra of marked counts above. If $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_L$, the restriction is exactly the original marked points with positions in $\Delta$.

Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $Q_i$ be probability measures on $X_i$, and let $P$ be a probability on $\prod_{i=1}^mX_i$. $$D(T_*P\Vert T_*Q)\leq D(P\Vert Q),\qquad \|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}:=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\leq\sqrt{D(P\Vert Q)/2}.$$
The entropy convention is the directional KL definition of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]], and the total-variation convention is the event-supremum convention of [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]. The inequality remains valid when $D=+\infty$.

Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the finite phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the constructed band, and set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$. This is a mathematical statement about a normalized measure restriction; it does not assert $D_n\to0$ or global total-variation convergence.

derivations.claim:
The phase reference has a measurable density. For each $q$, integrate the band indicator over the $N_n$-mark reference; Tonelli gives a measurable normalizer. On the $B_n$-full set where it is positive, division gives the conditional kernel $b_n(\cdot|q)$; choose a fixed probability kernel on the null complement. The conditional chain rule, nonnegativity of the positional divergence, and [F3] give
$$J_n:=E_{B_n}D(b_n(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_n})\le D(M_n^{ph}||C_n^{ph}).$$

For each $q$, partition its finitely many points into those in each of the $L_n^{\rm pack}$ disjoint translates $C_j$ packed in the periodic cube, plus the remainder. This is a measurable finite partition; ordering the points by the cell codes in [F2] identifies each block with a finite-dimensional standard-Borel mark space, even though its size depends on $q$. $$D(b_n(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_n})\ge\sum_{j=1}^{L_n^{pack}}D(b_{n,j}(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_{Δ_j}(q)}),$$

For $\Delta\subseteq C$, restriction of the ordered mark vector on $q\cap C$ to the points in $q\cap\Delta$ is measurable. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

By torus translation invariance, represent any bounded Borel region $\Delta$ by a fixed translate inside $\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Choose an axis-parallel half-open cube $C\supseteq\Delta$ of side $\ell>0$, independent of $n$, and pack $L_n^{\rm pack}=\lfloor L_n/\ell\rfloor^d$ disjoint translates of $C$ into the periodic cube, so $L_n^{\rm pack}/V_n\to1/|C|$. For the independent Gaussian mark reference $\nu_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]],
$$E_{B_n}D(b_{n,\Delta}(\cdot|q)||\nu_b^{\otimes N_\Delta(q)})\leq D(M_n^{\rm ph}||C_n^{\rm ph})/L_n^{\rm pack}.$$
Thus the left side tends to zero. When $\Delta$ itself is an axis-parallel half-open cube, take $C=\Delta$ to obtain the stated packing rate $1/|\Delta|$. Occupancy $N_\Delta(q)$ is random; the comparison is for the full spatially selected set of particles, not a fixed set of labels.

This is an element of $\Omega^{\rm mark}$, with the induced sigma-algebra of marked counts above. If $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_L$, the restriction is exactly the original marked points with positions in $\Delta$.

Let $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$ be the probability laws $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]] that are invariant under every $T_x$ and satisfy $E_PN_{C_0}<\infty$. Stationarity then makes every bounded-region count integrable, because a bounded set meets finitely many unit cells.

A real measurable function $f$ on $\Omega$ is local if there is a bounded Borel set $A$ such that $f$ is measurable with respect to the restriction $\omega\mapsto\omega|_A$. It is tame if there is a finite $b\geq0$ such that $|f(\omega)|\leq b(1+N_A(\omega))$ for every $\omega$ and one such bounded $A$. Write $\mathcal T$ for the family of all local tame functions. Each $f\in\mathcal T$ is integrable under every $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$.

The local-tame topology $\tau_L$ on $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$ is the initial topology generated by all maps $P\mapsto E_P f$, $f\in\mathcal T$. Equivalently, a net $(P_\alpha)$ converges to $P$ in $\tau_L$ exactly when $E_{P_\alpha}f\to E_Pf$ for every measurable local $f$ with at most linear growth in the count of a bounded support. Bounded local indicators are among these tests, so this topology separates distinct probability laws. The domain restriction to finite-intensity stationary laws ensures every displayed expectation is a finite real number.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. Use the stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, the specific relative entropy $I(P)$, the intensity $\rho(P)$, and the positional energy density $\Phi(P)=\mathcal E(P)$ defined in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are established below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.

derivations.claim: Let $B_n$ be the shell positional marginal and let $\widehat B_n$ sample $B_n$ followed by independent $\nu_b$ marks. Form two augmented laws on (all positions $q$, marks attached to $q\cap\Delta$): the first is the corresponding marginal of $M_n^{\rm ph}$ and the second is that of $\widehat B_n$. Conditional on $q$, their mark laws are $b_{n,\Delta}(\cdot|q)$ and $\nu_b^{\otimes N_\Delta(q)}$. The relative-entropy chain rule therefore makes the augmented divergence exactly the conditional KL average in [F1]. Restricting the augmented observation to positions and marks in $\Delta$ is measurable; data processing and Pinsker [F2] show that the local marked restrictions of $M_n^{\rm ph}$ and $\widehat B_n$ have total variation tending to zero. For bounded $G$, the expectation difference is at most $2\|G\|_\infty$ times this event-supremum distance, hence tends to zero.

Integrate $G$ against the finite product $\nu_b$ marks at fixed local $q$ and call the result $g(q\cap\Delta)$. The lift construction [F5] gives this measurable kernel and its infinite marked law; since $G$ is bounded, $|g|\leq\|G\|_\infty$. By [F6], $g$ is local-tame. Therefore $E_{\widehat B_n}G=B_n(g)\to P_*(g)=E_{P_*^{\rm mark}}G$ by [F3]. The canonical factorization in [F4] and canonical positional convergence in [F3] give the second limit. By [F4], the matching full activity is $\exp(\alpha)/\kappa_b$; this identifies the same infinite variational marked state and says nothing about convergence of finite-volume grand laws.

Suppose |G|≤C(1+N_Δ). By [F6], bounded indicators of each count value are local-tame, so their probabilities converge under B_n by [F3]; the mean count also converges because N_Δ is local-tame. For integer K, E_{B_n}(N_Δ-K)^+=E_{B_n}N_Δ-E_{B_n}(N_Δ∧K); for fixed K this converges to the corresponding P_* expectation. If N_Δ>2K, then N_Δ≤2(N_Δ-K), so E[N_Δ1_{N_Δ>2K}]≤2E(N_Δ-K)^+. First take limsup over n, then K→∞; integrability of N_Δ under P_* makes this tail vanish. Indeed P_* is stationary with finite unit-cell intensity by [F7], and bounded Δ meets only finitely many unit cells. This proves uniform integrability of 1+N_Δ under B_n. The shell and Gaussian lift have the same local count law. The limiting marked lift has the same local count as P_*, so its tail also vanishes. Truncate G to N_Δ≤K; it is bounded, so step 1.1 applies. Both finite-volume omitted tails are bounded by C E[(1+N_Δ)1_{N_Δ>K}], uniformly vanishing as K→∞. Let n→∞ and then K→∞ to obtain the claimed shell limit.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[thm-csm-full-shell-positional-minimizer]]. Let $M_n^{\rm ph}$ be the normalized phase-reference restriction to $A_n$, and let $B_n$ be its positional marginal. Given the full position configuration $q$, let $b_{n,A}(\cdot|q)$ be the shell conditional law of marks on the marked local restriction of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. By torus translation invariance, represent any bounded Borel region $\Delta$ by a fixed translate inside $\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Choose an axis-parallel half-open cube $C\supseteq\Delta$ of side $\ell>0$, independent of $n$, and pack $L_n^{\rm pack}=\lfloor L_n/\ell\rfloor^d$ disjoint translates of $C$ into the periodic cube, so $L_n^{\rm pack}/V_n\to1/|C|$. For the independent Gaussian mark reference $\nu_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]],
$$E_{B_n}D(b_{n,\Delta}(\cdot|q)||\nu_b^{\otimes N_\Delta(q)})\leq D(M_n^{\rm ph}||C_n^{\rm ph})/L_n^{\rm pack}.$$
Thus the left side tends to zero. When $\Delta$ itself is an axis-parallel half-open cube, take $C=\Delta$ to obtain the stated packing rate $1/|\Delta|$. Occupancy $N_\Delta(q)$ is random; the comparison is for the full spatially selected set of particles, not a fixed set of labels.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Use the model and dimensionless energy $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Let $L_n\to\infty$, $V_n=L_n^d$, and integers $N_n$ satisfy $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$, where $\rho$ is an interior attainable density for the positional canonical rate. Fix $b>0$. Assume $F_b(\rho)$ is the periodic exact-particle log-partition rate supplied by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]] for every $b'$ in a neighborhood of $b$, and is differentiable at $b$. Write $C_n^{\rm ph}$ for the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical law, and define
$$e_b(\rho)=-\partial_bF_b(\rho)+\frac{d\rho}{2b}.$$
Then, for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that
$$C_n^{\rm ph}\!\left(\left|\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le 2e^{-c_\varepsilon V_n}\quad(n\ge n_0).$$
Consequently there is a nonincreasing sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the full phase band
$$A_n=\{N=N_n,\ |\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)|\le\delta_n\}$$
has $C_n^{\rm ph}(A_n)\to1$. It has positive finite phase-reference measure for all sufficiently large $n$. This constructs a controlled shrinking window; it makes no claim about every prescribed shell width or an exact energy surface.

Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. Positions $x=q/\ell_0$ are dimensionless numerical coordinates; write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. The dimensionless positional energy $U_{L,bc}$ is the physical pair energy divided by $E_0$, with $bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$ and the exact image convention above. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. On an $N$-point configuration, attach one momentum $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ to each point and use the symmetric product reference $r^{\otimes q}$ with $r(dp)=dp/p_*^d$. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite; the factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on the torus, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are torus-translation invariant.

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC and HB, the exact superstable regular pair interaction and periodic-image convention of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], and integer side lengths $L_n\to\infty$ with exact particle numbers $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$ at an interior attainable density. Fix $b>0$. Assume the positional canonical log rate is $F_b(\rho)$, and choose finite $\alpha$ with
$$P_{\rm Leb}(α,b)=F_b(ρ)+αρ,$$
where $P_{\rm Leb}$ is the grand pressure per numerical volume with Lebesgue $1/N!$ normalization. Let the positional grand variational minimizer of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]] at activity $\exp(\alpha)$ and inverse temperature $b$ be the singleton $\{P_*\}$. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the band of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]], set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$, and let $B_n$ be its positional marginal. For any local-tame test $f$, write $B_n[f]=E_{B_n}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$ and $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]=E_{C_n^{\rm pos}}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$, where $\omega^{(L_n)}$ is the periodic continuation. Let $\bar B_n$ be the barycenter of $R_{L_n,\omega}$ under $B_n$. Then $\bar B_n$ converges to $P_*$ in $\tau_L$, equivalently $B_n[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every local-tame $f$; also $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every such $f$. The periodized empirical fields of the exact-$N_n$ canonical laws converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$ by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]], and $P_*$ has intensity $\rho$. Here $P_*$ is an infinite-volume positional variational state; no finite-volume grand-canonical local convergence or DLR identification is asserted.

Assume AC. Let $P$ be any probability law on the simple locally finite positional configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], and let $
u$ be a probability on the momentum mark space $\mathbb R^d$. Use the marked configuration space $\Omega^{m mark}$ and local restrictions $\xi_\Delta$ of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. Define translations by $T_yq=\{x+y:x\in q\}$ and $T_y^{m mark}\xi=\{(x+y,p):(x,p)\in\xi\}$. Then there is a unique probability law $P^{m mark}$ on $\Omega^{m mark}$ whose positional projection is $P$ and whose marks, conditional on the entire positional configuration, are independent with common law $
u$. If $P$ is translation invariant, meaning $(T_y)_\#P=P$ for every $y\in\mathbb R^d$, then $(T_y^{m mark})_\#P^{m mark}=P^{m mark}$ for every $y$. For the Gaussian $
u_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], this is the independent Gaussian-marked positional lift. This is a mathematical marking construction, not a physical preparation or a convergence result.

Fix one named $g$ and write $S_\Delta=\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}(g(p_x)-E_\nu g)$. For positive $t$ in reciprocal units to $g$, the unbounded test $tS_\Delta$ is dimensionless; define $h_M:=\max(-M,\min(M,tS_\Delta))$ and first use this bounded truncation in [F4]. The bounds $|h_M|\leq t|S_\Delta|$ and $e^{h_M}\leq1+e^{tS_\Delta}$, together with shell integrability from [F3] and the Gaussian exponential moment [F2], permit dominated convergence as $M\to\infty$. Since $N_\Delta\leq N_n$ and $c_g(t)$ is finite near zero, the reference exponential moment is finite at each $n$. Thus the variational inequality extends to $tS_\Delta$ and gives
$$tE_{b_{n,\Delta}(.|q)}S_\Delta\le D(b_{n,\Delta}(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_\Delta})+N_\Delta c_g(t)$$
for sufficiently small t>0. Testing with -tS_Δ gives the analogous inequality for -E S_Δ and c_g(-t). The integrals are finite: the shell bounds total kinetic energy at each n, and the Gaussian exponential moments exist by [F2]. Averaging over B_n yields
$$|E_{M_n^{ph}}S_\Delta|\le\{E_{B_n}D(b_{n,\Delta}||ν_b^{⊗N_\Delta})+E_{B_n}N_\Delta\max(c_g(t),c_g(-t))\}/t.$$

For any fixed exact-$N_n$ configuration on the torus, averaging $N_\Delta$ over all torus translations gives $N_n|\Delta|/V_n$: each of its $N_n$ points is translated into $\Delta$ for a set of translation parameters of Lebesgue measure $|\Delta|$. Translation invariance of $B_n$ and $C_n^{\rm pos}$ therefore gives $E_{B_n}N_\Delta=E_{C_n^{\rm pos}}N_\Delta=N_n|\Delta|/V_n\to\rho|\Delta|$. For fixed $t>0$, the first numerator term in step 1.1 vanishes by [F1]. The limsup is at most $\rho|\Delta|\max(c_g(t),c_g(-t))/t$; this tends to zero as $t\downarrow0$ because $c_g(\pm t)=O(t^2)$ by [F2]. Hence $E_{M_n^{\rm ph}}S_\Delta\to0$. Adding $E_{B_n}N_\Delta\,E_{\nu_b}g$ and substituting the three means in [F2] proves the shell formulas. By [F5], $E_{P_*}N_\Delta=\lim_nE_{C_n^{\rm pos}}N_\Delta=\rho|\Delta|$. Conditional independent marking [F6] gives the same three limits for the variational-grand marked law; the exact canonical law has them by independent marking as well.

Fix the model, physical reference conventions, mass, potential and energy window specified by [[def-csm-full-marked-model]] and [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Identify the action reference a_0 of [[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]] with h_ref=ℓ_0p_* from the marked model. Adopt the following alternative preparations whenever their normalizations are finite and positive:

1. At fixed exact particle number $N$, controls and $T>0$, use the canonical density proportional to $e^{-\beta H}$ relative to the declared phase reference, as in [[post-csm-canonical-preparation]].
2. For a sequence satisfying all hypotheses of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]—including AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, HB, an interior attainable density, the periodic exact-particle log-rate hypothesis near $b$, and differentiability at $b$—at fixed exact $N_n$ use the uniform full-phase reference law restricted to its constructed band $A_n$. “Uniform” means normalized restriction of that finite reference measure; it is an energy-window preparation, not a zero-width surface measure. This postulate makes no existence claim for that specific band when those theorem hypotheses fail.
3. For particle exchange, use the countable-sector grand preparation of [[post-csm-grand-preparation]]. Its full dimensionless activity is the fugacity $z_{\rm ph}:=e^{\beta_{\rm phys}\mu}>0$, where $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and the chemical potential $\mu$ is in J per particle. When matching positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ at inverse temperature $b$, choose $z_{\rm ph}=z/\kappa_b$, as in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]].

These laws are adopted statistical preparations. They do not follow from Hamiltonian energy conservation, do not assert that any isolated dynamics reaches these distributions, and do not encode an experimental observation. The band sequence is the particular controlled shrinking window constructed conditionally by [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]].

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **ultrafilter extension principle** says that every filter on a set is contained in an ultrafilter on that set ([[def-ultrafilter]]).

It is also called the **ultrafilter lemma** and is equivalent over ZF to the Boolean prime ideal theorem, abbreviated BPI. Items below write **assume UL/BPI** precisely when they use this extension principle; they do not thereby assume the full axiom of choice.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[def-function]],
> [[def-natural-numbers]]) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** [[def-choice-function]] and
[[def-axiom-of-choice]] select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and [[def-countable-choice]] does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ ([[def-power-set]], [[def-cartesian-product]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]); a natural is the set of its predecessors ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. Their graphs are nested. By induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. The dimensionless positional energy $U_{L,bc}$ is the physical pair energy divided by $E_0$, with $bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$ and the exact image convention above. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $Q_i$ be probability measures on $X_i$, and let $P$ be a probability on $\prod_{i=1}^mX_i$. Write $P_i$ for its $i$th marginal and use the directional extended relative entropy $D(\cdot\Vert\cdot)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Q_m)\geq\sum_{i=1}^mD(P_i\Vert Q_i).$$
If the left side is finite, the conditional chain rule gives the stronger equality
$$D(P\Vert\textstyle\bigotimes_iQ_i)=D(P_1\Vert Q_1)+\sum_{i=2}^m E_P\,D(P_{X_i\mid X_1,\ldots,X_{i-1}}\Vert Q_i),$$
and each conditional increment is at least $D(P_i\Vert Q_i)$. If the left side is infinite, the displayed inequality is understood in the extended order and is automatic. This applies to finitely many disjoint spatial blocks after their particle counts and positions have been fixed; zero-occupancy blocks contribute zero.

derivations.claim: Under $A_N$, $X_1=1$ surely and the remaining coordinates retain their independent Bernoulli-$\theta$ law. The likelihood $dA_N/dP_N$ is $1/\theta$ on $\{X_1=1\}$ and zero elsewhere, so integration gives $D(A_N\Vert P_N)=\log(1/\theta)$. Equivalently, [F1] decomposes the divergence into $D(\delta_1\Vert\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\theta))=\log(1/\theta)$ and a zero conditional remainder. Dividing by $N$ gives vanishing entropy density.

Under $A_N$, $H_N=\epsilon(1+Y_N)$ with $Y_N$ binomial $(N-1,\theta)$. Since $Y_N$ is the sum of $N-1$ independent Bernoulli coordinates, $E Y_N=(N-1)\theta$ and $\operatorname{Var}(Y_N)=(N-1)\theta(1-\theta)$, by expanding the mean and variance and using zero cross-covariances. Thus $E(H_N/N)=\epsilon[1+(N-1)\theta]/N\to\epsilon\theta$ and $\operatorname{Var}(H_N/N)=\epsilon^2(N-1)\theta(1-\theta)/N^2\to0$. For any $\eta>0$, $1_{\{|H_N/N-E(H_N/N)|\geq\eta\}}\leq(H_N/N-E(H_N/N))^2/\eta^2$; integrating gives the Chebyshev bound and convergence in probability. Its Shannon entropy is $(N-1)h(\theta)/N\to h(\theta)$, where $h(\theta)=-\theta\log\theta-(1-\theta)\log(1-\theta)$. Yet the first coordinate remains one and is at total-variation distance $1-\theta$ from Bernoulli$(\theta)$. This proves all claims and refutes the statement.

By second-order stationarity,
$\mathbb E|V(t)|^2=\sum_i C_{ii}(0)=\mathbb E|V(0)|^2$ for every $t$.
Tonelli applied to the nonnegative jointly measurable function $|V|^2$
therefore gives
$\mathbb E\int_0^T|V(s)|^2\,ds=T\mathbb E|V(0)|^2<\infty$.
Consequently the path integral of $|V|^2$ is finite almost surely; [F4] on
$[0,T]$ then makes $V$ pathwise integrable. Moreover,
$|X(T)|^2\le T\int_0^T|V(s)|^2ds$, so $X(T)\in L^2$.

The bound in step 1.1 and Cauchy–Schwarz in probability give
$\mathbb E\int_0^T|V(s)|\,ds\le T(\mathbb E|V(0)|^2)^{1/2}<\infty$.
Fubini and $\mathbb E[V(s)]=0$ therefore give $\mathbb E[X(T)]=0$.
For each $i,j$, [F4] and stationarity give
$\mathbb E|V_i(u)V_j(v)|\le\mathbb E|V(0)|^2$ on the finite square
$[0,T]^2$. Fubini therefore permits expansion of
$\mathbb E[X_i(T)X_j(T)]$ as the double integral of
$\mathbb E[V_i(u)V_j(v)]$. Splitting the square into $u\le v$ and $v\le u$,
then writing $s=|v-u|$, gives the two terms
$\int_0^T(T-s)C_{ij}(s)ds$ and
$\int_0^T(T-s)C_{ji}(s)ds$. Since the means are zero, this is the stated
covariance formula.

$\frac12\mathbf1_{[0,T]}(s)(1-s/T)(C_{ij}(s)+C_{ji}(s))$. As $T\to\infty$
it converges pointwise to $\frac12(C_{ij}(s)+C_{ji}(s))$ and is bounded by
the integrable function
$\frac12(|C_{ij}(s)|+|C_{ji}(s)|)$. By [F2], each matrix entry converges to
the stated integral.

$a^\top\operatorname{Cov}(X(T))a/(2T)\ge0$ because it is a scaled variance.
Entrywise convergence from step 3.1 gives
$a^\top Da=\lim_{T\to\infty}a^\top\operatorname{Cov}(X(T))a/(2T)\ge0$.

Then

$$u(t)\le a(t)+\int_{t_0}^t a(s)b(s)\exp\!\left(\int_s^t b(r)\,dr\right)ds.$$

If $a$ is nondecreasing, this gives $u(t)\le a(t)\exp(\int_{t_0}^t b)$. The time-reflected form assumes $u(t)\le a(t)+\int_t^{t_0}b(s)u(s)\,ds$ for $t\le t_0$. In particular, when $a=A\ge0$ and $b=B\ge0$ are constant, the two orientations give $u(t)\le A e^{B|t-t_0|}$.

derivations.claim: If $a=b$, the only time is the prescribed initial time and the solution map is the identity, so the claims hold. Otherwise lift $G$ periodically to $\widetilde G:J\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and write $z=(x,v)$ and $B(t,z)=(v,\widetilde G(t,x))$. On every compact time interval and bounded state ball, $B$ is continuous, bounded and Lipschitz in state because $D_xG$ is bounded. Thus [F1] gives unique local solutions. Along any such solution, if $M:=\sup_{I\times\mathbb T^d}|G|$, then $|V(t)-v_0|\le M|t-a|$ and $|X(t)-x_0-(t-a)v_0|\le M|t-a|^2/2$ for lifted positions. Hence a solution on a finite subinterval of $I$ remains in one bounded state cylinder. On a slightly larger cylinder the field has one finite bound and one finite state-Lipschitz constant, so the quantitative [F1] time estimate gives a common positive continuation length for every point of the trajectory. Finitely many such equal-length continuations cover $I$. Uniqueness on overlaps from [F1] gives one solution on all of $I$.

Fix a compact subinterval and a base state $z_0$. The bound on $D_zB$ and [F2] give $|z(t,z_0+h)-z(t,z_0)|\le C|h|$ uniformly in $t$ for small $h$. In the integral equations, set $\Delta_h(t):=z(t,z_0+h)-z(t,z_0)$ and $A_h(t):=\int_0^1D_zB\bigl(t,z(t,z_0)+\theta\Delta_h(t)\bigr)\,d\theta.$ Then $\Delta_h(t)=h+\int_a^t A_h(s)\Delta_h(s)\,ds$. Uniform continuity of $D_zB$ on the compact time interval and torus gives $A_h\to A:=D_zB(t,z(t,z_0))$ uniformly in $t$. The linear integral equation $J(t)=I+\int_a^t A(s)J(s)\,ds$ has a unique solution by the same Picard iteration as [F1]. Subtracting it from the equation for $\Delta_h$, applying [F2], and using $\sup_t\|A_h-A\|\to0$ proves $\sup_t|\Delta_h(t)-J(t)h|/|h|\to0$. Thus $D_{z_0}z(t,z_0)=J(t)$ and it satisfies $\dot J=D_zB(t,z(t,z_0))J$, $J(a)=I$. Since $D_zB$ is bounded uniformly in state, [F2] also gives $\sup_{t\in I,z_0}\|J(t,z_0)\|<\infty$.

For each $r\ge2$, the candidate $r$-th state derivative $J_r$ satisfies the linear variational equation $\dot J_r=D_zB(t,z)J_r+\sum_{\substack{\pi\text{ a partition of }\{1,\ldots,r\}\\|\pi|\ge2}}D_z^{|\pi|}B(t,z)\bigl[J_{|C_1|},\ldots,J_{|C_{|\pi|}|}\bigr],\qquad J_r(a)=0,$ where $C_1,\ldots,C_{|\pi|}$ are the blocks of $\pi$ and $z=z(t,z_0)$. The coefficient and all higher derivatives of $B$ are bounded uniformly in state. By induction, the forcing term is therefore bounded uniformly over initial states; [F2] gives a unique $J_r$ with a uniform finite-time bound. Applying the difference-quotient argument of step 1.2 to the equation for $J_{r-1}$, using uniform continuity of each $D_z^jB$ on the compact time interval and periodic state variable for $j\le r$, shows that this $J_r$ is its derivative. Induction proves smooth dependence and the asserted uniform bounds. Solving the same system backward in time gives the inverse map, and uniqueness makes the two maps inverse. If $B$ is also smooth in time, $\partial_tz=B(t,z)$ and the state-jet equations give every mixed time-state derivative by repeated chain rule.

boundaries.evidence: N=1 is permitted: the interaction sum is empty and the flow is free streaming, covered by the bounded-force continuation1.1. The phase space itself is nonempty for d>=1,L>0; normalized initial density excludes a zero-mass law.
Statement: the proof remain valid when W is constant, so K=0; the finite flow is free and the Liouville density is transported.
Statement: the proof covers N=1: the interaction sum is empty, and the complete flow is free motion on the torus times Euclidean momentum.

Statement and the proof assert the flow and transport for every real t, including t=0 and both signs of time.
