If $D$ is exterior-measurable, properness gives $\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_D f\mid\xi)=\mathbf1_D(\xi)\gamma_\Delta(f\mid\xi)$. For a bounded cylinder function $f$ depending only on spins in $\Delta\cup C_\Delta$, the kernel depends on the remaining exterior only through $C_\Delta$, so for every finite-boundary assignment $\eta$, $$\int_{Q_\eta} f\,d\mu=\mu(Q_\eta)\sum_{\sigma_\Delta}\gamma_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)f(\sigma_\Delta\eta).$$ Apply this identity to the diagonal cylinder function $f=\operatorname{diag}(A e^{itH_\Delta^\eta/\hbar}Be^{-itH_\Delta^\eta/\hbar})$. Summing the displayed identities over the finitely many boundary assignments gives, for real $t$, $$\omega_\mu(A\alpha_t(B))=\sum_{\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{C_\Delta}}\mu(Q_\eta)\operatorname{Tr}_\Delta\!\left(\rho_\Delta^\eta A e^{itH_\Delta^\eta/\hbar}Be^{-itH_\Delta^\eta/\hbar}\right).$$

Summing over $\sigma$ and using $\sum_\sigma P_\sigma=I_\Delta$ shows that the constant is $\mu_\omega(Q_\eta Q_\zeta)/Z_\Delta^\eta$, including when this numerator is zero. Therefore $$\mu_\omega(P_\sigma Q_\eta Q_\zeta)=\gamma_\Delta(\sigma\mid\eta)\,\mu_\omega(Q_\eta Q_\zeta).$$

Step 2.2 identifies its boundaries with $\omega_\mu(A\alpha_t(B))$ and $\omega_\mu(\alpha_t(B)A)$, proving the KMS condition for local pairs.

Every exterior cylinder event is a finite disjoint union of events $Q_\eta Q_\zeta$ after refining it to specify all spins in $C_\Delta$. [F10] states that every lambda-system containing a pi-system contains its generated sigma-algebra, hence the two measures agree on that sigma-algebra. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $D=\dim H\ge1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. With composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity and the induced operator norm, $\mathcal B(H)$ is a nonzero unital complex C*-algebra in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. In particular it is complete, $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\|B\|$, $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$, $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ and $\|I\|=1$. The matrix $\|A\|^2I-A^*A$ is positive semidefinite and has a positive square root in $\mathcal B(H)$.

Every complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal B(H)\to\mathbb C$ that is positive, meaning $\omega(B^*B)\ge0$ for all $B$, has a unique positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ such that $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ for all $A$. It is bounded and satisfies

$$|\omega(A)|\le\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)\|A\|\quad(A\in\mathcal B(H)),\qquad \|\omega\|=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=\omega(I).$$

Consequently the canonical states of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]] are exactly the trace pairings of density operators of [[def-qc-density-operator]]; for a positive functional, normalization $\omega(I)=1$ is equivalent to norm one. The result includes zero positive functionals, nonfaithful densities and $D=1$; it makes no infinite-dimensional density representation assertion.

Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, the finite spin dimension $q\ge1$, the local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z=\max_{x,y\in Z}d_\infty(x,y)$; for finite nonempty $X,Y\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)=\min_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_\infty(x,y)$.

A **uniformly bounded finite-range interaction** is a family $\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_Z$, indexed by finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, such that $\Phi(Z)^*=\Phi(Z)$ and there are an integer $M\ge1$, a finite $R\ge0$, and $\kappa<\infty$ satisfying

$$\Phi(Z)=0\quad\text{if }|Z|>M\text{ or }\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z>R,\qquad\kappa:=\sup_{x\in\Gamma}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\Phi(Z)\|<\infty.$$

The norm in this sum is the operator norm in the local matrix algebra $\mathcal A_Z$. If a model lists several terms with the same support, first add them in that local algebra; the resulting single operator is $\Phi(Z)$, and $\kappa$ uses its norm. Thus no multiplicity is implicit.

For a finite region $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, define the **free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian** by summing only terms whose complete support lies inside $\Lambda$; terms meeting $\Lambda$ but extending outside it are omitted:

$$H_\Lambda:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_\Lambda.$$

It is a finite sum of self-adjoint matrices. For a fixed scale $\hbar>0$ and any finite $\Omega\supseteq\Lambda$, embed $H_\Lambda$ in $\mathcal A_\Omega$ by the canonical factor inclusion and define

$$\alpha_t^\Lambda(A):=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Omega,\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

These actions are compatible as $\Omega$ increases, because the extra tensor factors carry the identity. On $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ this is the ordinary finite matrix Heisenberg dynamics.

In physical SI bookkeeping, when $\Phi(Z)$ is interpreted as an energy, $\Phi(Z)$, $\kappa$, and $H_\Lambda$ have units J, $t$ has units s, and $\hbar$ is the adopted reduced Planck constant with units J s. The mathematics below uses only $\hbar>0$ and asserts no measured parameter value.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its norm completion as in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. These assumptions give the conditional unital C*-algebra structure supplied by [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]].

For any increasing finite exhaustion $(\Lambda_n)_{n\ge1}$ in the convention of [[lem-qsm-boundary-dynamics-cauchy]]—that is, each $\Lambda_n$ is finite, $\Lambda_n\subseteq\Lambda_{n+1}$, and $\bigcup_{n\ge1}\Lambda_n=\mathbb Z^d$—the free-boundary finite-volume maps $\alpha_t^{\Lambda_n}$ converge in norm on every local observable, uniformly for $t$ in compact intervals. Their limit is independent of the exhaustion and extends uniquely to a strongly continuous one-parameter group $\alpha_t$ of maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$. Here “one-parameter group” means $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$. Each $\alpha_t$ is a bijective complex-linear unital $*$-homomorphism (a $*$-automorphism), with inverse $\alpha_{-t}$. Strong continuity means $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for every fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. This result does not assert that an infinite-volume Hamiltonian is an element of $\mathcal A$ or a bounded operator on a preselected infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, have finite on-site spin dimension $q\ge1$ and quasi-local spin algebra $\mathcal A$. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction with free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonians, and let $\alpha_t$ be the strongly continuous thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. Fix $\beta>0$ and $\hbar>0$. Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity, and the finite-matrix state/density-norm interface exactly as stated in Facts [A1]–[A2].

For any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\Gamma$, extend each finite Gibbs density on $\mathcal A_{\Lambda_n}$ by normalized trace densities on the outside sites, as in [[lem-qsm-gibbs-strip-limit]]. Every pointwise convergent subsequence of these algebraic states has a limit $\omega$ that is a $\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time, with strip width $\beta\hbar$. At least one such subsequential limit exists under [A1]–[A2].

The conclusion is a conditional mathematical existence result for bounded finite-dimensional spin interactions. It does not assert uniqueness, clustering, phase classification, a global infinite-volume Gibbs density matrix, or dynamical relaxation to equilibrium.

Let $d\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and let $\Phi$ be a translation-invariant uniformly bounded finite-range interaction as in [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. For each finite nonempty $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, let $H_\Lambda$ be its free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian, $Z_\Lambda(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(e^{-\beta H_\Lambda})$, and $p_\Lambda(\beta)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$, where $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}$ is the ordinary finite-matrix trace of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Fix $\beta>0$, measured in inverse joules when the interaction terms are assigned energy units.

Write $d_\infty(x,y):=\max_{1\le j\le d}|x_j-y_j|$ for the lattice metric of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For a finite $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $x\in\Lambda$, define $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$. A sequence of finite nonempty regions $(\Lambda_n)$ is van Hove if $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed integer $r\ge0$, the inner boundary $\partial_r\Lambda_n:=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$ satisfies $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$. Then $p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)$ converges to the same finite value $p_\Phi(\beta)$ for every van Hove sequence; in particular, for positive integers $L$, the cube limit for $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ exists and equals this value. The normalization is dimensionless log-partition per lattice site; the finite-volume Helmholtz free energy per site is $-\beta^{-1}p_\Lambda(\beta)$.

If $B_\Lambda=B_\Lambda^*$ is any finite-volume boundary perturbation with $\|B_{\Lambda_n}\|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$, replacing $H_{\Lambda_n}$ by $H_{\Lambda_n}+B_{\Lambda_n}$ leaves the same pressure limit. This theorem makes no claim for changes to the bulk interaction.

An **infinite spin state** is a bounded positive normalized functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with local density matrices $\rho_\Lambda$ specified by $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(\rho_\Lambda A)$ for $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, as in [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. A bounded local observable is an element of some $\mathcal A_\Lambda$; a measurement observable is self-adjoint. Its model expectation is $\omega(A)$, real for self-adjoint $A$. For ordered bounded local observables $A_1,\ldots,A_n$, define the ordered correlation $C_\omega(A_1,\ldots,A_n):=\omega(A_1\cdots A_n)$. It may be complex when the product is not self-adjoint, depends on the order when observables do not commute, and has the product of their assigned units. The state functional is dimensionless on dimensionless operators; if $A$ has an assigned unit, $\omega(A)$ has that same unit.

Within this formulation, primitive model inputs are the dimensionless integers $d,q$, the lattice spacing $a$, the positive constants $\hbar,k_B$, the temperature $T$, and the interaction coefficients $\Phi$ (or $J_{ij},h_i$ in the diagonal Ising submodel). The inverse temperature, finite Hamiltonians, partition functions, pressure/free-energy/entropy/energy densities, and state correlations are derived constructions under their stated hypotheses. The Born probability interpretation and the identification of KMS states with physical equilibrium are adopted separately; neither follows from this mathematical definition.

In SI bookkeeping, $a$ is measured in metres, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and $T>0$ in kelvins. The finite-range interaction coefficients are specified inputs; a term $\Phi(Z)$ has units joules when interpreted as energy. The dimensionless local spin matrices (including the Pauli matrices in the spin-$\tfrac12$ submodel) do not by themselves identify a magnetic moment or an applied field. In a term $-h_i Z_i$, $h_i$ is an energy coefficient in joules; any identification with a laboratory field or magnetic moment requires a separate coupling and calibration model. No numerical parameter value is specified here.

The inverse-temperature parameter is the derived quantity $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, in joules$^{-1}$. For finite $\Lambda$, the free-boundary Hamiltonian $H_\Lambda=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)$ and the finite partition function $Z_\Lambda(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(e^{-\beta H_\Lambda})$ are defined by [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] and [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. When $\Phi$ is an energy interaction, $H_\Lambda$ is in joules, $\beta H_\Lambda$ is dimensionless, and $Z_\Lambda$ is positive and dimensionless. The finite-volume Gibbs density $\rho_{\Lambda,\beta}=e^{-\beta H_\Lambda}/Z_\Lambda$ is a finite-region density matrix; it is not an asserted density matrix on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

For $t$ in seconds, the finite-volume Heisenberg evolution is $\alpha_t^\Lambda(A)=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}$. The thermodynamic dynamics $\alpha_t$ exists under the exact hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. The $\beta$-KMS criterion for this dynamics uses a bounded continuous strip function with lower edge $\omega(A\alpha_t(B))$, upper edge $\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)$, and imaginary-time width $\beta\hbar$ seconds, exactly as in [[def-qsm-kms-state]]. This is a mathematical state criterion; no global infinite-volume Gibbs trace is part of the definition.

For $x,y\in\mathbb Z^d$, write $d_\infty(x,y):=\max_{1\le j\le d}|x_j-y_j|$. For a finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $x\in\Lambda$, define $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$, using the convention of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]]. The minimum exists because the complement is nonempty and its distances from $x$ are positive integers. For a translation-invariant interaction $\Phi$ of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]] and finite nonempty $\Lambda$, define the finite-volume dimensionless log-partition per site by $p_\Lambda(\beta):=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. A sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ is van Hove here when $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and for each fixed integer $r\ge0$, the inner boundary $\partial_r\Lambda_n=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$ satisfies $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$. Under the precise finite-range and translation-invariance assumptions of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]], the common finite limit is $p_\Phi(\beta):=\lim_n p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)$. It is dimensionless per lattice site, not a pressure in pascals. Define the finite-volume free energy per site $f_\Lambda(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}p_\Lambda(\beta)$ and the thermodynamic free energy per site $f_\Phi(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}p_\Phi(\beta)=-k_BT\,p_\Phi(\beta)$, in joules per site. Dividing by the model cell volume $a^d$ gives a free-energy density in joules per cubic metre when $d=3$; this fixed-lattice quantity does not by itself define a mechanical equation of state or pressure in pascals.

A state is **spatially translation invariant** when $\omega(\tau_x(A))=\omega(A)$ for every $x\in\mathbb Z^d$ and local $A$, with $\tau_x$ as defined in [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. For such a state, let $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ and define the dimensionless cube entropy per site
$$s(\omega):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{-\operatorname{Tr}_{Q_L}(\rho_{Q_L}\log\rho_{Q_L})}{L^d},\qquad 0\log0:=0.$$
Under Countable Choice and the full Axiom of Choice [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]], the exact entropy-density supplier [[lem-qsm-stationary-spin-entropy-density]] establishes that this limit exists for every such state and equals the infimum over positive integer cube sides. These thermodynamic limits are restricted to the supplier's stated assumptions and do not assert that a prepared physical material realizes a translation-invariant state.

For a finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $x\in\Lambda$, define $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$, using the convention of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]]. The minimum exists because the complement is nonempty and its distances from $x$ are positive integers. For a translation-invariant interaction $\Phi$ of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]] and finite nonempty $\Lambda$, define the finite-volume dimensionless log-partition per site by $p_\Lambda(\beta):=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. A sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ is van Hove here when $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and for each fixed integer $r\ge0$, the inner boundary $\partial_r\Lambda_n=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$ satisfies $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$. It is dimensionless per lattice site, not a pressure in pascals. Dividing by the model cell volume $a^d$ gives a free-energy density in joules per cubic metre when $d=3$; this fixed-lattice quantity does not by itself define a mechanical equation of state or pressure in pascals.

A state is **spatially translation invariant** when $\omega(\tau_x(A))=\omega(A)$ for every $x\in\mathbb Z^d$ and local $A$, with $\tau_x$ as defined in [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. For such a state, let $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ and define the dimensionless cube entropy per site
$$s(\omega):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{-\operatorname{Tr}_{Q_L}(\rho_{Q_L}\log\rho_{Q_L})}{L^d},\qquad 0\log0:=0.$$
Under Countable Choice and the full Axiom of Choice [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]], the exact entropy-density supplier [[lem-qsm-stationary-spin-entropy-density]] establishes that this limit exists for every such state and equals the infimum over positive integer cube sides. The corresponding physical entropy density is $k_Bs(\omega)/a^d$, in joules per kelvin per cubic metre for $d=3$. For the translation-invariant finite-range energy interaction, the same supplier defines the energy density per site $u_\Phi(\omega)=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\omega(\Phi(S))$; it is in joules per site when $\Phi$ is an energy interaction, and $u_\Phi(\omega)/a^d$ is the energy density per physical volume in $d=3$. These thermodynamic limits are restricted to the supplier's stated assumptions and do not assert that a prepared physical material realizes a translation-invariant state.

Adopt, for this bounded finite-dimensional quantum spin model, the following physical interpretation and equilibrium rule. A prepared state is a positive normalized functional $\omega$ on the quasi-local observable algebra of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. The model assigns the Born probability $\omega(P)$ to a local projective-measurement outcome represented by a projection $P\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$; the probabilities of the mutually orthogonal spectral projections of a finite-region self-adjoint observable sum to one. For a physical equilibrium preparation at temperature $T>0$, adopt as the model's equilibrium criterion that $\omega$ is a $\beta$-KMS state for the thermodynamic dynamics $\alpha_t$, with $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and the physical-time strip of width $\beta\hbar$ seconds as in [[def-qsm-kms-state]]. This is an adopted model postulate, not a deduction from the algebraic state definition or from the finite-volume Gibbs identity.

The postulate does not claim that an actual material has the specified interaction parameters, that a system dynamically relaxes to a KMS state, that equilibrium is unique, or that an apparatus realizes a specified projective measurement. It reports no experiment or measured value. Finite-volume approximations, when used, remain distinct from the infinite-volume state and its local restrictions.

Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, $d\geq1$, a translation-invariant symmetric pair coupling $J_{i+k,j+k}=J_{ij}$ with $J_{ij}=0$ for $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$ for some finite $R$, a constant finite field $h_i=h\in\mathbb R$, and $\beta>0$, in the diagonal model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]]. If
$$\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\sum_{j\ne i}\tanh(\beta|J_{ij}|)<1,$$
then the full quasi-local matrix algebra has exactly one $\beta$-KMS state. This strict influence bound is sufficient, not sharp. For homogeneous nearest-neighbor coupling $J$, it reduces to $2d\tanh(\beta|J|)<1$. The result is for the longitudinal diagonal interaction and makes no transverse-field claim.

Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, $d=1$, finite $\beta>0$, $\hbar>0$, a uniform field $h_i=h\in\mathbb R$, and nearest-neighbor couplings $J_{i,i+1}=J_{i+1,i}=J\in\mathbb R$ with all other pair couplings zero, in the diagonal model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]]. Then the full quasi-local matrix algebra has exactly one $\beta$-KMS state. The conclusion concerns the longitudinal diagonal Ising chain; no transverse-field term is included.

Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, $d=2$, uniform nearest-neighbor coupling $J>0$, zero field, $\beta J\geq2$, and $\hbar>0$, in the diagonal spin-$\tfrac12$ model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]]. Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, a finite on-site dimension $q\ge1$, a lattice spacing $a>0$ metres, and finite-region Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ and matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. The observable algebra is the norm completion $\mathcal A$ of the directed union of the local algebras, as in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. An **infinite spin state** is a bounded positive normalized functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with local density matrices $\rho_\Lambda$ specified by $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(\rho_\Lambda A)$ for $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, as in [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. A bounded local observable is an element of some $\mathcal A_\Lambda$; a measurement observable is self-adjoint. Its model expectation is $\omega(A)$, real for self-adjoint $A$. For ordered bounded local observables $A_1,\ldots,A_n$, define the ordered correlation $C_\omega(A_1,\ldots,A_n):=\omega(A_1\cdots A_n)$. It may be complex when the product is not self-adjoint, depends on the order when observables do not commute, and has the product of their assigned units. The state functional is dimensionless on dimensionless operators; if $A$ has an assigned unit, $\omega(A)$ has that same unit.

Within this formulation, primitive model inputs are the dimensionless integers $d,q$, the lattice spacing $a$, the positive constants $\hbar,k_B$, the temperature $T$, and the interaction coefficients $\Phi$ (or $J_{ij},h_i$ in the diagonal Ising submodel). The inverse temperature, finite Hamiltonians, partition functions, pressure/free-energy/entropy/energy densities, and state correlations are derived constructions under their stated hypotheses. The Born probability interpretation and the identification of KMS states with physical equilibrium are adopted separately; neither follows from this mathematical definition.

In SI bookkeeping, $a$ is measured in metres, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and $T>0$ in kelvins. The finite-range interaction coefficients are specified inputs; a term $\Phi(Z)$ has units joules when interpreted as energy. The dimensionless local spin matrices (including the Pauli matrices in the spin-$\tfrac12$ submodel) do not by themselves identify a magnetic moment or an applied field. In a term $-h_i Z_i$, $h_i$ is an energy coefficient in joules; any identification with a laboratory field or magnetic moment requires a separate coupling and calibration model. No numerical parameter value is specified here.

The inverse-temperature parameter is the derived quantity $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, in joules$^{-1}$. For finite $\Lambda$, the free-boundary Hamiltonian $H_\Lambda=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)$ and the finite partition function $Z_\Lambda(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(e^{-\beta H_\Lambda})$ are defined by [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] and [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. When $\Phi$ is an energy interaction, $H_\Lambda$ is in joules, $\beta H_\Lambda$ is dimensionless, and $Z_\Lambda$ is positive and dimensionless. The finite-volume Gibbs density $\rho_{\Lambda,\beta}=e^{-\beta H_\Lambda}/Z_\Lambda$ is a finite-region density matrix; it is not an asserted density matrix on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

For $t$ in seconds, the finite-volume Heisenberg evolution is $\alpha_t^\Lambda(A)=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}$. The thermodynamic dynamics $\alpha_t$ exists under the exact hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. The $\beta$-KMS criterion for this dynamics uses a bounded continuous strip function with lower edge $\omega(A\alpha_t(B))$, upper edge $\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)$, and imaginary-time width $\beta\hbar$ seconds, exactly as in [[def-qsm-kms-state]]. This is a mathematical state criterion; no global infinite-volume Gibbs trace is part of the definition.

For $x,y\in\mathbb Z^d$, write $d_\infty(x,y):=\max_{1\le j\le d}|x_j-y_j|$. For a finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $x\in\Lambda$, define $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$, using the convention of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]]. The minimum exists because the complement is nonempty and its distances from $x$ are positive integers. For a translation-invariant interaction $\Phi$ of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]] and finite nonempty $\Lambda$, define the finite-volume dimensionless log-partition per site by $p_\Lambda(\beta):=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. A sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ is van Hove here when $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and for each fixed integer $r\ge0$, the inner boundary $\partial_r\Lambda_n=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$ satisfies $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$. Under the precise finite-range and translation-invariance assumptions of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]], the common finite limit is $p_\Phi(\beta):=\lim_n p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)$. It is dimensionless per lattice site, not a pressure in pascals. Define the finite-volume free energy per site $f_\Lambda(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}p_\Lambda(\beta)$ and the thermodynamic free energy per site $f_\Phi(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}p_\Phi(\beta)=-k_BT\,p_\Phi(\beta)$, in joules per site. Dividing by the model cell volume $a^d$ gives a free-energy density in joules per cubic metre when $d=3$; this fixed-lattice quantity does not by itself define a mechanical equation of state or pressure in pascals.

A state is **spatially translation invariant** when $\omega(\tau_x(A))=\omega(A)$ for every $x\in\mathbb Z^d$ and local $A$, with $\tau_x$ as defined in [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. For such a state, let $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ and define the dimensionless cube entropy per site
$$s(\omega):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{-\operatorname{Tr}_{Q_L}(\rho_{Q_L}\log\rho_{Q_L})}{L^d},\qquad 0\log0:=0.$$
Under Countable Choice and the full Axiom of Choice [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]], the exact entropy-density supplier [[lem-qsm-stationary-spin-entropy-density]] establishes that this limit exists for every such state and equals the infimum over positive integer cube sides. The corresponding physical entropy density is $k_Bs(\omega)/a^d$, in joules per kelvin per cubic metre for $d=3$. For the translation-invariant finite-range energy interaction, the same supplier defines the energy density per site $u_\Phi(\omega)=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\omega(\Phi(S))$; it is in joules per site when $\Phi$ is an energy interaction, and $u_\Phi(\omega)/a^d$ is the energy density per physical volume in $d=3$. These thermodynamic limits are restricted to the supplier's stated assumptions and do not assert that a prepared physical material realizes a translation-invariant state.

Adopt the model and units of [[def-qsm-infinite-spin-physical-quantities]] and the equilibrium criterion of [[post-qsm-infinite-spin-equilibrium]]. Let $T>0$, $k_B>0$, and $\hbar>0$. Let $Z_i$ be the dimensionless Pauli matrix with eigenvalues $\pm1$ at site $i$, and let the diagonal spin-$\tfrac12$ Ising interaction of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]] have symmetric energy coefficients $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$ and fields $h_i$ in joules, finite range, and a uniform per-site bound. Thus
$$H_\Lambda=-\sum_{i\in\Lambda}h_iZ_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda}J_{ij}Z_iZ_j,$$
with each unordered internal pair counted once. Here $|i-j|_1:=\sum_{k=1}^d|i_k-j_k|$ is the lattice $\ell^1$ distance, and $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$.

1. **Sufficient high-temperature uniqueness.** For translation-invariant symmetric pair couplings, a constant finite field $h_i=h$, and
$$\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\sum_{j\ne i}\tanh\!\left(\frac{|J_{ij}|}{k_BT}\right)<1,$$
the full quasi-local algebra has exactly one $\beta$-KMS state. In the homogeneous nearest-neighbor model this sufficient condition is $2d\tanh(|J|/(k_BT))<1$.

2. **One-dimensional uniqueness.** For $d=1$, uniform nearest-neighbor coupling $J\in\mathbb R$ and constant finite field $h$, every $T>0$ gives exactly one full-algebra $\beta$-KMS state.

3. **Two-dimensional sufficient coexistence.** For $d=2$, uniform nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic coupling $J>0$, zero field, and $T\le J/(2k_B)$, there are at least two distinct spatially translation-invariant full-algebra $\beta$-KMS states $\omega_+$ and $\omega_-$ with opposite nonzero dimensionless magnetizations $\omega_+(Z_i)\ge m_*>0$ and $\omega_-(Z_i)\le-m_*<0$. Here spatial translation invariance means $\omega(\tau_x(A))=\omega(A)$ for every local $A$ and $x\in\mathbb Z^2$, with $\tau_x$ from [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. Put $K=\beta J$, $r=3e^{-2K}$, $\delta(K)=\frac43\frac{r^4(5-4r)}{(1-r)^2}$, and $m_*=1-2\delta(K)$. This is a sufficient coexistence bound; $T=J/(2k_B)$ is not asserted to be the critical temperature, the states are not asserted to be extremal, and no transverse-field result follows.

For the same two-dimensional model with uniform coupling $J$ and variable uniform longitudinal energy coefficient $h$, put
$$H_\Lambda(h)=-J\sum_{\substack{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda\\|i-j|_1=1}}Z_iZ_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}Z_i,$$
where each internal unordered nearest-neighbor pair is counted once. At fixed $\beta$, let $\Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2$ and define the dimensionless log-partition pressure per site
$$p_\beta(h):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n|}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}\!\left(e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}(h)}\right).$$
Under the stated coexistence condition this limit exists, is not differentiable at $h=0$, and satisfies $(p_\beta(h)-p_\beta(0))/h\ge\beta m_*$ for every $h>0$ and $(p_\beta(h)-p_\beta(0))/h\le-\beta m_*$ for every $h<0$. The $p_\beta$ here is dimensionless per site, not a mechanical pressure in pascals.

derivations.claim: The displayed Hamiltonian is the homogeneous nearest-neighbor specialization of the diagonal interaction in [F1], with each unordered internal edge counted once and the field term once per site. Its energy coefficients have units joules, so $\beta J=J/(k_BT)$ and $\beta h=h/(k_BT)$ are dimensionless.

In $d=1$, [F1] applies for every finite $J,h$ and $T>0$. In $d=2$, substitution of the $2d=4$ nearest-neighbor terms into the strict row-sum criterion yields the sufficient high-temperature condition in the Example, while $\beta J\ge2$ is equivalent to $T\le J/(2k_B)$ and gives the sufficient coexistence condition. Thus the three displayed regimes follow from [F1], and parameters outside these sufficient conditions receive no conclusion here.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in H$ write $v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1}\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=v_{\pi^{-1}(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n-1)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$ have a repeated factor, that is, $v_i=v_j$ for some distinct $i,j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, then $P_-(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=0$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: The tensor factors and product pairing in the Definition are supplied by [F1]. For every $n\ge1$, [F2] makes $P_\pm^{(n)}$ an orthogonal projection. The range of an orthogonal projection is closed: if $P x_k=x_k$ and $x_k\to x$, boundedness of $P$ gives $P x=\lim_k P x_k=\lim_k x_k=x$. Therefore each $\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}$ is a closed subspace of the complete tensor Hilbert space and is itself complete.

For $\psi,\varphi\in\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h)$, Cauchy–Schwarz for the square-summable nonnegative sequences $(\|\psi_n\|)_n$ and $(\|\varphi_n\|)_n$ gives
$\sum_n|\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle|\le(\sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_n\|\varphi_n\|^2)^{1/2}<\infty$. Hence the displayed pairing converges absolutely, is sesquilinear, and is positive definite because $\langle\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2=0$ forces every coordinate to vanish.

Let $(\psi^{(k)})_k$ be Cauchy in this norm. For each fixed $n$, $(\psi_n^{(k)})_k$ is Cauchy in the complete sector $\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}$, so it converges to some $\psi_n\in\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}$. If $k\ge K$ and $\|\psi^{(k)}-\psi^{(m)}\|\le\varepsilon$ for all $m\ge K$, then for every finite $N$, passing $m\to\infty$ in the finite sum yields $\sum_{n\le N}\|\psi_n-\psi_n^{(k)}\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$. Also $\sum_{n\le N}\|\psi_n\|^2\le2\|\psi^{(k)}\|^2+2\varepsilon^2$. Taking suprema over finite $N$ proves $\sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty$, so $\psi\in\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h)$, and then $\|\psi^{(k)}-\psi\|\le\varepsilon$ for all $k\ge K$. Thus the direct sum is complete.

For $\psi\in\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h)$, truncating after sector $N$ changes its squared norm by $\sum_{n>N}\|\psi_n\|^2\to0$. Therefore the finite-particle subspace is dense and $\Omega$ is a unit vector.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $I$ be a specified finite or countably infinite
mode set with a fixed enumeration, and let $\mathfrak h=\ell^2(I)$ have its
coordinate orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\in I}$. Put
$\mathfrak h^{\otimes 0}=\mathbb C$, $\mathfrak h^{\otimes 1}=\mathfrak h$,
and define each completed tensor power recursively by
$\mathfrak h^{\otimes(n+1)}=\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes\mathfrak h$,
using the first-variable-linear product inner product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. For $n\ge1$, let
$U_\pi$ permute the tensor factors for $\pi\in S_n$, and let
$$
P_\pm^{(n)}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\chi_\pm(\pi)U_\pi, \qquad \chi_+(\pi)=1,\quad \chi_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),
$$
with $P_\pm^{(0)}=I_{\mathbb C}$. The permutation-sector theorem
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] makes these orthogonal
projections. Define the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors
$\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}:=\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(n)}$. Define
$$
\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h):=\left\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\psi_n\in\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)},\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}, \qquad \langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{n\ge0}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle.
$$
The vector $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$ is the vacuum, and the finite-particle
subspace consists of vectors with only finitely many nonzero components.

This is a mathematical construction for a specified mode basis. Choosing its
symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a physical species is a separate model
postulate. No spin-statistics theorem or physical species assignment is part of
the definition.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $n\ge1$, and $H^{\otimes n}$ the $n$-fold completed tensor power ($H^{\otimes1}:=H$, $H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in H$ write $v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1}\in H^{\otimes n}$ for the iterated elementary tensor.

(a) For every $\pi$ in the symmetric group $S_n$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) there is a unique unitary $U_\pi\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ with

$$U_\pi(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=v_{\pi^{-1}(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n-1)},$$

and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$, $U_{\pi}^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$.

(b) The operators

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi$$

(with $\operatorname{sgn}$ the sign homomorphism, [[thm-sign-is-a-homomorphism]]) are orthogonal projections.

(c) $U_\pi P_+=P_+U_\pi=P_+$ and $U_\pi P_-=P_-U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-$ for every $\pi$; consequently the range of $P_+$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$.

(d) If $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$ have a repeated factor, that is, $v_i=v_j$ for some distinct $i,j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, then $P_-(v_0\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{n-1})=0$.

Selecting the symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a particle species is a physical postulate, not a theorem of this construction; no spin-statistics statement is proved here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $T$ be a
densely defined linear operator on $H$, with domain $D(T)$ dense in $H$
([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]], [[def-dense-top]]).
Since $D(T)$ is dense, and since $H$ is complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]), every
bounded linear functional on the normed space $(D(T),\|\cdot\|)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) extends uniquely to a bounded linear
functional $\widetilde\varphi$ on $H$ of the same norm, by setting
$\widetilde\varphi(z)=\lim_n\varphi(z_n)$ for any sequence $z_n\in D(T)$ with
$z_n\to z$ in $H$; the limit exists because $\varphi$ is bounded on a dense
subspace and $H$ is complete, and it does not depend on the sequence because a
bounded functional is uniformly continuous.

A vector $y\in H$ belongs to the **adjoint domain** $D(T^*)$ when the linear
functional $\varphi_y:D(T)\to\mathbb C$, $\varphi_y(x)=\langle Tx,y\rangle$, is
bounded on $(D(T),\|\cdot\|)$. In that case Hilbert space Riesz representation
([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]) applied to the extension
$\widetilde{\varphi_y}$ produces a unique vector $T^*y\in H$ with
$$T^*y\text{ is the unique }w\in H\text{ such that }\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,w\rangle\quad\text{for all }x\in D(T),$$
equivalently $\widetilde{\varphi_y}(z)=\langle z,T^*y\rangle$ for all $z\in H$.
The map $T^*:D(T^*)\to H$, $y\mapsto T^*y$, is the **adjoint** of $T$.

**Well-definedness.** The functional $\varphi_y$ is linear in $x$ for each
$y$, so its domain of boundedness $D(T^*)$ is a linear subspace: if
$\varphi_y,\varphi_{y'}$ are bounded so is $\varphi_{ay+by'}$ for scalars
$a,b$, because the first-variable-linear convention gives
$\varphi_{ay+by'}=\overline a\,\varphi_y+\overline b\,\varphi_{y'}$. On
$D(T^*)$ the map $T^*$ is linear: if $y,y'$ are represented by $w,w'$, then
$ay+by'$ is represented by $aw+bw'$, since
$\langle x,aw+bw'\rangle=\overline a\langle x,w\rangle+
\overline b\langle x,w'\rangle$; the representing vector is unique. By Riesz representation for the Hilbert space
$H$ a vector $w\in H$ is determined by the values $\langle z,w\rangle$ with
$z$ ranging over $H$, and those values are determined by the functional
$\widetilde{\varphi_y}$. Equivalently, if $w,w'$ both represent $\varphi_y$,
then $\langle x,w-w'\rangle=0$ for every $x\in D(T)$; density of $D(T)$ and
continuity of the inner product extend this equality to every $x\in H$, and
taking $x=w-w'$ gives $w=w'$. Finally only
ambient-norm boundedness of $\varphi_y$ on $D(T)$ is required: no extension,
no closure and no closedness of $T$ is presupposed.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $T$ be a linear
operator on $H$ with domain $D(T)$ and graph $\Gamma(T)$
([[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]]).

$T$ is **densely defined** when $D(T)$ is a dense subset of $H$
([[def-dense-top]]); **closed** when $\Gamma(T)$ is a closed subset of
$H\oplus H$; and **closable** when $T$ has a closed extension.
Recall that the graph norm is $\|x\|_T=(\|x\|^2+\|Tx\|^2)^{1/2}$.

**The graph-norm dictionary.** The following three statements are part of the
definition's content and are proved in the remarks below rather than assumed:

1. $\|\cdot\|_T$ is a norm on $D(T)$, and
   $x\mapsto(x,Tx)$ is an isometric isomorphism of $(D(T),\|\cdot\|_T)$ onto
   $\Gamma(T)$;
2. $T$ is closed if and only if $(D(T),\|\cdot\|_T)$ is a complete metric space
   ([[def-complete-metric-space]]);
3. if $T$ is closed, then $D(T)$ is a Hilbert space for the inner product
   $\langle x,y\rangle_T=\langle x,y\rangle+\langle Tx,Ty\rangle$ whose induced
   norm is $\|\cdot\|_T$.

A linear subspace $D_0\subseteq D(T)$ is a **core** for a closed operator $T$
when $D_0$ is dense in $(D(T),\|\cdot\|_T)$, equivalently when
$\overline{\Gamma(T|_{D_0})}=\Gamma(T)$, where the closure is taken in
$H\oplus H$ and $T|_{D_0}$ denotes the restriction of $T$ to $D_0$.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: Let $n=|m|$. In the bosonic permutation average $P_+^{(n)}x_m$, each distinct product word with occupation profile $m$ occurs $\prod_jm_j!$ times out of $n!$ permutations. Therefore $$ P_+^{(n)}x_m=\frac{\prod_jm_j!}{n!}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W(m)}w, \qquad |\mathcal W(m)|=\frac{n!}{\prod_jm_j!}. $$ The product words are orthonormal by [F1], so the squared norm of this average is $\prod_jm_j!/n!$; the prefactor in $|m\rangle_B$ makes its norm one. Distinct occupation profiles have disjoint word supports, hence their vectors are orthogonal.

If a fermionic list repeats a mode, [F2] makes its antisymmetrization zero; $\Omega_F$ excludes these profiles. For distinct occupied modes, the $n!$ permuted product words are distinct orthonormal vectors with coefficients $\pm1/n!$, so $\|P_-^{(n)}x_m\|^2=1/n!$. The prefactor $\sqrt{n!}$ normalizes the vector. Distinct occupied subsets have disjoint product-word support and are orthogonal.

The fixed enumeration identifies a finite-support configuration with a finite sequence of natural indices and finitely many nonnegative integer labels (or bits); the union over all finite sequence lengths is countable. Thus $\Omega_B$ and $\Omega_F$ are countable and their $\ell^2$ coordinate descriptions are well defined.

On the bosonic basis, shifting the coordinate index gives $\|a_jc\|^2=\sum_m m_j|c_m|^2$ and $\|a_j^\dagger c\|^2=\sum_m(m_j+1)|c_m|^2$. Hence the stated weighted domains are exactly the domains on which the shifted coefficient sequences lie in $\ell^2$. If $c^{(r)}\to c$ and either shifted sequence converges in $\ell^2$, coordinate convergence shows the limiting output has the same weighted-shift coordinates; its square summability puts $c$ in the displayed domain. Thus both maximal shifts are closed. Testing the adjoint identity against each basis vector forces the reverse weighted shift [F3], while Cauchy--Schwarz gives the converse pairing bound [F4]. Truncating to finite initial sets of configurations makes the weighted tails tend to zero in graph norm, so $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a core for both shifts under the graph definition in [F3].

Product words span a dense subspace of each tensor power by [F1]. Applying the bounded projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ to that dense span gives a dense subspace of each projected sector. Every projected product word is either zero or a scalar multiple of the corresponding occupation vector from steps 1.1–1.2. Thus the occupation vectors are complete in each sector and, after taking the direct sum over $n$, form orthonormal bases of the Fock spaces.

For $i=j$, direct action on $|m\rangle_B$ gives $a_ja_j^\dagger|m\rangle_B=(m_j+1)|m\rangle_B$ and $a_j^\dagger a_j|m\rangle_B=m_j|m\rangle_B$. For $i\ne j$, both orders of distinct coordinate shifts give the same coefficient and same occupation vector, so the shifts commute; the same direct coordinate calculation applies to two annihilators and two creators. This proves the CCR on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$, without asserting that unbounded commutators are defined on all Fock space.

Each fermionic shift maps a subset of an orthonormal basis into another orthonormal subset with coefficients of modulus at most one, so it is a contraction on the finite span and extends boundedly. For distinct $i,j$, the two orders in any CAR anticommutator are either both zero or have equal magnitudes and opposite signs: toggling the earlier mode changes by one the number of occupied modes preceding the later index. For $i=j$, if $m_j=0$ then $c_jc_j^\dagger|m\rangle_F=|m\rangle_F$ and $c_j^\dagger c_j|m\rangle_F=0$; if $m_j=1$ the roles reverse. The other same-mode anticommutators vanish. Thus all CAR identities hold on the basis span and extend by boundedness to the whole Fock space.

boundaries.evidence: Statement, vacuum convention: The zero occupation configuration exists even for I empty and is assigned the vacuum explicitly; products of occupation factorials then equal1 and the basis consists of that vacuum.
At m_j=0 the annihilation term is explicitly zero; Proof 3.1 checks both fermionic occupancy cases and obtains the identity anticommutator.
For a single bosonic mode the basis is indexed by N_0; one fermionic mode has exactly vacuum and occupied vectors, and Proof 3.1 verifies CAR in both cases.
Proof 1.2 explicitly excludes repeated fermionic modes because their antisymmetrization vanishes, while Proof 1.1 keeps repeated bosonic modes with the product factorial normalization.
The bosonic commutators are asserted only on D_fin in Proof 2.2; maximal weighted domains and their graph cores are established in 1.4, without extending unbounded CCR to every vector.

Proof 1.3 enumerates configurations by finite sequences from the fixed mode enumeration; this constructs the countable indexing within the inherited Fock assumptions instead of choosing arbitrary occupation orderings.

boundaries.reason: The theorem supplies occupation bases and operator relations; it does not claim that arbitrary operators satisfying CAR reconstruct the chosen Fock representation.
Proof 3.1 verifies CAR for the explicit signed shifts, without a converse representation theorem.
