Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Let $1\le q\le n$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^q$ be $C^1$ in the sense of [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. Suppose $F(x_*)=0$ and some $q\times q$ minor of the derivative matrix $DF(x_*)$ is invertible. This nonsingular-minor hypothesis is the explicit full-row-rank condition used here. If $q<n$, then after permuting coordinates $x=(u,v)\in\mathbb R^{n-q}\times\mathbb R^q$, there are open neighborhoods $P$ of $u_*$ and $Q$ of $v_*$ and a unique $C^1$ map $\varphi:P\to Q$ such that

$$F(u,v)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v=\varphi(u)\qquad((u,v)\in P\times Q).$$

Its derivative is

$$D\varphi(u)=-D_vF(u,\varphi(u))^{-1}D_uF(u,\varphi(u)).$$

Thus the local zero set is a graph over $n-q$ free coordinates. If $q=n$, the zero is locally isolated, so the local graph dimension is zero. Here “local graph dimension $k$” means a local graph parameterized by an open subset of $\mathbb R^k$, with a singleton counted as dimension zero.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Then there is an open
neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ of $p$ and a smooth future-directed tetrad field
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ on $U$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]), i.e.
$g_q(E_A(q),E_B(q))=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$ for all $q\in U$ with
$E_0(q)$ future-directed for every $q\in U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: For every vector $X$, $u_a(\Delta X)^a=u_aX^a+(u_au^a)(u_bX^b)=0$ and $\Delta u=0$. If $X\in u^\perp$, then $\Delta X=X$. Hence $\operatorname{im}\Delta=u^\perp$, $\ker\Delta=\mathbb Ru$, and $\Delta^2=\Delta$. Also $g(\Delta X,Y)=g(X,Y)+g(X,u)g(u,Y)=g(X,\Delta Y)$ for all $X,Y$, so $\Delta$ is self-adjoint and is the orthogonal projection onto $u^\perp$.

Since $\delta^a{}_c=\Delta^a{}_c-u^a u_c$, expansion in both indices gives
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd}-u^a u_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd}-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d\,u^b+u^a u^b u_cu_d\mathsf T^{cd}.$$
By the definitions this is the stated decomposition. Orthogonality of $Q$ and $P$ follows by $u_a\Delta^a{}_c=0$, so $\pi$ is spatial as well. Since $g_{ab}\Delta^{ab}=3$, the definition of $p_{\mathrm{mech}}$ gives $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. The component formulas recover $\varepsilon_u,Q,P$ from any such decomposition, so it is unique.

In the chosen tetrad of [F3], identify symmetric contravariant tensors with the ten-dimensional vector space $\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbb R^4)$ and write $T^A{}_B=\mathsf T^{AC}\eta_{CB}$ for their mixed components. For $w\in\mathbb B^3$, put $\gamma(w)=(1-|w|^2)^{-1/2}$ and $\widehat u^A(w)=\gamma(w)(1,w^1,w^2,w^3)$, the tetrad components of $u(x,w)$ from clause 4, and define
$$\Phi_i(T,w):=T^i{}_A\widehat u^A(w)-w^iT^0{}_A\widehat u^A(w)\quad(i=1,2,3).$$
This is a smooth map on the open subset $\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbb R^4)\times\mathbb B^3\cong\mathbb R^{10}\times\mathbb B^3$ of $\mathbb R^{13}$, and $\Phi(T_0,0)=0$. At $T_0=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon_0,p_0,p_0,p_0)$ as a contravariant matrix, the mixed matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(-\varepsilon_0,p_0,p_0,p_0)$. Since $\partial_{w^j}\widehat u^0(0)=0$ and $\partial_{w^j}\widehat u^k(0)=\delta^k_j$, direct differentiation gives $\partial_{w^j}\Phi_i(T_0,0)=p_0\delta_{ij}+\varepsilon_0\delta_{ij}=h_0\delta_{ij}$. Thus $D_w\Phi(T_0,0)=h_0I_3$ is invertible by $h_0>0$.

Put $
u_u=-u\cdot J$. Then $J-
u_u u=J+u(u\cdot J)=\Delta J=V$, and [step 1.1] shows $V\in u^\perp$. If $J=
u u+W$ with $W\perp u$, contracting with $u$ forces $
u=
u_u$ and applying $\Delta$ forces $W=V$.

$Q=0$ is equivalent to $\Delta(\mathsf T^\sharp u)=0$, where $(\mathsf T^\sharp u)^a:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_b$. By [step 1.1], $\ker\Delta=\mathbb Ru$, so this holds exactly when $\mathsf T^a{}_b u^b$ is a scalar multiple of $u^a$, the timelike-eigenvector condition.

Apply [F2] with $q=3$ to $\Phi(T,w)=0$. The $3\times3$ minor in the $w$ variables is invertible by step 1.3, so near $(T_0,0)$ the zero set is a unique $C^1$ graph $w=\varphi(T)$. Choose an open ball $W\subset\mathbb B^3$ about $0$ within the graph neighborhood and shrink the tensor neighborhood so that $\varphi(T)\in W$. In the chosen tetrad, the component map $x\mapsto T^A{}_B(x)$ is $C^1$, because $\mathsf T$ is $C^1$ and the tetrad is smooth. Shrink to a neighborhood $U\subset O_0$ on which these components remain in that tensor neighborhood; then $w_L(x):=\varphi(T(x))$ is $C^1$, and $u_L(x):=u(x,w_L(x))$ is a $C^1$ future unit timelike field. The equations $\Phi_i(T(x),w_L(x))=0$ say that the spatial components of $\mathsf T^A{}_B(x)u_L^B(x)$ equal $w_L^i(x)$ times its time component, so $\mathsf T^A{}_B(x)u_L^B(x)=\lambda(x)u_L^A(x)$ for a scalar $\lambda(x)$. By step 2.2 this is equivalent to $Q_{u_L(x)}(x)=0$, and uniqueness of the local graph gives the claimed uniqueness of $w_L$.

Let $r:=\sqrt{-g(J,J)}>0$. Then $u_E=J/r$ is future unit timelike and $\Delta_{u_E}J=J+u_E(u_E\cdot J)=J+(J/r)(-r)=0$. Conversely, if a future unit timelike $u$ has $\Delta_uJ=0$, step 2.1 gives $J=\lambda u$ for a scalar $\lambda$. Since both $J$ and $u$ are future timelike, $\lambda>0$; hence $-g(J,J)=\lambda^2$ forces $\lambda=r$ and $u=u_E$.

If $g(\ell,u)=0$, then $\ell\in u^\perp$, and [F4] makes the restricted metric positive definite; since $g(\ell,\ell)=0$, this would force $\ell=0$. Therefore $g(\ell,u)\ne0$, so $\mathsf T^\sharp u=\rho\ell\,g(\ell,u)$ is a nonzero null vector. It cannot equal $\lambda u$ for any scalar $\lambda$: if $\lambda=0$ it is nonzero, and if $\lambda\ne0$ the right side is timelike while the left side is null. Thus no timelike eigenvector exists.

Substitute the first-order laws into [F1] under the no-work assumption
$u_bf^b=0$ of [A3]. They give

$-V^a\nabla_a(\mu/T)=L\Delta^{ab}\nabla_a(\mu/T)\nabla_b(\mu/T)$.
The rest-space metric induced by $\Delta$ is positive definite by [F5]; with
$T,c>0$ and nonnegative coefficients every summand is nonnegative, proving
the stated residual inequality.

In Minkowski coordinates, $T^{00}=\epsilon$ and $T^{i0}=Q^i$ for the
fixed-rest stress of [A2]. The temporal balance $\nabla_aT^{a0}=f^0=0$ is
$c^{-1}\partial_t\epsilon+\partial_iQ^i=0$. The spatial components are
$\nabla_aT^{ai}=c^{-1}\partial_tQ^i+\partial_i p=f^i$, as required by [A2].
Using $\epsilon=\epsilon_0+C\vartheta$ and $q=cQ=-\kappa\nabla\vartheta$,
the temporal balance becomes $C\partial_t\vartheta+\nabla\cdot q=0$, or
$C\partial_t\vartheta-\kappa\Delta\vartheta=0$. Put $a_h=\kappa/C>0$ and
$U(\mathbf x,\tau)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma(\mathbf x-\mathbf y,\tau)
\vartheta_0(\mathbf y)\,d\mathbf y$. The smooth compactly supported datum in
[A2] is bounded and uniformly continuous, so [F4] gives a smooth solution of
$U_\tau=\Delta U$ for $\tau>0$ with initial trace $\vartheta_0$ locally
uniformly. Then $\vartheta(\mathbf x,t)=U(\mathbf x,a_ht)$ solves the fixed-rest
equation and has the stated boundary trace. Kernel positivity [F2] and
$\vartheta_0\ge0$ give $\vartheta\ge0$. The unit integral from [F3] and
$\vartheta_0\le\delta$ give
$$\vartheta(\mathbf x,t)\le\delta\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma(\mathbf x-\mathbf y,a_ht)\,d\mathbf y=\delta,$$
so the temperature remains in the specified state interval.

Write $u^0=1+O(|\mathbf w|^2)$ and $u^i=w^i+O(|\mathbf w|^2)$ in the
homogeneous rest perturbation of [A4]. With $x^0=ct$,
$a^i=u^a\nabla_a u^i=c^{-1}\dot w^i$ to first order, so the first-order
acceleration heat law gives $Q^i=-\kappa T_0\dot w^i/c^2$. In

$T^{0i}=h_0w^i+Q^i$: the perfect part contributes $h_0w^i$, the term
$u^0Q^i$ contributes $Q^i$, and $Q^0u^i$ is second order. All spatial
derivatives vanish, so $\partial_0T^{0i}=0$ gives
$h_0\dot w^i/c+\dot Q^i/c=0$. Multiplication by $c$ gives
$h_0\dot w^i+\dot Q^i=0$, the stated homogeneous linearized momentum equation.

Since $\vartheta_0$ is continuous, nonnegative, and nonzero, it is bounded
below by a positive constant on some closed ball of positive radius. For every
fixed $\mathbf x$ and $t>0$, the continuous kernel
$\Gamma(\mathbf x-\mathbf y,a_ht)$ has a positive minimum on that ball by
[F2], so the convolution from step 1.2 is strictly positive. Thus

$t>0$ because $\operatorname{supp}\vartheta_0$ is compact; it cannot contain

finite propagation.

$Q^i=-\alpha\dot w^i$ into the equation of step 1.3 gives

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice and let $n\ge1$, and let
$u_0:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and uniformly continuous. Define
$u(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Gamma(x-y,t)u_0(y)\,dy$ for $t>0$ and
$u(x,0):=u_0(x)$. Then $u$ is $C^\infty$ on
$\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)$, satisfies $\partial_tu=\Delta_xu$ there, is
bounded with $\|u(\cdot,t)\|_\infty\le\|u_0\|_\infty$, and converges locally
uniformly at the initial time:
$\sup_{x\in K}|u(x,t)-u_0(x)|\to0$ as $t\downarrow0^+$ for every compact
$K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$.

derivations.claim:
Write $u=(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$. Future timelikeness gives $u^0>0$ and
$-(u^0)^2+(u^1)^2+(u^2)^2+(u^3)^2=-1$, so
$|\mathbf u|^2=(u^0)^2-1<(u^0)^2$. Consequently
$\ell_bu^b=-u^0+u^1<0$, since $u^1\le|\mathbf u|<u^0$. Hence
$\epsilon_u=\rho(\ell_bu^b)^2>0$.

Contract the stress decomposition in [F1] on its first index with $u_a$.
Using $u_au^a=-1$, $u_aQ^a=0$, and $u_aP^{ab}=0$ gives
$u_aT^{ab}=-\epsilon_u u^b-Q^b$. Since $T$ is symmetric, this means
$T^a{}_bu^b=-\epsilon_u u^a$ if $Q=0$. By the definition of $T^a{}_b$ and
the metric, the left side is $\rho\ell^a(\ell_bu^b)$, a nonzero null vector
by step 1.1.
The right side is nonzero timelike because $\epsilon_u>0$ and $u$ is timelike.
Equality is impossible because equal vectors have equal quadratic norm, while
these norms are respectively zero and negative. Hence $Q\ne0$ for every
candidate future unit timelike $u$, and the tensor has no Landau frame.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. The negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform is continuous $\mathcal F:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$, and
$$\mathcal F(\partial^\alpha f)(\xi)=(2\pi i\xi)^\alpha\widehat f(\xi),\qquad \partial^\beta\widehat f=\mathcal F((-2\pi ix)^\beta f).$$

Assume countable choice. For every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ and every $x\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\widehat f(\xi)e^{2\pi ix\cdot\xi}\,d\xi.$$
The integral is absolutely convergent.

Assume countable choice and let $n\ge1$. Fourier transformation on Schwartz space extends uniquely to a surjective complex-linear isometry $\mathcal F_2:L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$. It preserves the first-variable-linear inner product, and hence is unitary.

Assume Countable Choice and use the negative-sign $2\pi$ normalization.  If
$f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$, then

$$\mathcal F u_f=u_{\widehat f},$$

where $\widehat f$ is the integral Fourier transform.  If
$f\in L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$, then

$$\mathcal F u_f=u_{\mathcal F_2f},$$

where $\mathcal F_2$ is the Plancherel extension.  These equalities are in
$\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)$ and therefore depend only on the corresponding
almost-everywhere classes.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge2$, a bounded $C^1$ domain Omega and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}F\cdot\nu\,dS$. Both integrals are finite, with the continuous interior derivative convention and the outward normal on every boundary component.

Fix an integer $n\ge1$. With the complex smooth-function convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]] and multi-indices of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], define
$$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|,\qquad \mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)=\{f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C):p_{\alpha\beta}(f)<\infty\text{ for all }\alpha,\beta\}.$$
The zero multi-index gives $x^0=1$ and $\partial^0f=f$. These are actual smooth functions, not equivalence classes. The notation $C_c^\infty$ uses the support convention in [[def-c-c-and-c-c-infinity-on-rn]].

Pointwise differentiation is linear; thus $p_{\alpha\beta}(f+g)\le p_{\alpha\beta}(f)+p_{\alpha\beta}(g)$ and $p_{\alpha\beta}(cf)=|c|p_{\alpha\beta}(f)$. In particular this set is a complex vector space and each $p_{\alpha\beta}$ is a seminorm. The zero function belongs to it. Since $p_{00}(f)=0$ forces $f(x)=0$ for every $x$, the family separates functions. No choice principle is needed.

derivations.claim: For any real symmetric matrix $H$, maximize $z^{\mathsf T}Hz$ on the compact unit sphere. Differentiating along every tangent direction shows the maximizing vector is an eigenvector; its orthogonal complement is invariant under $H$, so induction gives an orthonormal eigenbasis. Applying this to $M$ constructs $M^{1/2}$ and $M^{-1/2}$. The condition $MA_j=A_j^{\mathsf T}M$ makes $\widetilde A_j=M^{1/2}A_jM^{-1/2}$ symmetric. Therefore each eigenvalue in $v_*$ is real and has absolute value at most $\sum_j\|\widetilde A_j\|$, so $v_*<\infty$. With $e=U^{\mathsf T}MU/2$ and $F_j=U^{\mathsf T}MA_jU/2$, the product rule gives $\partial_te+\sum_j\partial_{x_j}F_j=-U^{\mathsf T}SU\le0$ for every smooth solution, and $|F\cdot\nu|\le v_*e$ by diagonalizing $\widetilde A(\nu)$.

For Schwartz data, [F1] permits componentwise Fourier transformation of the system, giving $\partial_t\widehat U=C(\xi)\widehat U$ with $C(\xi)=-2\pi i\sum_j\xi_jA_j-B$. The matrix exponential $E(t,\xi)=e^{tC(\xi)}$, defined by its locally uniformly convergent power series, solves this finite-dimensional ODE. For $z(t)=E(t,\xi)z_0$, $\frac d{dt}(z^*Mz)=-2z^*Sz\le0$, because $MA(\xi)$ is real symmetric and its multiple by $-i$ has zero real quadratic part. Thus $\|E(t,\xi)\|_M\le1$ for $t\ge0$, uniformly in $\xi$; for $t<0$, $|\frac d{dt}(z^*Mz)|\le2\|M^{-1/2}SM^{-1/2}\|z^*Mz$, so Grönwall gives a uniform $e^{C|t|}$ bound on bounded time intervals.

Differentiating the matrix exponential with respect to $\xi_j$ gives $\partial_{\xi_j}E(t,\xi)=\int_0^tE(t-s,\xi)(-2\pi iA_j)E(s,\xi)\,ds$. Repeating this identity expresses every fixed $\xi$-derivative as a finite sum of ordered insertion integrals with constant matrix factors between evolution matrices. The uniform bounds from step 1.2 and the finite integration-simplex volumes bound each such derivative uniformly in $\xi$ on compact time intervals. Time derivatives multiply by $C(\xi)$ and therefore have at most polynomial growth in $\xi$. Leibniz's rule now shows $E(t,\cdot)\widehat U_0$ is Schwartz, uniformly in its seminorms on compact time intervals.

For periodic smooth data, integration by parts in a coordinate with maximal $|k_j|$ gives $|\widehat U_k(0)|\le C_N(1+|k|)^{-N}$ for every $N$. The series $U(t,x)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}e^{2\pi i k\cdot x/L}E(t,k/L)\widehat U_k(0)$ and every differentiated series converge uniformly on compact time intervals, by the same matrix-exponential derivative bounds and the lattice-shell estimate that a unit-width shell in $\mathbb Z^3$ has $O((1+r)^2)$ points. Hence it is a global smooth periodic solution and solves the PDE termwise. The modewise $M$-estimate from step 1.2 yields contraction of every weighted coefficient norm. For $s>3/2$, Cauchy–Schwarz and $M\ge\lambda_{\min}(M)I$ give $\sum_k|\widehat U_k(t)|\le\lambda_{\min}(M)^{-1/2}(\sum_k(1+|k/L|^2)^{-s})^{1/2}(\sum_k(1+|k/L|^2)^s\widehat U_k(t)^*M\widehat U_k(t))^{1/2}$; the first sum converges by the shell bound, proving the asserted uniform norm estimate. Integrating the equation against each periodic exponential shows that every solution coefficient solves the same finite-dimensional ODE, proving uniqueness.

Define $U(t)=\mathcal F^{-1}(E(t,\cdot)\widehat U_0)$. By [F2] this inverse is pointwise the absolutely convergent Fourier integral; the decay proved in step 2.1 permits every spatial and time derivative to pass under that integral, proves the PDE, and recovers $U(0)=U_0$. Conjugation symmetry of $C(\xi)$ and $\widehat U_0(-\xi)=\overline{\widehat U_0(\xi)}$ makes $U$ real.

By [F3] the Plancherel transform is unitary, and [F4] identifies it with the integral transform in $\mathcal S'$. Multiplying the pointwise $M$-norm estimate in step 1.2 by $(1+|\xi|^2)^s$ and integrating gives the stated $H^s_M$ contraction for every $s\ge0$.

Fix $t_*>0$, $x_*$, and $0\le t<t_*$. Put $R(t)=v_*(t_*-t)$ and $E(t)=\int_{B_{R(t)}(x_*)}e(t,x)\,dx$. In polar coordinates, the fundamental theorem of calculus differentiates this moving-ball integral; the PDE energy identity and [F5] then give $E'(t)=-\int_{\partial B_{R(t)}}(F\cdot\nu+v_*e)\,dS-\int_{B_{R(t)}}U^{\mathsf T}SU\,dx\le0$, since $|F\cdot\nu|\le v_*e$. If the initial data vanish on $B_{v_*t_*}(x_*)$, then $E(0)=0$; positivity of $M$ and $E(t)\ge0$ force $U(t,x_*)=0$ by continuity as $t\uparrow t_*$. For any $x$ with $|x-x_0|<R-v_*t_*$, the ball $B_{v_*t_*}(x)$ is contained in $B_R(x_0)$, proving the stated shrinking-ball conclusion. Applying the same argument to the difference of two solutions proves local uniqueness. Periodic lifts give the identical geodesic-ball conclusion on $\mathbb T_L^3$. If $v_*=0$, every symmetric $\widetilde A_j$ has zero spectrum and hence is zero, so each $A_j=0$; the pointwise ODE preserves spatial support.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, let $\nabla$ be its metric-compatible torsion-free connection, and
let $u$ be a smooth future-directed vector field with $g(u,u)=-1$. Put
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$,
$a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and $\Delta^b{}_a=\delta^b{}_a+u^bu_a$.
Take a smooth fixed-composition state from [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] with
$n>0$, $T>0$, $s=n\sigma_p$, and $h=\epsilon+p=Ts+\mu n$ as in
[[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. Define the perfect stress tensor and particle
current by

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^a u^b+p\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a.$$

For any smooth vector field $f^b$, the balance equation $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$
is equivalent to the pair

$$D\epsilon+h\theta=-u_bf^b,\qquad ha^c+\Delta^{ca}\nabla_a p=\Delta^c{}_bf^b,$$

and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ is equivalent to $Dn+n\theta=0$. Whenever both balances
hold, the exact entropy identities are

$$T\nabla_a(su^a)=-u_bf^b,\qquad nT D\sigma_p=-u_bf^b.$$

In particular, when $f=0$, the entropy current $su$ is divergence-free and
specific entropy is advected, $D\sigma_p=0$. These are conditional identities
for supplied smooth fields; they assert no solution existence or physical
applicability beyond the stated model data.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be nonempty and open, let $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$, and define
$$Y:=\{(n,s)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R:(1/n,s/n)\in X\},\qquad \varepsilon(n,s):=n\,e(1/n,s/n).$$
For $(n,s)\in Y$, put $v=1/n$, $\sigma_p=s/n$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, $H=e+pv$, $h=\varepsilon+p=nH$, and $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Then the following identities hold as equalities of differentials on $Y$:
$$d\varepsilon=T\,ds+\mu\,dn,\qquad \varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n,\qquad dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu.$$

For parcel totals $\mathsf S\in\mathbb R$ (entropy), $\mathsf V>0$ (proper volume), and $\mathsf N>0$ (marker count) with $(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X$, define
$$E(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):=\mathsf N\,e(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N).$$
Then $E$ is $C^2$, is positively homogeneous of degree one, and satisfies
$$dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N,\qquad E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N.$$
If $E$ is viewed on its open domain in $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, its Hessian annihilates the radial vector $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Use the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian data, local state, and conventions of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]], with $n>0$, $T>0$, $c>0$, $x^0=ct$, and smooth future unit $u$. Assume positive $C^1$ coefficients $\zeta$ and $\tau$, set $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, and let $\Pi$ be a smooth scalar. In the bulk-only branch take

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_au^a$, and $a^b_{\rm acc}=Du^b$. Adopt the corrected relaxation law

$$\beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right)$$

and the extended entropy current $S^a=[s-\beta\Pi^2/(2T)]u^a$. Then the stress and particle equations imply

$$D\epsilon+(h+\Pi)\theta=0,\qquad (h+\Pi)a^b_{\rm acc}+\Delta^{ba}\nabla_a(p+\Pi)=0,\qquad Dn+n\theta=0,$$

and every actual smooth solution of the stated corrected law satisfies

$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\ge0.$$

Here $\beta$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, $\Pi,\epsilon,p,h$ have units Pa, $D,\theta,a_{\rm acc}$ have inverse-length components, and the correction $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has the units of entropy density. The law is an explicit model assumption; dropping its derivative term does not yield the stated sign identity in general.

There is an exact homogeneous solution on the explicitly specified Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$; its Levi-Civita derivative is ordinary coordinate differentiation. Fix a state point $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplied local state domain with $v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and take the constant state map $(v,\sigma_p)(x)=(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, so $n_0=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ are constant. For constant positive coefficients $\zeta_0,\tau_0$, let $u=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, $T=T_0$, and define the smooth scalar field $\Pi(x)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0}$ on all of $M$, where $t=x^0/c$. The stress and particle balances and the corrected law hold, with strict entropy production wherever $\Pi(x)\ne0$. This mathematical witness is not a general nonlinear existence theorem or a claim of physical applicability in any separately selected near-equilibrium regime.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be nonempty and open, let $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$, and define
$$Y:=\{(n,s)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R:(1/n,s/n)\in X\},\qquad \varepsilon(n,s):=n\,e(1/n,s/n).$$
For $(n,s)\in Y$, put $v=1/n$, $\sigma_p=s/n$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, $H=e+pv$, $h=\varepsilon+p=nH$, and $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Then the following identities hold as equalities of differentials on $Y$:
$$d\varepsilon=T\,ds+\mu\,dn,\qquad \varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n,\qquad dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu.$$

For parcel totals $\mathsf S\in\mathbb R$ (entropy), $\mathsf V>0$ (proper volume), and $\mathsf N>0$ (marker count) with $(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X$, define
$$E(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):=\mathsf N\,e(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N).$$
Then $E$ is $C^2$, is positively homogeneous of degree one, and satisfies
$$dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N,\qquad E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N.$$
If $E$ is viewed on its open domain in $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, its Hessian annihilates the radial vector $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$.

The local response statements are conditional. At a state with $T>0$ and $e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}>0$, temperature is a valid local coordinate at fixed $v$, and the per-marker heat capacity
$$c_v:=\left(\frac{\partial e}{\partial T}\right)_v=\frac{T}{e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$, the isentropic compressibility
$$\kappa_{\sigma_p}:=-\frac1v\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial p}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac1{v e_{vv}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$ and $h>0$, the local pressure-energy response
$$\alpha_{\sigma_p}:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\varepsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n h}$$
is positive. If $X$ is convex and $e$ is convex on $X$, then $D^2e$ is positive semidefinite. Positivity of the displayed diagonal responses is not asserted to imply convexity, a sound cone, or an evolution theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$, and let $A_1,A_2,A_3,B,M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be constant matrices. Assume $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite, each $MA_j$ is symmetric, and $S:=(MB+B^{\mathsf T}M)/2$ is positive semidefinite. Consider

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_{x_j}U+BU=0.$$

Use [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]: for $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^3$, the scalar seminorm is $p_{\alpha\beta}(f):=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^3}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$, and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ consists of functions for which all these seminorms are finite. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ means maps $U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)$ with real-valued components such that each component, viewed as complex-valued with zero imaginary part, belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$; its vector seminorms are $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}(U):=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq m}p_{\alpha\beta}(U_\ell)$. For $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ there is a unique global smooth solution, Schwartz in $x$ at each time and continuous in every $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}$ on compact time intervals. With the negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, put $\widehat U(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}U(x)\,dx$ and define, for $s\ge0$,

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M}^2:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|\xi|^2)^s\widehat U(\xi)^*M\widehat U(\xi)\,d\xi.$$

For $t\ge0$, $\|U(t)\|_{H^s_M}\le\|U_0\|_{H^s_M}$ for every $s\ge0$; hence the solution depends continuously on the data in each such norm. The same conclusions hold for smooth periodic data on the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, $L>0$, with Fourier coefficients $\widehat U_k=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}U(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x/L}\,dx$ and

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k/L|^2)^s\widehat U_k^*M\widehat U_k.$$

For periodic data, $\|U(t)\|_\infty\le C_{s,L,M}\|U_0\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}$ for each integer $s>3/2$.

For a unit vector $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, write $A(\nu)=\sum_j\nu_jA_j$ and $\widetilde A(\nu)=M^{1/2}A(\nu)M^{-1/2}$. The finite speed

$$v_*:=\sup_{|\nu|=1}\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde A(\nu))\}$$

is finite. If $v_*>0$, $R>v_*t$, and $U_0$ vanishes on $B_R(x_0)$, then $U(t)$ vanishes on $B_{R-v_*t}(x_0)$ for $0\le t<R/v_*$. The same assertion holds on $\mathbb T_L^3$ using its geodesic distance. If $v_*=0$, every $A_j=0$ and the system is a pointwise linear ODE, so spatial support does not move. These are conclusions for the displayed linear systems; no variable-coefficient or nonlinear existence claim is included.

Fix an integer $n\ge1$. With the complex smooth-function convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]] and multi-indices of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], define
$$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|,\qquad \mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)=\{f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C):p_{\alpha\beta}(f)<\infty\text{ for all }\alpha,\beta\}.$$
The zero multi-index gives $x^0=1$ and $\partial^0f=f$. These are actual smooth functions, not equivalence classes. The notation $C_c^\infty$ uses the support convention in [[def-c-c-and-c-c-infinity-on-rn]].

Pointwise differentiation is linear; thus $p_{\alpha\beta}(f+g)\le p_{\alpha\beta}(f)+p_{\alpha\beta}(g)$ and $p_{\alpha\beta}(cf)=|c|p_{\alpha\beta}(f)$. In particular this set is a complex vector space and each $p_{\alpha\beta}$ is a seminorm. The zero function belongs to it. Since $p_{00}(f)=0$ forces $f(x)=0$ for every $x$, the family separates functions. No choice principle is needed.

derivations.claim: At $\lambda=0$, $u_0=\partial_{x^0}$ and $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$. Differentiating the unit normalization gives $\delta u^0=0$, so the first variations of $D\epsilon$, $\theta$, and the spatial acceleration are respectively $c^{-1}r_t$, $\operatorname{div}w$, and $c^{-1}\partial_t w$. Because $\Pi_0=0$ and the background $u,T,\beta$ are constant, the product $\Pi\nabla_a(\beta u^a/T)$ has zero first variation. By [F2], $\delta p=a_s r$. Linearizing the energy projection in [F1] gives $r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0$, and its spatial projection gives $w_t+(c/h_0)\nabla(a_s r+\Pi)=0$. The linearized corrected law is $(\tau/(\zeta c))\partial_t\Pi+\Pi/(\zeta c)=-\operatorname{div}w$; multiplication by $\zeta c$ gives the third equation. For consistency, at fixed $\sigma_p$ [F2] gives $\partial_n\epsilon=T\sigma_p+\mu=h/n$, hence $\delta n=(n_0/h_0)r$; the first equation then implies $(\delta n)_t+c n_0\operatorname{div}w=0$, the linearized particle balance.

Differentiate $\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}$ and substitute the system: the $r\operatorname{div}w$ terms cancel, the $\Pi\operatorname{div}w$ terms cancel, and the remaining relaxation term is $-\Pi^2/\zeta$. Thus $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\Pi)w]=-\Pi^2/\zeta\le0$.

Let $U=(r,w,\Pi)$ and $M=\operatorname{diag}(a_s/h_0,h_0I_3,\tau/\zeta)$. For each spatial index $j$, the nonzero entries of the principal matrix are $(A_j)_{r,w_j}=ch_0$, $(A_j)_{w_j,r}=ca_s/h_0$, $(A_j)_{w_j,\Pi}=c/h_0$, and $(A_j)_{\Pi,w_j}=\zeta c/\tau$; hence $MA_j$ is symmetric. The damping matrix is $B=\operatorname{diag}(0,0_{3\times3},1/\tau)$, with $MB=\operatorname{diag}(0,0_{3\times3},1/\zeta)\ge0$. The longitudinal block of $A(\nu)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}0&ch_0&0\\ ca_s/h_0&0&c/h_0\\0&\zeta c/\tau&0\end{pmatrix}$, whose characteristic polynomial is $-\lambda[\lambda^2-c^2(a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0))]$; transverse velocities have zero speed. Apply [F3] to obtain the actual global solution, uniqueness, energy contraction, and finite propagation at $v_{\rm bulk}$.

Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives $(a_s r+\Pi)^2\le(h_0a_s+\zeta/\tau)[(a_s/h_0)r^2+(\tau/\zeta)\Pi^2]$. Therefore for every unit $\nu$, $|c(a_s r+\Pi)w\cdot\nu|\le c\sqrt{a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0)}\,\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}$ by $2XY\le X^2+Y^2$. Since $c>0$, $v_{\rm bulk}\le c$ is equivalent to $a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0)\le1$. With $r$ spatially constant, $w=0$, and $\Pi=0$, the first mode is stationary; constant transverse $w$ with $r=\Pi=0$ is stationary as well.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Use $\mathcal M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, future direction $\partial_{x^0}$, and reference causal cone $\{V:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$, whose boundary speed in $(t,\mathbf x)$ coordinates is $c$. Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. The background fields are this constant state, $u_0=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, and $\Pi_0=0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv},c>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$.

A first variation is defined by a family $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda},u_\lambda,\Pi_\lambda)$ jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, through the displayed background, with $u_\lambda$ future unit, meaning $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ and $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, set $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$. At each $\lambda$, set $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $T_\lambda=e_{\sigma_p}(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $D_\lambda=u_\lambda^a\partial_a$, and $\theta_\lambda=\partial_a u_\lambda^a$. The bulk stress and current are $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+(p_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda)\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$ and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$, and the corrected law of [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] is $\beta D_\lambda\Pi_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda/(\zeta c)=-\theta_\lambda-(T_\lambda\Pi_\lambda/2)\partial_a(\beta u_\lambda^a/T_\lambda)$, where $\beta=\tau/\zeta$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$, $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, and this corrected law, set equal to zero; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear system. Impose $\delta\sigma_p=0$, put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and denote $\delta\Pi$ by $\Pi$ in the linearized system below. Take constant coefficients $\zeta,\tau>0$.

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n_0h_0}>0$$

as supplied by [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. The resulting linearized system is

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau\Pi_t+\Pi=-\zeta c\operatorname{div}w.$$

Its positive quadratic energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2+\frac{\tau}{\zeta}\Pi^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\Pi)w]=-\Pi^2/\zeta$. The normal characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm v_{\rm bulk}$, where

$$v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{a_s+\frac{\zeta}{\tau h_0}}.$$

By [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]], initial data $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^5)$ with the componentwise real convention of [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, have unique global smooth solutions, contractive in the corresponding energy and Sobolev norms, with finite propagation at $v_{\rm bulk}$. The branch is inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0)\le1$. Constant density and transverse velocity modes can persist, so contraction does not mean every mode decays. No nonlinear or variable-coefficient existence theorem is claimed.

Use the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian data, local state, and conventions of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]], with $n>0$, $T>0$, $c>0$, $x^0=ct$, and smooth future unit $u$. Assume positive $C^1$ coefficients $\zeta$ and $\tau$, set $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, and let $\Pi$ be a smooth scalar. In the bulk-only branch take

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_au^a$, and $a^b_{\rm acc}=Du^b$. Adopt the corrected relaxation law

$$\beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right)$$

and the extended entropy current $S^a=[s-\beta\Pi^2/(2T)]u^a$. Then the stress and particle equations imply

$$D\epsilon+(h+\Pi)\theta=0,\qquad (h+\Pi)a^b_{\rm acc}+\Delta^{ba}\nabla_a(p+\Pi)=0,\qquad Dn+n\theta=0,$$

and every actual smooth solution of the stated corrected law satisfies

$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\ge0.$$

Here $\beta$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, $\Pi,\epsilon,p,h$ have units Pa, $D,\theta,a_{\rm acc}$ have inverse-length components, and the correction $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has the units of entropy density. The law is an explicit model assumption; dropping its derivative term does not yield the stated sign identity in general.

There is an exact homogeneous solution on the explicitly specified Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$; its Levi-Civita derivative is ordinary coordinate differentiation. Fix a state point $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplied local state domain with $v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and take the constant state map $(v,\sigma_p)(x)=(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, so $n_0=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ are constant. For constant positive coefficients $\zeta_0,\tau_0$, let $u=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, $T=T_0$, and define the smooth scalar field $\Pi(x)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0}$ on all of $M$, where $t=x^0/c$. The stress and particle balances and the corrected law hold, with strict entropy production wherever $\Pi(x)\ne0$. This mathematical witness is not a general nonlinear existence theorem or a claim of physical applicability in any separately selected near-equilibrium regime.

derivations.claim: Direct differentiation of $e$ gives $e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=0$ and $e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=n_0h_0/3$. Thus [A2] verifies the local state's positive $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv}$ hypotheses, and [F1] supplies $a_s=e_{vv}/(n_0h_0)=1/3$. The choice $\zeta=\tau h_0$ gives $\zeta/(\tau h_0)=1$, so all remaining strict positivity hypotheses of [F1] hold.

Substitution gives $v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{1/3+1}=2c/\sqrt3$. Since $4/3>1$ and $c>0$, $2c/\sqrt3>c$. The separate entropy identity in [F2] is nonnegative whenever its actual-solution hypotheses hold, including $T>0$; that conditional sign statement supplies no bound on this characteristic speed.

Fix a real parameter $a_R>0$ and let the temperature coordinate range over the open interval $T\in(0,\infty)$. Define the entropy-only radiation state maps

$$\varepsilon_T(T):=a_RT^4,\qquad p_T(T):=\frac13a_RT^4,\qquad s_T(T):=\frac43a_RT^3.$$

Here $\varepsilon_T$ and $p_T$ are scalar-valued maps on $(0,\infty)$, and $s_T$ is the entropy coordinate as a scalar-valued map on the same interval. Put $h_T(T):=\varepsilon_T(T)+p_T(T)$. No particle-number coordinate, particle-number current, or chemical-potential coordinate is part of this state space.

Also define maps on the positive entropy-coordinate interval by

$$\tau(s):=\left(\frac{3s}{4a_R}\right)^{1/3},\qquad \varepsilon_s(s):=a_R\tau(s)^4,\qquad p_s(s):=\frac13\varepsilon_s(s),\qquad s\in(0,\infty).$$

The displayed formulas define functions on the stated domains. In the conventional SI physical reading, $T$ is measured in K, $a_R$ in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-4}$, $\varepsilon_T,p_T$ in J m$^{-3}$, and $s_T$ in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$. These units do not assign an empirical value to $a_R$. In particular, this definition does not derive a quantum blackbody coefficient or assert that any physical system realizes these maps.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Fix an integer $n\ge1$. With the complex smooth-function convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]] and multi-indices of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], define
$$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|,\qquad \mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)=\{f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C):p_{\alpha\beta}(f)<\infty\text{ for all }\alpha,\beta\}.$$
The zero multi-index gives $x^0=1$ and $\partial^0f=f$. These are actual smooth functions, not equivalence classes. The notation $C_c^\infty$ uses the support convention in [[def-c-c-and-c-c-infinity-on-rn]].

Pointwise differentiation is linear; thus $p_{\alpha\beta}(f+g)\le p_{\alpha\beta}(f)+p_{\alpha\beta}(g)$ and $p_{\alpha\beta}(cf)=|c|p_{\alpha\beta}(f)$. In particular this set is a complex vector space and each $p_{\alpha\beta}$ is a seminorm. The zero function belongs to it. Since $p_{00}(f)=0$ forces $f(x)=0$ for every $x$, the family separates functions. No choice principle is needed.

Assume countable choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$, and let $A_1,A_2,A_3,B,M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be constant matrices. Assume $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite, each $MA_j$ is symmetric, and $S:=(MB+B^{\mathsf T}M)/2$ is positive semidefinite. Consider

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_{x_j}U+BU=0.$$

Use [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]: for $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^3$, the scalar seminorm is $p_{\alpha\beta}(f):=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^3}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$, and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ consists of functions for which all these seminorms are finite. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ means maps $U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)$ with real-valued components such that each component, viewed as complex-valued with zero imaginary part, belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$; its vector seminorms are $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}(U):=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq m}p_{\alpha\beta}(U_\ell)$. For $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ there is a unique global smooth solution, Schwartz in $x$ at each time and continuous in every $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}$ on compact time intervals. With the negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, put $\widehat U(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}U(x)\,dx$ and define, for $s\ge0$,

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M}^2:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|\xi|^2)^s\widehat U(\xi)^*M\widehat U(\xi)\,d\xi.$$

For $t\ge0$, $\|U(t)\|_{H^s_M}\le\|U_0\|_{H^s_M}$ for every $s\ge0$; hence the solution depends continuously on the data in each such norm. Assume countable choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$, and let $A_1,A_2,A_3,B,M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be constant matrices. Assume $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite, each $MA_j$ is symmetric, and $S:=(MB+B^{\mathsf T}M)/2$ is positive semidefinite. Consider

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_{x_j}U+BU=0.$$

Use [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]: for $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^3$, the scalar seminorm is $p_{\alpha\beta}(f):=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^3}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$, and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ consists of functions for which all these seminorms are finite. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ means maps $U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)$ with real-valued components such that each component, viewed as complex-valued with zero imaginary part, belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$; its vector seminorms are $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}(U):=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq m}p_{\alpha\beta}(U_\ell)$. For $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ there is a unique global smooth solution, Schwartz in $x$ at each time and continuous in every $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}$ on compact time intervals. With the negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, put $\widehat U(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}U(x)\,dx$ and define, for $s\ge0$,

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M}^2:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|\xi|^2)^s\widehat U(\xi)^*M\widehat U(\xi)\,d\xi.$$

For $t\ge0$, $\|U(t)\|_{H^s_M}\le\|U_0\|_{H^s_M}$ for every $s\ge0$; hence the solution depends continuously on the data in each such norm. The same conclusions hold for smooth periodic data on the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, $L>0$, with Fourier coefficients $\widehat U_k=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}U(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x/L}\,dx$ and

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k/L|^2)^s\widehat U_k^*M\widehat U_k.$$

For periodic data, $\|U(t)\|_\infty\le C_{s,L,M}\|U_0\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}$ for each integer $s>3/2$.

For a unit vector $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, write $A(\nu)=\sum_j\nu_jA_j$ and $\widetilde A(\nu)=M^{1/2}A(\nu)M^{-1/2}$. The finite speed

$$v_*:=\sup_{|\nu|=1}\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde A(\nu))\}$$

is finite. If $v_*>0$, $R>v_*t$, and $U_0$ vanishes on $B_R(x_0)$, then $U(t)$ vanishes on $B_{R-v_*t}(x_0)$ for $0\le t<R/v_*$. The same assertion holds on $\mathbb T_L^3$ using its geodesic distance. If $v_*=0$, every $A_j=0$ and the system is a pointwise linear ODE, so spatial support does not move. These are conclusions for the displayed linear systems; no variable-coefficient or nonlinear existence claim is included.

statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Fix an integer $n\ge1$. With the complex smooth-function convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]] and multi-indices of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], define
$$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|,\qquad \mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)=\{f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C):p_{\alpha\beta}(f)<\infty\text{ for all }\alpha,\beta\}.$$
The zero multi-index gives $x^0=1$ and $\partial^0f=f$. These are actual smooth functions, not equivalence classes. The notation $C_c^\infty$ uses the support convention in [[def-c-c-and-c-c-infinity-on-rn]].

Pointwise differentiation is linear; thus $p_{\alpha\beta}(f+g)\le p_{\alpha\beta}(f)+p_{\alpha\beta}(g)$ and $p_{\alpha\beta}(cf)=|c|p_{\alpha\beta}(f)$. In particular this set is a complex vector space and each $p_{\alpha\beta}$ is a seminorm. The zero function belongs to it. For the three-dimensional product, the mass outside the cube of coordinate distances less than $\delta$ is bounded by the sum of the three one-dimensional tail masses, hence tends to zero. Let $C,\kappa,\tau,T_0,L>0$. Let $\Omega$ be either $\mathbb R^3$ or the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$. Consider real smooth fields $\theta:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $q:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying

$$C\theta_t+\operatorname{div}q=0,\qquad \tau q_t+q=-\kappa\nabla\theta.$$

The derivatives are ordinary derivatives of the Euclidean spatial coordinates; on the torus they are defined using periodic lifts. Write $U=(\theta,q)$ and let $e_j$ be the $j$th standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^3$. Define

$$A_j:=\begin{pmatrix}0&e_j^{\mathsf T}/C\\(\kappa/\tau)e_j&0_{3\times3}\end{pmatrix},\qquad B:=\operatorname{diag}(0,(1/\tau)I_3),\qquad M:=\operatorname{diag}(C,(\tau/\kappa)I_3).$$

Then the displayed system is $U_t+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_jU+BU=0$. The matrix $M$ is a positive symmetrizer, meaning $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite and $MA_j$ is symmetric for each $j$. For a unit direction $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, define the principal matrix $A(\nu):=\sum_{j=1}^3\nu_jA_j$; its eigenvalues are $0$ (multiplicity two) and $\pm v_h$, where $v_h:=\sqrt{\kappa/(C\tau)}>0$. For a fixed comparison speed $c_*>0$, $v_h\le c_*$ if and only if $\kappa\le C\tau c_*^2$.

For every such solution and every $s_0\in\mathbb R$, define the specified quadratic effective entropy density and flux by

$$s_{\rm eff}:=s_0+\frac{C\theta}{T_0}-\frac{C\theta^2}{2T_0^2}-\frac{\tau|q|^2}{2\kappa T_0^2},\qquad j_s:=\frac{q}{T_0}-\frac{\theta q}{T_0^2}.$$

Every smooth solution satisfies the exact identities

$$\partial_t s_{\rm eff}+\operatorname{div}j_s=\frac{|q|^2}{\kappa T_0^2}\ge0,\qquad \partial_t e_L+\operatorname{div}(\theta q)=-\frac{|q|^2}{\kappa},\qquad e_L:=\frac12\left(C\theta^2+\frac{\tau}{\kappa}|q|^2\right).$$

For every unit direction $\nu$, its quadratic flux satisfies $|\theta q\cdot\nu|\le v_h e_L$. The density $e_L$ is a positive quadratic Lyapunov density, not a physical energy density. The entropy identity asserts nonnegative production for this specified quadratic effective current; it does not assert positivity of $s_{\rm eff}$ for arbitrary data or a nonlinear material entropy law. These equations define the mathematical subsystem considered here; the sources give model context and do not establish a material-specific realization.

Use the exact global-solution, Fourier-coefficient, and weighted-norm conventions in [F1]. For initial data $U_0=(\theta_0,q_0)\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^4)$ or $C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^4)$, the unique global smooth evolution, its weighted Sobolev contraction, and finite propagation at speed $v_h$ follow conditionally from [F1] after checking the matrices below. On $\mathbb T_L^3$, for every integer $r>3/2$, set

$$K_{r,L,C}:=C^{-1/2}\left(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k/L|^2)^{-r}\right)^{1/2}<\infty,$$

where $C>0$ is the heat-capacity coefficient and $\|\cdot\|_{H^r_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}$ is the norm in [F1]. The periodic global solution supplied conditionally by [F1] obeys $T_0+\theta(t,x)>0$ for all $t\ge0$ whenever $K_{r,L,C}\|U_0\|_{H^r_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}<T_0$. The constant uses only the temperature component $C|\widehat\theta_k|^2$ of the supplied quadratic norm, so it does not compare heat-flux and temperature coordinates by a least eigenvalue. Although [F1] states a generic periodic supremum bound with unspecified constant $C_{s,L,M}$, the explicit $K_{r,L,C}$ bound here is derived directly from Fourier reconstruction and the stated norm contraction.

If the symbols receive their conventional SI thermal interpretation, take $\theta,T_0$ in K, $C$ in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$, $\kappa$ in W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, $\tau$ in s, $L$ in m, $q$ in W m$^{-2}$, and the comparison speed $c_*$ in m s$^{-1}$. Use the spatial coordinates in the inherited Fourier norms as their numerical values in metres, so the unit-frequency term in $1+|k/L|^2$ uses the reference length $1$ m. Then $s_0$ and $s_{\rm eff}$ have entropy-density units J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$, $j_s$ has entropy-flux units J m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, and $e_L$ has units J K m$^{-3}$ rather than energy-density units. The norm $\|U\|_{H^r_M}$ has units $\sqrt{\mathrm{J\,K\,m^{-3}}}$ and $K_{r,L,C}$ has units $\sqrt{\mathrm{m^3\,K/J}}$, so their product has temperature units. For a small comoving parcel with marker count $N_p$, proper volume $V$, and entropy $S$, this model assigns energy $E=N_p e(V/N_p,S/N_p)$. The physical interpretation of the marker as a particle count is part of this fixed-composition material model, not a consequence of the mathematical marker definition.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be nonempty and open, let $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$, and define
$$Y:=\{(n,s)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R:(1/n,s/n)\in X\},\qquad \varepsilon(n,s):=n\,e(1/n,s/n).$$
For $(n,s)\in Y$, put $v=1/n$, $\sigma_p=s/n$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, $H=e+pv$, $h=\varepsilon+p=nH$, and $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Then the following identities hold as equalities of differentials on $Y$:
$$d\varepsilon=T\,ds+\mu\,dn,\qquad \varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n,\qquad dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu.$$

For parcel totals $\mathsf S\in\mathbb R$ (entropy), $\mathsf V>0$ (proper volume), and $\mathsf N>0$ (marker count) with $(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X$, define
$$E(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):=\mathsf N\,e(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N).$$
Then $E$ is $C^2$, is positively homogeneous of degree one, and satisfies
$$dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N,\qquad E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N.$$
If $E$ is viewed on its open domain in $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, its Hessian annihilates the radial vector $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

derivations.claim: By the state definitions, $de=e_v\,dv+e_{\sigma_p}\,d\sigma_p=-p\,dv+T\,d\sigma_p$, while $v=1/n$ and $\sigma_p=s/n$ give $dv=-dn/n^2$ and $d\sigma_p=ds/n-s\,dn/n^2$. Therefore $d\varepsilon=d(ne)=e\,dn+n\,de=T\,ds+(e+pv-T\sigma_p)\,dn=T\,ds+\mu\,dn$. Also $\varepsilon+p=n(e+pv)=n(T\sigma_p+\mu)=Ts+\mu n$.

On the open set $\mathcal D=\{(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):\mathsf V>0,\mathsf N>0,(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X\}$, the parcel energy is a $C^2$ composition. Differentiating at fixed other parcel coordinates gives $\partial_{\mathsf S}E=e_{\sigma_p}=T$, $\partial_{\mathsf V}E=e_v=-p$, and $\partial_{\mathsf N}E=e-(\mathsf V/\mathsf N)e_v-(\mathsf S/\mathsf N)e_{\sigma_p}=e+pv-T\sigma_p=\mu$. Thus $dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N$.

Differentiate $\varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n$ and substitute the first identity in step 1.1. The terms $T\,ds$ and $\mu\,dn$ cancel, leaving $dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu$. This is a state-function identity on the open domain.

Using $\mu=e+pv-T\sigma_p$ and $\mathsf V=\mathsf N v$, $\mathsf S=\mathsf N\sigma_p$, we have $T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N=\mathsf N(T\sigma_p-pv+e+pv-T\sigma_p)=\mathsf N e=E$. This is a deduction within the adopted continuum material model, not an empirical statement.

current by

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^a u^b+p\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a.$$

For any smooth vector field $f^b$, the balance equation $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$

specific entropy is advected, $D\sigma_p=0$. These are conditional identities
for supplied smooth fields; they assert no solution existence or physical
applicability beyond the stated model data.

Use the state, signature, connection, and perfect-fluid data of

$f=0$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. Put $v=1/n$, $H=(\epsilon+p)/n=e+pv$, and let

For the momentum one-form $P=(H/c)u^\flat$, consider a smooth closed curve
$\gamma_0:[0,1]\to M$ with equal endpoint values and a local flow
$\Phi_\lambda$ of $u$ defined on a neighborhood of its compact image. Write
$\gamma_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda\circ\gamma_0$ and

$$\iota_u d(Hu^\flat)=T\,d\sigma_p,\qquad \frac{d\mathcal C}{d\lambda}=\frac1c\int_{\gamma_\lambda}T\,d\sigma_p.$$

region swept out by the loop. The local identity does not assert circulation
conservation merely from $D\sigma_p=0$, nor does it assume a global flow,
complete spacetime, or shock solution.

In the global Cartesian coordinates, $g_{ab}$ is constant. Let $
abla_{\partial_a}\partial_b=\Gamma^d{}_{ab}\partial_d$. The coordinate fields commute, so torsion freedom in [F1] gives $\Gamma^d{}_{ab}=\Gamma^d{}_{ba}$; metric compatibility gives $\partial_ag_{bc}=\Gamma^d{}_{ab}g_{dc}+\Gamma^d{}_{ac}g_{bd}$. Writing this compatibility identity with the permutations $(a,b,c)$, $(b,a,c)$, and $(c,a,b)$, then adding the first two and subtracting the third, the terms with $\Gamma^d{}_{ac}$ and $\Gamma^d{}_{bc}$ cancel by symmetry and leave $2g_{cd}\Gamma^d{}_{ab}=\partial_ag_{bc}+\partial_bg_{ac}-\partial_cg_{ab}=0$. Nondegeneracy of $g$ gives $\Gamma^d{}_{ab}=0$. Since $u$, the state, $n_0$, $\varepsilon_0$, and $p_0$ are constant, $J^a=n_0u^a$ and $\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon_0u^au^b+p_0(g^{ab}+u^au^b)$ have constant components. Their partial derivatives and every connection term vanish, so $
abla_aJ^a=0$ and $
abla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$. This verifies the adopted local balances on the prescribed background.

The vector $w=\gamma(1,\boldsymbol\beta)$ is future unit because $g(w,w)=\gamma^2(-1+|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)=-1$. Since $u\cdot w=-\gamma$ and $g^{ab}w_aw_b=-1$, contraction with the adopted stress gives $\mathsf T^{ab}w_aw_b=\varepsilon_0(u\cdot w)^2+p_0(g^{ab}+u^au^b)w_aw_b=\varepsilon_0\gamma^2+p_0(-1+\gamma^2)=(\varepsilon_0+p_0)\gamma^2-p_0$. When $\boldsymbol\beta=0$, $\gamma=1$ and this reduces to $\varepsilon_0$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(M,g,N)$, $u$, $\nabla$, and the fixed-composition state be as in
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]], with
$g(u,u)=-1$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. Define
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $\Delta_{ab}=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$\Delta_a{}^b=\delta_a{}^b+u_au^b$, and $D=u^a\nabla_a$,
$\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and the spatial symmetric
trace-free shear

$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)} -\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$

where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Suppose smooth fields
$\Pi$, $Q^a$, $V^a$, and $\pi^{ab}$ obey $u_aQ^a=u_aV^a=0$,
$u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $\pi^{ab}$ is symmetric with $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Set

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab} +u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a+V^a.$$

If $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$ and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$, the vector field

$$S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T}$$

satisfies the exact identity

$$\nabla_aS^a=-\frac{\Pi\theta+\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T} -\frac{Q^a(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)}{T^2} -V^a\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\mu}{T}\right)-\frac{u_bf^b}{T}.$$

This identity applies to the stated smooth fields and conventions; it does not
select a constitutive law or assert that any such fields solve an evolution
problem.

Use the time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, Levi-Civita connection, smooth future unit observer congruence, and length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Here a **frame** means this smooth observer field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$ and its pointwise rest spaces; it does not mean a coordinate chart or a tetrad. On a nonempty open region $O$, take a $C^2$ fixed-composition state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$ with $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, state function $e\in C^2(X)$, and $T=\partial_{\sigma_p}e>0$ as adopted by [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]]. The mathematical state maps are $n=v^{-1}$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\varepsilon=ne$, and $p=-\partial_v e$; their meanings and units are those in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]].

Write $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the rest-space projector, derivative along the observer congruence, expansion, acceleration, and spatial symmetric trace-free shear by
$$\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^a u^b,\qquad D=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad \theta=\nabla_a u^a,\qquad a_b=u^c\nabla_c u_b,$$
$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$
where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Put $Y_b=\nabla_bT+Ta_b$ and $Z_b=\nabla_b(\mu/T)$, using the chemical potential $\mu$ from [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. The number current, stress tensor and entropy current in the selected branch are
$$J^a=nu^a+V^a,\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab}+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T},$$
with $u_aV^a=u_aQ^a=u_a\pi^{ab}=0$ and $\pi^{ab}$ symmetric and trace-free. Adopt the source-free balances $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$ together with the first-order gradient closures
$$\Pi=-\zeta c\theta,\qquad \pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab},\qquad Q^a=-\frac{\kappa}{c}\Delta^{ab}Y_b,\qquad V^a=-L\Delta^{ab}Z_b.$$

Here $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; $\theta$, $a_b$ and $\sigma_{ab}$ have inverse-length components; $\Pi$, $\pi^{ab}$ and $Q^a$ have units Pa; $\zeta,\eta\in C^1(O)$ have units Pa s; $\kappa\in C^1(O)$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$; and $L\in C^1(O)$ has formal units $\mathrm{marker^2\,K\,J^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. The temperature and chemical-potential gradients have units K m$^{-1}$ and J marker$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ m$^{-1}$, respectively. The coefficient fields satisfy $\zeta,\eta,\kappa,L\geq0$.
