Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The roles of these quantities as primitive model inputs are framework-specific. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. Define the lapse $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and unit observer $u_\xi:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a supplied proper-temperature scalar $T>0$ in kelvins, define the Killing-normalized temperature field $T_\xi:=N_\xi T$. It is not assumed constant; if a separate equilibrium argument proves constancy on its stated domain, denote that value by $T_K$. The finite matter charge and its side-flux convention are those in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]] and [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; their charge-balance clause retains its explicitly conditional finite-slab hypotheses. This charge is not a general gravitational energy.

Keep covector types separate. A mechanical momentum covector $p_a$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$; its Killing energy is $E_\xi(p):=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ in joules. An energy-valued covector $\pi_a$ already has units joules and pairs as $E_\xi(\pi):=-\pi_a\xi^a$, without another factor of $c$. An inverse-length wave covector $k_a$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and pairs as $E_\xi(k):=-\hbar c\,k_a\xi^a$. For a specified charged stationary gauge, charge $q$ has coulombs and a potential covector $A_a$ in length coordinates has units $\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$; when a global stationary potential is actually defined, $\Phi_\xi:=-cA_a\xi^a$ has volts and $q\Phi_\xi$ has joules. A charged energy or chemical-potential convention requires its stated gauge and reference; no global potential, electrochemical equilibrium, or constancy is asserted here.

When $T_K>0$ is supplied, distinguish the inverse-temperature vector $\beta^a:=u_\xi^a/(k_BT)=\xi^a/(k_BT_K)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, from the scalar $\beta_K:=1/(k_BT_K)$, also in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a quantum statistical model, let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra: an associative complex algebra with nonzero identity $1$, a complete norm satisfying $\|AB\|\leq\|A\|\,\|B\|$, and a conjugate-linear involution $A\mapsto A^*$ satisfying $(A^*)^*=A$, $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$, and $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$. Its elements represent bounded observables. Let $\{\alpha_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ be bijective complex-linear maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserving multiplication and involution, with $\alpha_t(1)=1$, $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}$, and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$; require $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ to be norm-continuous for every $A\in\mathcal A$. A state is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\geq0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. For $b>0$ in the chosen flow-parameter units, define $S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq b\}$. The state $\omega$ satisfies the KMS condition at width $b$ when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ with $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$, continuous on $S_b$ and complex-differentiable at every point of its interior, such that

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

This all-observable boundary-value definition uses no separately declared analytic subalgebra. With the quantum statistical calibration $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$, a physical-time parameter $t$ in seconds has KMS width $b_t=\hbar\beta_K$ seconds. If the flow parameter is length $\lambda=ct$, use the reparameterized group $\widetilde\alpha_\lambda:=\alpha_{\lambda/c}$; its KMS width is $b_\lambda=c\hbar\beta_K$ metres. These are unit and parameter-convention assignments only. This definition introduces no Hilbert-space operator $H_K$ and does not identify the abstract automorphism flow or its strip width with the finite matter charge $H_\xi$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. This item asserts neither the existence of an observable algebra or flow for a given thermodynamic-gravity model nor the existence of a KMS state or equilibrium.

On a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H\subset M$,
write $i:\mathcal H\hookrightarrow M$ for the inclusion. A generator $\chi$
here is a smooth section of $i^*TM$ with $\chi_p\in T_p\mathcal H$
nonzero and null at each $p\in\mathcal H$. For a smooth tangent field $X$
on $\mathcal H$ and a smooth vector field $V$ along it, define
$\nabla_XV:=(i^*\nabla)_XV$ by [[def-pullback-connection]], applied to the
ambient tangent bundle and its metric-selected connection. The prescription
is independent of frames by
[[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. In particular,
$\nabla_\chi\chi$ is a vector field along $\mathcal H$ and needs no chosen
ambient extension. If $\chi$ is the restriction of a smooth ambient field
$\widetilde\chi$, the same theorem gives
$\nabla_\chi\chi=(\nabla_{\widetilde\chi}\widetilde\chi)|_{\mathcal H}$;
thus this convention also covers the supplied ambient Killing generators.
The generator may admit a scalar $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ defined by
$\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa_{\rm geom}\chi$. When the flow parameter has length units, $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; the corresponding acceleration-unit quantity $\kappa_{\rm acc}:=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. This definition does not assert a horizon exists, that $\kappa$ is constant, or that a temperature law follows. The formula $T_K=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}/(2\pi k_B)$ requires a specified quantum/semiclassical model, and an area-entropy formula requires a separate thermodynamic identification. In particular, equal units do not identify local material entropy, finite statistical entropy, and area entropy, and no generalized second law is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

abla_{(c}u_{d)}-(	heta/3)\Delta^{ab}\Delta_{ab}=	heta-(	heta/3)3=0$, since $u^cu^d
abla_cu_d=	frac12u^c
abla_c(g(u,u))=0$. Thus $\pi=-2\eta c\sigma$ is also symmetric, spatial, and trace-free. The state, observer, and regularity hypotheses of [F1] are supplied by [F2], [F4], and the given actual solution. Applying [F1] therefore gives

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Use the fixed-composition local-equilibrium state, smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, smooth future unit observer congruence $u$, and length coordinates $x^0=ct$ from [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] and [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. In particular, $n>0$, $T>0$, $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, and $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$ have those suppliers' meanings. In a selected bulk-only branch, adopt the stress, number current, and source-free balances
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$
where $\Pi$ is a smooth scalar bulk pressure. Let $\zeta,\tau\in C^1(O)$ be positive coefficient fields with SI units Pa s and s, respectively, and define $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, with units Pa$^{-1}$. Adopt the extended entropy current and derivative-corrected relaxation law
$$S^a=\left(s-\frac{\beta\Pi^2}{2T}\right)u^a,\qquad \beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right).$$
Here $\Pi$ has units Pa, $D$ and $\theta$ have inverse-length units, and each side of the relaxation law has units m$^{-1}$; $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has entropy-density units J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$.

For each application, specify a nonempty open near-equilibrium regime in the pointwise state and first-derivative data around $\Pi=0$, based at constant zero-gradient reference data, and use the current and law only while the fields remain in that declared regime. Require enough field regularity for the balances and entropy divergence to hold classically. The mathematical result [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] supplies the exact matching conditional entropy identity and one homogeneous witness; its actual statement and proof are conditional on the listed mathematical inputs and assume exactly countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). It motivates this selection and is used by the downstream deductions, but it does not derive the adopted physical postulate.

This is a restricted constitutive assumption for the selected material. It does not derive the equation of state, assert universal validity, or adopt existence of a general nonlinear solution. It makes no causal or stability claim; positive relaxation time alone supplies neither. No empirical observation is supplied.

Use the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian data, local state, and conventions of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]], with $n>0$, $T>0$, $c>0$, $x^0=ct$, and smooth future unit $u$. Assume positive $C^1$ coefficients $\zeta$ and $\tau$, set $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, and let $\Pi$ be a smooth scalar. In the bulk-only branch take

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_au^a$, and $a^b_{\rm acc}=Du^b$. Adopt the corrected relaxation law

$$\beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right)$$

and the extended entropy current $S^a=[s-\beta\Pi^2/(2T)]u^a$. Then the stress and particle equations imply

$$D\epsilon+(h+\Pi)\theta=0,\qquad (h+\Pi)a^b_{\rm acc}+\Delta^{ba}\nabla_a(p+\Pi)=0,\qquad Dn+n\theta=0,$$

and every actual smooth solution of the stated corrected law satisfies

$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\ge0.$$

Here $\beta$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, $\Pi,\epsilon,p,h$ have units Pa, $D,\theta,a_{\rm acc}$ have inverse-length components, and the correction $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has the units of entropy density. The law is an explicit model assumption; dropping its derivative term does not yield the stated sign identity in general.

There is an exact homogeneous solution on the explicitly specified Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$; its Levi-Civita derivative is ordinary coordinate differentiation. Fix a state point $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplied local state domain with $v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and take the constant state map $(v,\sigma_p)(x)=(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, so $n_0=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ are constant. For constant positive coefficients $\zeta_0,\tau_0$, let $u=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, $T=T_0$, and define the smooth scalar field $\Pi(x)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0}$ on all of $M$, where $t=x^0/c$. The stress and particle balances and the corrected law hold, with strict entropy production wherever $\Pi(x)\ne0$. This mathematical witness is not a general nonlinear existence theorem or a claim of physical applicability in any separately selected near-equilibrium regime.

Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, as defined in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. A chart is a smooth coordinate map; an observer congruence is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$; its integral curves, an adapted chart, and a tetrad field are distinct objects. The exact regularity and rest-space conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and the chart/congruence distinction of [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] apply. An orthogonal family of rest slices is not available for every congruence.

For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The roles of these quantities as primitive model inputs are framework-specific. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. Define the lapse $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and unit observer $u_\xi:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a supplied proper-temperature scalar $T>0$ in kelvins, define the Killing-normalized temperature field $T_\xi:=N_\xi T$. It is not assumed constant; if a separate equilibrium argument proves constancy on its stated domain, denote that value by $T_K$. The finite matter charge and its side-flux convention are those in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]] and [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; their charge-balance clause retains its explicitly conditional finite-slab hypotheses. This charge is not a general gravitational energy.

Keep covector types separate. A mechanical momentum covector $p_a$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$; its Killing energy is $E_\xi(p):=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ in joules. > $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

On a nonempty open region of the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian model of [[post-tgr-bulk-relaxation-model]], assume an actual solution of its source-free stress and particle balances and corrected relaxation law. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Fix $c>0$ and take $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future causal cone $\{V\in\mathbb R^4:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$. For $V^0>0$, membership in this cone is exactly the coordinate-speed condition $|d\mathbf x/dt|\leq c$; its boundary speed is the reference speed $c$. The constant rest observer is $\bar u=(1,0,0,0)$.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, let $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and fix $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv}>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$. A first variation is defined by a family of state maps $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda}):M\to X$ and fields $u_\lambda:M\to\mathbb R^4$, jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, with the displayed reference state and $\bar u$ as their constant $\lambda=0$ values and with $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$, $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, write $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$; put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and impose the adiabatic first-variation condition $\delta\sigma_p=0$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of the no-force balances $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$ and $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, with $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+p_\lambda\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$, and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear balances. Differentiating $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ gives $\delta u^0=0$.

The local Gibbs identity of [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] gives

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})}{n_0h_0},$$

and assume additionally $a_s\le1$. In the adopted units, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $r$ and $h_0$ have units Pa, and $w$ and $a_s$ are dimensionless. Since $x^0=ct$ and $\bar u=\partial_{x^0}$, the first variations of the no-force perfect-fluid projection equations of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] are

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0.$$

For initial data $U_0=(r_0,w_0)$ whose real components belong componentwise to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ as defined by [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or for smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, these equations have the unique global smooth solution supplied by [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]]. The positive quadratic energy density $\mathcal E=\tfrac12[(a_s/h_0)r^2+h_0|w|^2]$ has flux $c a_s r w$, and the solution is contractive in the corresponding weighted $L^2$ and Sobolev norms. Its characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$; for positive $a_s$, this propagation cone lies inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s\le1$. These are statements about this frozen linear system only; they do not assert a nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution theorem.

For the formal coefficient comparison in [A3], if the same linear equations are assigned $a_s>1$, their plane-wave speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}>c$. If they are assigned $a_s<0$, smooth periodic modes grow as $e^{c\sqrt{-a_s}|k|t}$ at arbitrarily large wave numbers. The case $a_s=0$ is degenerate: the displayed positive energy matrix is no longer positive definite, so the stability proof above does not apply.

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and let
$\nabla$ be its unique torsion-free $g$-compatible connection supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix a nonempty
connected open set $O\subseteq M$. A **selected stationary thermal carrier** on
$O$ consists of a smooth future timelike vector field $\xi$ and a smooth
positive scalar field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$, where $T$ is measured in kelvins,
such that $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-killing-field]]. Equivalently, the criterion is
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ by
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. The round brackets mean
symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The choice of $\xi$ specifies the thermal congruence; no
coordinate chart or universal observer field is selected.

Set $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. Then
$g(u,u)=-1$. In the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, $u$ is
dimensionless and $cu$ is the physical four-velocity, with $c>0$ in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the inverse-temperature vector
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the Killing-normalized
temperature field $T_K:=N_\xi T$. Thus $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$; this definition
does not assert that $T_K$ is constant.

For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, put
$\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$, a dimensionless scalar. Define the rest-space metric,
derivative, acceleration, expansion and shear by
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\qquad D:=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_au^a,\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac13\theta h_{ab}.$$
Here $a$, $\theta$ and $\sigma$ have inverse-length units; the physical
proper acceleration is $c^2a$. The smooth tangent-bundle structure used by
the cited GR suppliers assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]; no stronger choice principle is part of this
definition.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and let
$\nabla$ be its unique torsion-free $g$-compatible connection supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix a nonempty
connected open set $O\subseteq M$. A **selected stationary thermal carrier** on
$O$ consists of a smooth future timelike vector field $\xi$ and a smooth
positive scalar field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$, where $T$ is measured in kelvins,
such that $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-killing-field]]. Equivalently, the criterion is
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ by
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. The round brackets mean
symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The choice of $\xi$ specifies the thermal congruence; no
coordinate chart or universal observer field is selected.

Set $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. Then
$g(u,u)=-1$. In the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, $u$ is
dimensionless and $cu$ is the physical four-velocity, with $c>0$ in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the inverse-temperature vector
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the Killing-normalized
temperature field $T_K:=N_\xi T$. Thus $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$; this definition
does not assert that $T_K$ is constant.

For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, put
$\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$, a dimensionless scalar. Define the rest-space metric,
derivative, acceleration, expansion and shear by
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\qquad D:=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_au^a,\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac13\theta h_{ab}.$$
Here $a$, $\theta$ and $\sigma$ have inverse-length units; the physical
proper acceleration is $c^2a$. The smooth tangent-bundle structure used by
the cited GR suppliers assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]; no stronger choice principle is part of this
definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

derivations.claim:
Differentiating $u^bu_b=-1$ gives $u^b\nabla_au_b=0$. Decompose the
first derivative slot into its component parallel to $u$ and its rest-space
projection: $\nabla_au_b=-u_a a_b+h_a{}^c h_b{}^d\nabla_cu_d$.
Symmetrizing the rest-space term and using the definitions of expansion and
shear yields
$\nabla_{(a}u_{b)}=-u_{(a}a_{b)}+\sigma_{ab}+\theta h_{ab}/3$.
Differentiating $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ then gives
$$\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=(k_BT)^{-1}\left[-u_{(a}(a_{b)}+\nabla_{b)}\log T)+\sigma_{ab}+\tfrac13\theta h_{ab}\right].$$

Contracting this identity with $u^au^b$ shows that
$\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ implies $D\log T=0$, hence $DT=0$ because
$T>0$.

Projecting both indices with $h$ gives
$\sigma_{ab}+\tfrac13\theta h_{ab}=0$. Taking its $h$-trace gives
$\theta=0$, since $h$ has rank three and $\sigma$ is trace-free; substituting
back gives $\sigma_{ab}=0$.

Contracting one index with $u$ and projecting the other with $h$ gives
$h_a{}^b(a_b+\nabla_b\log T)=0$. Thus the displayed temperature-gradient
condition also follows from the Killing equation.

Conversely, the four stated conditions make the parallel, mixed and
rest-space projections in step 1.1 all zero. Since
$T_xM=\operatorname{span}\{u_x\}\oplus u_x^\perp$ at every $x\in O$, these
projections determine the full symmetric tensor
$\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}$; it is zero, so $\beta$ is Killing. In particular,
the acceleration/temperature-gradient relation alone omits the necessary
conditions $DT=0$, $\theta=0$ and $\sigma=0$.

boundaries.evidence: Statement: The tensor identities are pointwise on O and remain vacuous if O is empty; connectedness is used only where stated.

boundaries.reason: No zero-valued parameter branch is part of this claim; see the item statement for its strictly positive hypotheses.
The claim has no one-term, one-index, or one-dimensional branch.

template_review.reason: The rest-space trace in Proof 2.2 is three, as fixed by the Lorentzian four-manifold. No dimension-one shear formula is claimed, and one isolated scalar condition cannot replace the four stated conditions.

boundaries.evidence: Statement takes g(u,u)=-1 and T>0; Proof 1.1 can divide by kBT and 2.1 can pass from D log T to DT. A null observer or zero-temperature vector is excluded by these hypotheses.

boundaries.reason: The item makes no interval-endpoint or closed-boundary assertion.

template_review.reason: The kinematic equivalence concerns smooth pointwise fields on open O. No limit at T=0 or at a boundary of the observer domain is asserted; each contraction is evaluated at admitted points.

boundaries.evidence: Proof 1.1 and 2.1–2.3 use algebraic projections along the supplied u; 3.1 invokes the pointwise direct-sum decomposition. No observer or tetrad has to be chosen over an indexed set.
Steps 1.1–2.3 extract all four kinematic conditions from the Killing equation.
Step 3.1 combines the four projections to recover the full symmetric tensor equation.

Then there are local coordinates $(u^1,\dots,u^n)$ near $p$ in which

$$ X=\frac{\partial}{\partial u^1}. $$

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$

Here the pullback by the local diffeomorphism $\Phi_t$ acts by $d\Phi_{-t}$ on each contravariant slot and by $d\Phi_t$ on each covariant slot.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

derivations.claim:
By the equivalent covariant characterization of a Killing field in
[[def-gr-killing-field]], and metric compatibility and torsion-freeness,
$(\mathcal L_\xi g)(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\xi,Y)+g(X,\nabla_Y\xi)$: expand the Lie
derivative from its flow definition, use
$[\xi,X]=\nabla_\xi X-\nabla_X\xi$, and cancel the two $\nabla_\xi$
terms with metric compatibility. Thus $\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ implies
$\mathcal L_\xi g=0$. The local flow identity
$\Phi_{s+h}=\Phi_h\circ\Phi_s$ and the pullback order give
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Phi_s^*g=\Phi_s^*(\mathcal L_\xi g)=0.$$
In local tensor components [F5] makes each component constant in $s$;
since $\Phi_0$ is the identity, $\Phi_s^*g=g$. Hence $\Phi_s$ is a local
isometry.

Define the pulled-back connection by
$(\Phi_s^*
abla)_XY:=\Phi_{s*}^{-1}(
abla_{\Phi_{s*}X}\Phi_{s*}Y)$.
A diffeomorphism preserves Lie brackets, so its pullback connection has zero
torsion whenever $
abla$ does. Since $\Phi_s^*g=g$, metric compatibility of
$
abla$ also makes $\Phi_s^*
abla$ compatible with $g$. The uniqueness in
[F3] gives $\Phi_s^*
abla=
abla$. The flow composition law also gives
$\Phi_{s*}\xi=\xi$.

Substituting $\Phi_s^*\nabla=\nabla$ and $\Phi_{s*}\xi=\xi$ into the
curvature definition [F4] gives $\Phi_s^*R=R$. Pullback commutes with tensor
products and contractions by their slot definitions, and the preserved
connection makes it commute with each covariant derivative. Repeating these
identities proves preservation of every finite covariant derivative and
contraction stated above; composing preserved scalar components with a smooth
function preserves the resulting scalar invariant.

Let $\eta$ be a Lorentz form on a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$. There
is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ with
$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for all $a,b$. Such a basis
is called **$\eta$-orthonormal**; in every $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis
exactly one basis vector is timelike and the other three are spacelike, and the
count is the inertia $(3,1,0)$ of $\eta$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with causal terminology as in
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], and let

$$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$$

be its **timelike set**. Components and closures refer to the topology obtained
by using any ordered basis to identify $V$ with Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$;
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], step 5.1, proves that the
resulting open sets are independent of the basis. By that lemma the
set $T$ has exactly two connected components, and each of them is nonempty,
open, convex and path-connected. A **time orientation** of $(V,\eta)$ is a
choice of one of these two components. Fixing such a choice, write $C^+$ for the
chosen component and

$$C^-:=T\setminus C^+$$

for the other component; thus $T=C^+\sqcup C^-$ is a disjoint union and
$C^+$, $C^-$ are exactly the two components supplied by the lemma. Relative to
this choice a vector $v\in V$ is

- **future timelike** when $v\in C^+$;
- **past timelike** when $v\in C^-$;
- **future null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$;
- **past null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$;
- **future causal** when it is future timelike or future null;
- **past causal** when it is past timelike or past null.

The sets $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ are the
**future closed cone** and the **past closed cone** of the time-oriented space
$(V,\eta,C^+)$. By [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] each of them
is a convex cone, their intersection is $\{0\}$, and a vector is causal exactly
when it is future causal or past causal, in which case exactly one of these two
alternatives holds: no nonzero vector is both future causal and past causal.
The timelike vectors are exactly the points of $T=C^+\cup C^-$, and
$0\notin T$ because $\eta(0,0)=0$; since a null vector is nonzero with
$\eta(v,v)=0$, no vector is both timelike and null, so the classes above are
mutually exclusive where the definitions say they are: no vector is both future
and past causal, and no timelike vector is null.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis. Write
$v=v^0e_0+v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ for the coordinates of $v$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]) and

$$\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}.$$

Then $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert^2$, and the timelike set
$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$ satisfies

$$T=T_+\cup T_-,\qquad T_+:=\{v:v^0>\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad T_-:=\{v:v^0<-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\}.$$

The sets $T_+$ and $T_-$ are nonempty, disjoint, open in $V$ (for the metric
topology of the distance $d(u,w):=\lVert c(u)-c(w)\rVert_2$ induced by the
coordinates $c(v):=(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$), convex and path-connected, and they are
exactly the two connected components of $T$. In every $\eta$-orthonormal
ordered basis the two displayed coordinate sets coincide with the two
components of $T$ in some order, and they may be interchanged relative to a
previously fixed naming of the components. Moreover

$$\operatorname{cl}(T_+)=\{v:v^0\ge\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{v:v^0\le-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{0\}.$$

Let $V$ be a $4$-dimensional real vector space ([[def-vector-space]],
[[def-dimension]]). A **Lorentz form** on $V$ is a symmetric bilinear form
$\eta:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]])
such that

1. $\eta$ is nondegenerate: both radicals
   $\operatorname{rad}_L(\eta)=\{u:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }v\}$ and
   $\operatorname{rad}_R(\eta)=\{v:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }u\}$ are
   $\{0\}$ ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]);
   and
2. $\eta$ has **inertia** $(3,1,0)$: in some (equivalently, in every) basis of
   $V$ in which the matrix of $\eta$ is diagonal, exactly three diagonal
   entries are positive, exactly one is negative, and none is zero
   ([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]).

The inertia of a symmetric bilinear form is the triple $(p,q,r)$ of numbers of
positive, negative and zero diagonal entries of any diagonalizing basis, and it
is independent of the diagonalizing basis by Sylvester's law of inertia
([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]); hence clause 2
is a property of $\eta$ itself and not of a chosen basis. The **associated
quadratic form** of $\eta$ is

$$q(v):=\eta(v,v),\qquad v\in V .$$

A **Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$** is a pair $(V,\eta)$
consisting of a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$ and a Lorentz form $\eta$
on $V$; the name records that the diagonal normal form of $\eta$ has one
negative entry followed by three positive entries. No positive-definite
structure on $V$ is assumed or implied by this definition, and $q$ takes both
negative and positive values on nonzero vectors: a basis in which
$\eta$ is diagonal with diagonal entries $-1,1,1,1$ exists by clause 2, and on
its first vector $q$ is $-1$, while on each of the other three it is $+1$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

derivations.claim:
In the future massive shell write $P=(E,rn)$, where
$E=\sqrt{M^2+r^2}$, $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$. Apply the assumed identity to
the two shell vectors $(E,rn)$ and $(E,-rn)$ and subtract. Dividing the
result by $2r>0$ gives
$2E A_{0i}n_i+b_i n_i=0$ for every $E>M$ and every unit $n$. For fixed $n$,
the left side is affine in $E$ and vanishes on an interval, so
$A_{0i}n_i=b_i n_i=0$; varying $n$ yields $A_{0i}=b_i=0$.

On the future null cone write $P=\rho(1,n)$ with $\rho>0$ and
$n\in S^2$. The identity becomes
$\rho^2A((1,n),(1,n))+\rho b(1,n)=0$ for every $\rho>0$; comparing the two
polynomial coefficients gives $A((1,n),(1,n))=b(1,n)=0$. Replacing $n$ by
$-n$ in the covector equation gives $b_0=0$ and $b_i n_i=0$ for every $n$,
so $b=0$.

The remaining massive-shell identity is
$A_{00}(M^2+r^2)+r^2 n^TA_{\rm sp}n+b_0\sqrt{M^2+r^2}=0$, where
$A_{\rm sp}=(A_{ij})$. Varying $n$ shows $n^TA_{\rm sp}n$ is a constant
$a$ on $S^2$. Taking $n=e_i$ gives $A_{ii}=a$; taking
$n=(e_i+e_j)/\sqrt2$ gives $A_{ij}=0$ for $i\ne j$. With
$z=\sqrt{M^2+r^2}$ the remaining identity is
$(A_{00}+a)z^2+b_0z-aM^2=0$ for every $z>M$. A polynomial vanishing on
an interval has all coefficients zero; since $M>0$, this yields
$a=A_{00}=b_0=0$, hence $A=b=0$.

In the quadratic null-cone equation, comparing $n$ and $-n$ gives
$A_{0i}=0$. Its value on $e_i$ yields $A_{ii}=-A_{00}$, and its value on
$(e_i+e_j)/\sqrt2$ yields $A_{ij}=0$ for $i\ne j$. Thus
$A=\operatorname{diag}(A_{00},-A_{00},-A_{00},-A_{00})=\lambda g$ with
$\lambda=-A_{00}$. This proves the null clause and completes the lemma.

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $x\in M$, and let
$M_*>0$ be a rest-energy parameter in joules. The **future massive shell at
$x$** is the Borel subset
$$\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}:=\{P\in T_xM:g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}.$$
Use any smooth future orthonormal tetrad near $x$, whose existence is
[[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]]. At $x$ write its basis as
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and, for $q=(q_1,q_2,q_3)\in\mathbb R^3$ with energy
coordinates in joules, put
$$E(q):=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2},\qquad P_e(q):=E(q)e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3q_i e_i.$$
Let $\lambda_3$ be Euclidean Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]). For every Borel set
$A\subseteq\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, with its subspace Borel sigma-algebra
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), define
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))\,\frac{1}{E(q)}\,d\lambda_3(q).$$
In these tetrad coordinates the shell equation is
$-(P^0)^2+|q|^2=-M_*^2$, and the future sheet has $P^0>0$, hence
$P^0=E(q)$. Thus $P_e$ is a bijection onto the shell with continuous inverse
$q_i=g(P,e_i)$, so it is a homeomorphism. Continuous preimages of Borel sets are Borel
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]), and
$1/E(q)$ is a positive continuous density. The nonnegative Lebesgue integral
over a measurable set is [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]; the
positive-density measure theorem [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]] makes
$\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ a positive Borel measure. Its coordinate expression is
$d^3q/E(q)$ and its units are $\mathrm{J^2}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $E=(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ and $F=(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3)$ be two
future-directed tetrads at $p$ ([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]).
Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Then there is a unique real
$4\times4$ matrix $\Lambda=(\Lambda^B{}_A)$ such that
$F_A=\sum_B\Lambda^B{}_AE_B$ for all $A$, and:

1. $\sum_{C,D}\Lambda^C{}_A\,\eta_{CD}\,\Lambda^D{}_B=\eta_{AB}$ for all
   $A,B$; equivalently $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$.
2. $\Lambda$ is invertible and $\det\Lambda=\pm1$.
3. $\Lambda^0{}_0>0$.
4. For every covariant $2$-tensor $T$ at $p$, its components in the two
   tetrads satisfy
   $T(F_A,F_B)=\sum_{C,D}\Lambda^C{}_A\Lambda^D{}_BT(E_C,E_D)$.
   More generally, for a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ each contravariant slot
   contributes a factor $(\Lambda^{-1})^A{}_B$ and each covariant slot a
   factor $\Lambda^A{}_B$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with causal terminology as in
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], and let

$$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$$

be its **timelike set**. Components and closures refer to the topology obtained
by using any ordered basis to identify $V$ with Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$;
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], step 5.1, proves that the
resulting open sets are independent of the basis. By that lemma the
set $T$ has exactly two connected components, and each of them is nonempty,
open, convex and path-connected. A **time orientation** of $(V,\eta)$ is a
choice of one of these two components. Fixing such a choice, write $C^+$ for the
chosen component and

$$C^-:=T\setminus C^+$$

for the other component; thus $T=C^+\sqcup C^-$ is a disjoint union and
$C^+$, $C^-$ are exactly the two components supplied by the lemma. Relative to
this choice a vector $v\in V$ is

- **future timelike** when $v\in C^+$;
- **past timelike** when $v\in C^-$;
- **future null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$;
- **past null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$;
- **future causal** when it is future timelike or future null;
- **past causal** when it is past timelike or past null.

The sets $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ are the
**future closed cone** and the **past closed cone** of the time-oriented space
$(V,\eta,C^+)$. By [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] each of them
is a convex cone, their intersection is $\{0\}$, and a vector is causal exactly
when it is future causal or past causal, in which case exactly one of these two
alternatives holds: no nonzero vector is both future causal and past causal.
The timelike vectors are exactly the points of $T=C^+\cup C^-$, and
$0\notin T$ because $\eta(0,0)=0$; since a null vector is nonzero with
$\eta(v,v)=0$, no vector is both timelike and null, so the classes above are
mutually exclusive where the definitions say they are: no vector is both future
and past causal, and no timelike vector is null.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis. Write
$v=v^0e_0+v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ for the coordinates of $v$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]) and

$$\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}.$$

Then $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert^2$, and the timelike set
$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$ satisfies

$$T=T_+\cup T_-,\qquad T_+:=\{v:v^0>\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad T_-:=\{v:v^0<-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\}.$$

The sets $T_+$ and $T_-$ are nonempty, disjoint, open in $V$ (for the metric
topology of the distance $d(u,w):=\lVert c(u)-c(w)\rVert_2$ induced by the
coordinates $c(v):=(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$), convex and path-connected, and they are
exactly the two connected components of $T$. In every $\eta$-orthonormal
ordered basis the two displayed coordinate sets coincide with the two
components of $T$ in some order, and they may be interchanged relative to a
previously fixed naming of the components. Moreover

$$\operatorname{cl}(T_+)=\{v:v^0\ge\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{v:v^0\le-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{0\}.$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $m\ge1$, let U,V be open subsets of $\mathbb R^m$, and let $T:U\to V$ be a $C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Borel $h:V\to[0,\infty]$, $\int_V h(y)\,dy=\int_U h(T(x))|\det DT(x)|\,dx$, with equality in $[0,\infty]$ and $0\cdot\infty=0$. This statement concerns Borel h; no completed-measurable substitution is asserted.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
Write $P(q)=(E(q),q)$ in the first tetrad and let $q'=Q(q)$ be the
spatial coordinates of the same future-shell vector in the second tetrad.
The tetrad change $\Lambda$ maps the entire future shell bijectively to itself;
the spatial coordinate and its inverse are smooth, so $Q$ is a global $C^1$
diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^3$. Form the $4\times4$ matrix
$C(q)=[P(q),\partial_1P(q),\partial_2P(q),\partial_3P(q)]$. Block
elimination gives
$\det C(q)=E(q)-|q|^2/E(q)=M_*^2/E(q)$.

The chain rule on the shell gives
$\Lambda C(q)=C(q')\operatorname{diag}(1,DQ(q))$. Taking absolute
determinants and using [F2] and step 1.1 yields
$$\frac{M_*^2}{E(q)}=\frac{M_*^2}{E(q')}|\det DQ(q)|,\qquad |\det DQ(q)|=\frac{E(q')}{E(q)}.$$

For any Borel $A$ on the shell, apply [F3] to the nonnegative Borel
function $h(q')=\mathbf1_A(P_{e'}(q'))/E(q')$. Then
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e'}(A)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))}{E(q')}|\det DQ(q)|\,d^3q=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))}{E(q)}\,d^3q=\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A),$$
where the first equality uses the common geometric vector and the second uses
step 2.1. This is equality of positive Borel measures, completing the proof.
